title: Sara's review of Tacos Doña Lena
summary: Absolutely amazing tacos in this hole in the wall joint. Zesty food made by zesty and kind folk.
body: Absolutely amazing tacos in this hole in the wall joint. Zesty food made by zesty and kind folk. Some of their food took me back to the yucatan peninsula. The comida takes time to get to the table but all in all, it's worth it. So many to-go orders being taken place and many tables scattered round the spot. Needless to say, the staff are big on courtesy and cleanliness. Their are about 6 fresh in house made salsa's to enjoy with the meal. The refreshing juices (aguas frescas) are made in house as well; with actual chunks of fruit and pulp. The juice is sweet and cold, pairing well with the savory food. I truly recommend the grande avocado quesadilla and the crispy tostada. Heck, the tacos are great as well. Their are many items on the menu, flexible and accommodating for any palette. Plenty of vegetarian items to choose from and the beans, tortillas are vegetarian (no lard). Bonus points! As many folk don't consume pork these days. Looking forward to revisiting and trying the nopal (cactus) and sopa (soup). Glad to have a warm spot such as Doña Lena in the neighborhood.
author: Sara I.

title: Sara's review of Verbena Coffee
summary: Such a great little coffee shop in the neighborhood, and it hasn't even been opened for 2 years. They are thriving in the memorial area and it's wonderful to continue supporting local business.
body: Such a great little coffee shop in the neighborhood, and it hasn't even been opened for 2 years. They are thriving in the memorial area and it's wonderful to continue supporting local business. I love visiting independently owned coffee shops and trying various drinks they craft in house. My favorite here being the London fog latte. It is a special bevvie close to my heart and not everyone knows how to make it correctly. I dig the loose leaf earl grey tea blend which they steep in warmed foamy milk. They add a fragrant vanilla syrup to the bevvie (which is typically added to a London fog). They array of flavors and aroma made me happy. Bergamot flavour is sharp and on point. Sipping on this gray colored latte on a gray & rainy day brought forth a cosy appeal. Coffee drinks are nice as well; such as the brown sugar latte. The brown sugar syrup is also made in house. Surprisingly the drink is not that sweet which is great. Asking to add cinnamon to the drink really brings out the brown sugar flavour. Cappuccinos are solid as well. I look forward to revisiting and trying the sliced loaf cakes and croissants that are delivered from a local bakery. The interior is all woodsy with tan colored furniture. It reminds me of Scandinavia. Sometimes they have popups with various cafe businesses, such as Koffeteria. Always fun to see what goes on with the neighborhood cafe. Until next time.
author: Sara I.

title: Review: 24 Hour Fitness - Sugar Land — 2016-01-19
summary: Been coming here for many.. many years.. They disappoint in terms of unfriendly staff workers whom ignore you whenever you walk into the gym. Wheres the customer service? Its certainly lacking. A few of the staff members are friendly (mostly the males) and a few of the male trainers. They often run
body: Been coming here for many.. many years.. They disappoint in terms of unfriendly staff workers whom ignore you whenever you walk into the gym. Wheres the customer service? Its certainly lacking. A few of the staff members are friendly (mostly the males) and a few of the male trainers. They often run out of towels and the gym is very warm during the winter. Why? I feel as if they turn off the AC during the winter season which makes for an unpleasant and stuffy workout. It's uncomfortable. I never use the gym showers or lockers. Why bother? I carry my purse with me throughout my workout rather than using one of the lockers. I often leave sweaty, messy and comfortably shower at my home which is in the neighborhood. If you're here to simply just workout and use a few machines then you'll be able to handle this gym. It's what I do. I come here to quietly workout and leave. Don't even bother to converse with the strange crowd whom float around this gym. I hope 24 hour fitness can provide complimentary wifi eventually as well. They are overdue. My two cents here.

body:
59 DINER!
Whats the name behind it?
I told my sister its obviously due to the fact that diners were very popular in the fifties. Therefore, I suggested it was named after the year 1959.
Then... she told me that i`ve got it all wrong, and that it has to deal with the road highway 59! Hahah.
The debate still continues..
..Anyways.
My friends, sister, and I came here late at night, after enjoying ourselves at a concert. Right when we stepped in, I felt as if I had been transported to the 'happy days' years. We were seated promptly, and had courteous service. I was craving something cheesy, so I choose the grilled cheese sandwich. It was delicious, and had a mix of two cheeses, with sliced tomatoes inside. The bread was thick and spicy texas toast. I hadn't had a gourmet cheese sandwich in forever, so it was nice to eat this up! The french fries that came a long were thin and crispy -- highly addictive.
My friends ordered the famous malts.They happily chugged down their malts, with an aftermath of a brain freeze!
59 Diner has a large menu chock full of items you don't usually find at other spots. It`s a nice change from the usual Denny`s and Ihops that are found nestled all around the 'burbs. I`m looking for another chance to try this place out again. Until next time!

title: Review: A Sweet Factory — 2010-06-06
summary: Here`s a sweet spot to satisfy your sweet tooth! Whats more is that its not your usual desserts. A Sweet Factory offers a variety of Mediterranean style pastries. If you are looking for a change from the typical brownies or cake, then I suggest giving this place a try. I LOVE the Kanafeh! It`s basic
body:
Here`s a sweet spot to satisfy your sweet tooth! Whats more is that its not your usual desserts. A Sweet Factory offers a variety of Mediterranean style pastries. If you are looking for a change from the typical brownies or cake, then I suggest giving this place a try.
I LOVE the Kanafeh! It`s basically a sweet cheese pastry, loaded with a mix of mozzarella and akawi cheese. Ask for the dessert to be warmed, so then when you eat it bite for bite, the cheese just oozes in your mouth! Make sure to top it off with attar (sweet syrup). You can`t miss this dessert, its BRIGHT orange! Just calling your name to be eaten up.
I have also enjoyed the other selection of desserts this place has to offer. I usually ask for a mixed box, so then I can take it home and relish on all the different varieties. The mixed box also comes in handy when you simply cannot decide on what dessert to order.
Arabian sweets are fragrant, sweet, and satisfying. The desserts smell of fresh orange blossoms and rose. It`s a beautiful change of smell and taste than the usual vanilla and chocolate.
The place is located in a simple and worn out plaza. The inside decoration of the pastry shoppe is no all that great either. Ah well, it`s not so bad once you realize how much this place has to offer. They are always churning up batches of fresh treats.

title: Review: Acacia Food Mart — 2025-03-06
summary: I enjoyed my time at Acacia food market this week. This market is a little small, but you'll be sure to find most things here that are Turkish/European/International. I love their packaged chocolates, dried spices, lentils/rice,, fresh baklava and fresh baked bread. I grew up eating most of these it
body:
I enjoyed my time at Acacia food market this week. This market is a little small, but you'll be sure to find most things here that are Turkish/European/International. I love their packaged chocolates, dried spices, lentils/rice,, fresh baklava and fresh baked bread. I grew up eating most of these items, so I love both their fresh items from their bakery as well as their packaged items from their store shelves. Customer service is little to none, it might be language barrier related, but I'm not bothered by it. When I visit this market, I know what I want. As a person that enjoys international cooking, I enjoy walking through various aisles. They have a lovely little bakery in the back corner of their market as mentioned. You can smell the fresh bread that is baked on a daily basis. They have quite a few dessert options, but my favorite will always be their baklava. They also have a "home" section with glassware,, Turkish tea cups, storage containers, soaps, etc. I found some baby products here as well!
I enjoyed the bakery bread when I got home and paired it with my homemade Turkish red lentil soup. So nourishing! Cozy and comfort at its finest.
Although a relatively small shoppe, they have quite a few things here. Parking is plenty, and they have long store hours as well. Come check this spot out!

title: Review: Afandim Restaurant — 2017-03-07
summary: Tasty and authentic Uyghur cuisine in Houston! My friends and I all had lunch here about 3 weeks ago. We were all warmly welcomed and were so excited to try many different dishes. One of my friends is of Uyghur background, so she happily introduced us to a few of the dishes. It was a lovely afternoo
body: Tasty and authentic Uyghur cuisine in Houston! My friends and I all had lunch here about 3 weeks ago. We were all warmly welcomed and were so excited to try many different dishes. One of my friends is of Uyghur background, so she happily introduced us to a few of the dishes. It was a lovely afternoon and our appetites were ready for some hearty food! To our disappointment, many of the items we wanted to try had already ran out. It was around mid afternoon on Saturday, when we all got together - but so many of the dishes were out! We at least got to try the handmade noodles with beef, broccoli with garlic, and lamb kebabs. The handmade noodles with strips of beef were my favorite. The noodles were tender and chewy, as was the beef. The dish was colorful and consisted of many bell peppers and onions. The broccoli was nice and simple and the lamb kebabs were okay. The kebabs, in my opinion were hard and chewy. I just had difficulty in eating them and some of the pieces were laced with fat. So, totally not my favorite. The tea was watered down and didn't taste quite right. This somewhat new restaurant has kinks to work out. I'd love to try the rice and bread dishes next time. I'd say to visit this restaurant early, in case anything runs out, as it did in our experience. Other than that, i'm looking forward in visiting again. The food was fresh and the service was appreciated. Uyghur cuisine is tasty and unique - not too salty nor too spicy. I definitely recommend this restaurant if in the China town - Bellaire area.

body:
This place isnt to sit inside. Who would want to anyways? Its definitely a grab-and-go spot where you can dive yourself into creamy and exotic South Asian ice cream, shakes, and drinks! They also serve up savoury snacks which I have not tried.
My only problem is the consistency with their frozen sweet treats. Sometimes the flavours were off, and did not have enough ingredients. Other than that, I would recommend the original falooda, which is a like a milkshake made with rose-flavoured syrup, fruits, nuts, jello, and kulfi (ice cream).
Definitely a spot to check out on those long summer nights...

title: Review: Agora — 2015-01-26
summary: Been coming here for the past few years.. and I can definitely say Agora is on my list for greatest coffee-shops in Houston. I recently tried one of the holiday lattes. body: Been coming here for the past few years.. and I can definitely say Agora is on my list for greatest coffee-shops in Houston. I recently tried one of the holiday lattes. I would definitely suggest trying a holiday beverage while its still on the menu. I don't usually order seasonal beverages, as I find them mostly too sweet. But Agora's cannot be compared to the typical Starbucks. It is far better. I decided on the gingerbread latte and I was pleasantly delighted. The beverage was warm, aromatic, and lightly spiced. I love the Greek, American, and European desserts showcased here as well. One of my favorites being the melomakorana cookie, which is a crispy nutty cookie doused in honey and cinnamon. Perfectly paired with a steaming cup of coffee. Mmm good! The diversity of visitors has definitely grown as well. There is still plenty of seating everytime I come in. That is always a major plus when visiting Agora's. Overall a great place to relax and have a nice cup of coffee or tea.

title: Review: Aki Steak & Sushi — 2017-03-23
summary: I'm liking the happy hour specials on Sunday - which are all day! My sister and friends were just here last weekend and we all enjoyed our dinner. Prices are quite decent for all items on the menu and their is a variety of foods to choose from. I like going to those kind of establishments - the ones
body: I'm liking the happy hour specials on Sunday - which are all day! My sister and friends were just here last weekend and we all enjoyed our dinner. Prices are quite decent for all items on the menu and their is a variety of foods to choose from. I like going to those kind of establishments - the ones that have more than just sushi on their menu. I was craving sushi and noodles, so my sister and I split between our meals. She ordered the Singaporean noodles with chicken. Typically, Singaporean noodles are salty. But in our case, this meal wasn't salty. But it sure was lacking flavor. We had to add soy sauce on our noodles, which we usually don't prefer. The noodles could have had more of a curry flavor. They were okay. Sushi was nice and simple, a bit on the thinner side. But I guess that's okay' cause the sushi was totally a bargain. I received 12 pieces for only $8. Totally a steal and worth visiting on Sundays. My friends enjoyed their steak, seafood, and Chinese dishes. I'll totally be back and order something new, maybe some fried rice or noodle soup. I didn't feel sick after leaving this restaurant - which can occur after dining on sushi. Nothing too amazing, but fresh food and kind servers. Lots of families here as this restaurant is tucked in the 'burbs. Give it a try if in the area.

title: Review: Al Rabba World Food — 2020-06-20
summary: I'm not sure where these super low ratings are coming from.. I visited this market today and had a nice experience. Granted upon walking in.. you'll notice how spaced out things are. Some areas in the market seem barren and desolate while others are packed full of items on shelves. Makes for an adve
body: I'm not sure where these super low ratings are coming from.. I visited this market today and had a nice experience. Granted upon walking in.. you'll notice how spaced out things are. Some areas in the market seem barren and desolate while others are packed full of items on shelves. Makes for an adventure to sift out some items I suppose. They've got a large bakery here.. all the way on the right side of the market. I cant comment on it because I didn't visit that section. Theres a large selection of produce and all kinds of fresh herbs. I was able to pick out quite a variety of vegetables and fruit. All of them seemed fresh including the peppers and ginger. I often make fresh batches of ginger tea so it was crucial to find the right stuff. There's quite an extensive selection of halal meat located in the butchers corner. All the meat items are packed well and dated securely. Al Rabba is quite a large market and I believe this store was previously a neighborhood Randall's. You'll find many international and American items here as it still holds the remnant's of the previous chain grocery store. There's a section that is full of culinary equipment and some dainty teacups that caught my eye. I was able to pick up quite a few items on my trip. Although this market is located in Sugar Land it's nestled deep within a neighborhood not close to the main roads. If you're familiar with New Territory, you'll know how massive that subdivision is. Won't be frequenting that often but it's definitely nice to have a new grocery spot in town that is diverse and clean.

title: Review: ALDI — 2017-02-17
summary: I've been frequenting Aldi's for awhile & its great to have a location that is closer to Sugar Land! They are a small German super-chain market that have sprouted all around the US. I would often visit the Aldi's past Riverstone. It would take time getting there, driving all the way down on highway
body: I've been frequenting Aldi's for awhile & its great to have a location that is closer to Sugar Land! They are a small German super-chain market that have sprouted all around the US. I would often visit the Aldi's past Riverstone. It would take time getting there, driving all the way down on highway six. I was excited when I randomly passed by this location a month ago before they were even opened. We finally received a coupon in the mail mentioning that they were open for business. Yay! Sadly I didn't get to use the coupon as it expired the day before we went. But not to worry, because the prices at Aldi are stellar anyway. As a lover of European chocolate, I often visit and stock up on Choceur chocolate! There are so many flavors and they are all delicious. My favorites are the hazelnut milk chocolate and chocolate butter biscuits. Two of the flavors that I enjoy were missing.. but maybe things had ran out that evening. There were soo many people inside! I purchased milk, yogurt and even fruits and vegetables this time. Everything tastes great and fresh. I recommend the raspberries, blueberries and even some of their produce. They have plenty of organic options in the dried goods section. I often purchase Aldi's line of organic apple cider vinegar, cereal, and snacks. All of the organic purchases are worth it without breaking your bank. Bye WholeFoods! (Just kidding, I still visit you time to time). Hehe. We even purchased these little tulips the day we went - which was the day before Valentines day. Anyway, I like the feel of Aldis - its a small neighborhood market which makes going in and out easy. Im looking forward in visiting again and purchasing more chocolate ;) and other items. Until next time!

title: Review: All About Cakes — 2012-03-26
summary: All About Cakes is a nice and new spot in Sugar Land. This town just got sweeter! My sisters and I came in a few minutes before closing. We were greeted warmly by the staff who told us they were closing, but let us in on some cupcakes anyways. Chef Michelle came in afterwards and greeted us as well.
body:
All About Cakes is a nice and new spot in Sugar Land. This town just got sweeter!
My sisters and I came in a few minutes before closing. We were greeted warmly by the staff who told us they were closing, but let us in on some cupcakes anyways. Chef Michelle came in afterwards and greeted us as well. I love the charm of this place. There's not many seats inside, but that's okay, as most probably order or cater their desserts anyways.
My sisters and I tried an assortment of flavors, such as red velvet, key lime, mocha chocolate chip, and banana pudding. All were nice and moist, with the right amount of frosting to cake ratio. The cupcakes had a very home made feel as well. My favorite was the banana pudding, as I have never tried it anywhere else, and banana is one of my favorite flavours. I like the concept of having classic southern favourites, such as the ones mentioned, and a few others Ive never seen before, such as peanut brittle, and butter pecan. A unique concept like this will definitely keep me coming back.
As mentioned, everyone was friendly and treated us kindly. I call that true southern hospitality! I will be back soon to try out their other charming flavors.

title: Review: Alpha Dessert Juice Cafe — 2016-07-21
summary: The cafe has expanded and it looks completely different inside, at least last time I visited. Which is rarely never. Their are murals and photographs of the Pakistani culture and history. body: The cafe has expanded and it looks completely different inside, at least last time I visited. Which is rarely never. Their are murals and photographs of the Pakistani culture and history. I think that's great and should be represented in a cafe such as Agha Juice. You can't go wrong with their "kulfi" which is basically Pakistani ice-cream that is thick and creamy. The flavor is super sweet because of the condensed milk. But the texture and flavor is great. You can get it as a stick or as a chopped up plate of kulfi. They have snacks and foods as well, which I'm not too familiar with, honestly. A bit too heavy for my liking anyway. But maybe the burgers are good? I came here on a hot and sweltering day, longing for something with coffee. Should have know that I cant get decent coffee inside of a south Asian cafe. I ordered the cold coffee drink - which was essentially an ice cream shake consisting of coffee ice cream, milk and ice. Not of my liking and it was too heavy and light tasting. But if creamy milk shakes are your thing, then you might dig it. The guy at the front took forever to make my drink and I had to remind him of my order. The service was off and the employee's need better training. Other than that, I suppose its better to stick to their kulfi, falooda, and south Asian inspired drinks and desserts.

body: I got my hair colored a warm chocolate brown.. so far.. I'm loving it. The colors complement my jet brown hair.. and you can see layers of the colors flowing together. Amy is an artist when it comes to hair colors, balayage, and ombre. My twin sister visited this salon a few years ago, based on a friends recommendation. I remember liking the results of my sisters hair.. but never decided to color until now. Amy mostly works with natural colors... as a stylist.. she is not a fan of bleached hair or working with bleach products. I appreciate her honesty.. and I like how she creates a natural look for her clients. If anyone knows me well enough.. they know I'm all about natural products, whether it be food, hair, or skin products. I was at the salon for about 4 hrs.. it did not take too long for my color, wash, and style. Amy and her staff are quick on their feet and very attentive. Whenever I had any questions, Amy gave a warm reassurance and carefully explained the procedures with some common sense. After all, she has worked with the hair service for 20 years, so I trusted her with her knowledge and intuition. Thankfully, everything went well. I was given a snack and water bottle, and was made to feel comfortable. Her husband and daughter are often at the salon as well, they were friendly and answered any lingering questions. I mostly watched t.v. and chilled out during my session. Time flies and I liked my overall results. Thanks Amy and staff.

title: Review: Anatolia Int’l Foods — 2015-05-28
summary: I never received warm customer service when I first started shopping here. But after seeing me visiting a couple of times, the store owner finally warmed up to me and my family. I never took the aloof customer service too personally anyways. I know that people may have language and cultural barriers
body: I never received warm customer service when I first started shopping here. But after seeing me visiting a couple of times, the store owner finally warmed up to me and my family. I never took the aloof customer service too personally anyways. I know that people may have language and cultural barriers. Anyhow, I like this ethnic shop because it carries a lot of unique and international grocery. Its not too far from where I live and it definitely beats driving all the way to Phoenicia. I still visit Phoenicia every now and then, but this spot is closer and its smaller as well, so it makes grabbing items quick. They have fresh cut meats and they also have fruits and vegetables. They have a nice dairy selection.. consisting of yogurt, labne and various European cheeses. I also like their spice selection as well. If you're looking into jazzing up your flavour palate, than I definitely recommend buying the spices here. They also have a nice candy and jam selection. I love buying the Turkish version of nutella here. It's the Ulker brand. They also carry this nice hazelnut spread which is delectable on toast. You can easily find a random and unique gift for someone here. All in all, Makkah Mart has something for everyone. It's a nice and clean shop that's tucked away in a quiet neighborhood.

title: Review: Anonymous Café — 2017-01-08
summary: I've been coming to Anonymous Café since the summer and I must say.. they do not disappoint! I enjoy visiting this cozy Greek style coffee house. It's a bit small inside but that definitely adds to the overall charm of the place. Its appealing and quaint inside with just a few tables and chairs. The
body: I've been coming to Anonymous Café since the summer and I must say.. they do not disappoint! I enjoy visiting this cozy Greek style coffee house. It's a bit small inside but that definitely adds to the overall charm of the place. Its appealing and quaint inside with just a few tables and chairs. There is even a sofa chair to cozy yourself up on. I have tried both Greek iced coffees and they are quite strong. I do not suggest these drinks if you are not into strong coffee. They are bitter and dark. I always ask for extra milk. Sometimes there's more ice than substance. So definitely make sure you get more coffee and less ice! Otherwise, its kind of a ripoff. Anyway, at least that's how I see it. There are lattes as well, which are quite nice. I absolutely enjoy the Greek desserts here. They are virtually difficult to find in Sugar Land and I suggest the honey & nut cookies, as well as the eckmeck. The eckmeck is a layered dessert consisting of shredded phillo, custard and cream. Topped with some toasted almonds and powdered sugar. It is heavenly! I enjoy the fragrant and syrupy desserts and they pair quite well with any coffee. I have not tried the pound cakes.. yet. But they look plump and tasty. They offer savory meals but I have not tried anything off the savory menu yet. The food served here looks fresh and homemade, so I definitely want to try it next time around. Besides, Greek food is know to be healthy! You just cant say no to a Mediterranean diet. :) Anyway, the folks running this place are quite friendly. They make you feel welcomed and at home. I highly suggest supporting this local business and I believe they deliver some of the best coffee in SL. Until next time!

title: Review: Asia Market Thai Lao Food — 2015-12-13
summary: Yum! Such delicious and authentic Thai food in Houston. I have tried many Thai restaurants in the city, but Asia Market truly stands out. First of all, its a hole in the wall type of market/restaurant. It is very small looking from the outside. The parking is a bit tight as well. I happened to drop
body: Yum! Such delicious and authentic Thai food in Houston. I have tried many Thai restaurants in the city, but Asia Market truly stands out. First of all, its a hole in the wall type of market/restaurant. It is very small looking from the outside. The parking is a bit tight as well. I happened to drop by for dinner on a whim, simply because I was hanging out in the Heights earlier in the afternoon. Otherwise, this place is too far from where I live. Bummer! Well back to the food.. My sister and I ordered Thai tea, vegetarian pad kee mao (noodle dish), vegetarian curry puff (appetizer) and green curry with rice. All of the dishes were tasty and brimming with flavour.. very home-made cooking style. The pad kee mao had large chunks of vegetables.. such as cabbage, carrot and water spinach. It was loaded with vegetables and spices. The flat wide rice noodles were soft and cooked nicely. My only complaint is that the food was spicier than I would have liked. Next time around, I would be cautious of the spice level and have them tone down the heat. I would also ask for a little less oil on the noodles as my stomach tends to dislike greasy food. The vegetarian curry puff was fantastic. This is an item that is hard to find in Houston. Think of an empanada brimming with thick stewed curry! I am sure that the potato and chicken curry puff is nice as well. The green curry had a home-made taste and I could tell that the spices were all pounded and made fresh in the curry, no spice pastes or anything. The Thai tea was refreshing, fragrant and out of this world. The sweetened iced beverage was exactly what my taste-buds needed when chowing down on hot food.The menu also contains Laotian food which I might try next time around. Their are a few interesting items that I have never tried before. The fact that a market is connected with the restaurant is also what I enjoyed. After having dinner, I wandered around and grabbed a few food ingredients from the many shelves. Their is even a fridge containing fresh herbs and hard to find ingredients. I was a happy camper as I love cooking Asian cuisine and identified ingredients such as galangal, kaffir lime leaves and pandan in the fridge aisle of the market. In summary, Asia Market is a great place to checkout if in the Heights. The food truly takes you away to another part of the world. Support local business and try it for yourself!

summary: Oh wow, I've been coming here since they opened, but totally just had the time to write a review... body:
Oh wow, I've been coming here since they opened, but totally just had the time to write a review...
Baklava Cafe has a nice selection of items to choose from: sandwiches, pastas, salads, soups, and more! My favorite item from Baklava Cafe has to be their chicken shawarma. The meat is always so juicy and tender, and the toppings inside the wrap are nice as well. I certainly don't mind that it may take a bit longer for the food to be made, but my only concern is that sometimes they are too slow with their service. I do hope they improve their service soon, as its almost been a year since this establishment has been opened. I also dislike that it gets quite hot inside the cafe. Because of that, It makes me only want to sit inside during the cooler months.
The desserts on the other hand are always wonderful. They have been in the dessert industry for many years and they truly know how to concoct up some sweet cakes, cookies, and pastries! The baklava here is always fresh, and the knafeh is nice as well. I also like how the cakes are lightly sweet with moist layers. Its an array of desserts that you can bring home, anytime, or whenever you have guests over.

summary: Nice little place to visit when in the Fountains Plaza in Stafford. Their are a few other Bambu locations cluttered in Houston, but this one is quite clean and quieter as well. My favorite drink here is the coconut cream tea with boba. Its unlike any other regular "coconut milk tea". Coconut cream m
body: Nice little place to visit when in the Fountains Plaza in Stafford. Their are a few other Bambu locations cluttered in Houston, but this one is quite clean and quieter as well. My favorite drink here is the coconut cream tea with boba. Its unlike any other regular "coconut milk tea". Coconut cream mixed in with actual coconut pieces in the drink really elevates the flavor. The viscosity of the drink is thick and the fragrant notes of actual coconut are present as well. I came here a few times during the warmer months and will definitely stop soon to get a cold and refreshing drink. Their are many beverages to choose from. Bambu also serves up some authentic Vietnamese style beverages with jelly, fruit, etc. Lots of interesting flavors consisting of basil seeds, lychee, avocado, etc. They have smoothies, coffee, tea, and just about anything to please your taste-buds. Their is something for everyone here. The prices are reasonable as well and its situated in a clean and vibrant shopping center. Try the coconut cream tea as I mentioned.. you wont be disappointed!

title: Review: Bayou City Seafood and Pasta — 2018-01-20
summary: I had the chance to try out Bayou City Seafood & Pasta earlier this week. Came here to have dinner with friends on a chilly Monday night. The outside of the restaurant looks quite shabby like a barbeque restaurant. The interior is casual, relaxed and dimly lit. I found my friends sitting towards the
body: I had the chance to try out Bayou City Seafood & Pasta earlier this week. Came here to have dinner with friends on a chilly Monday night. The outside of the restaurant looks quite shabby like a barbeque restaurant. The interior is casual, relaxed and dimly lit. I found my friends sitting towards the back of the restaurant.. gathered around a large table. It was easy to spot them.. the place is not too big. My friends and I were greeted warmly by the host and servers. The menu is quite simple.. mostly consisting of seafood items, such as crawfish, shrimp, and crab. The menu also boasts large platters of pasta, sandwiches/burgers and a few poultry items. I wasn't too hungry so I decided on the crab bisque. It was freezing that night so a big bowl of soup seemed ideal. Most of our group ordered crawfish, pasta, and a few appetizers. I enjoyed the spinach and artichoke dip which came with crisp tortilla chips, as well as the fried pickles. Everything came out bubbly, hot and fresh. I thought the crab bisque was okay. It was creamy yet had a strong taste for my liking and was salty. The complimentary garlic bread was salty as well. Most seafood restaurants in my experience add a bit too much salt in their food. Not the biggest fan of that. My friends seemed to enjoy their meal. Dessert cleaned the savory palette, as we all dug into our own bowls of rich chocolaty bread pudding. The bread pudding was perfect. Sweet, creamy and warm. I really enjoyed the chocolate flavor as well as the hints of cinnamon in the dessert. If I decide to visit again, I might try their crab cake sandwich or one of the pasta items. Prices are steep as they serve generous portions of fresh seafood. Again, as mentioned, great service and warm staff. Give this place a try and sea (see) for yourself.

title: Review: Beans Cafe CoffeeHouse — 2015-12-06

body: This little coffee shop is located in a lively plaza. I came here on a cold and dark Friday evening. My curiosity brought me here after ending a shift at work. The ambiance, environment and music playing were all appealing. I particularly liked how the furniture and tables were a mixture of different designs. There were a good amount of people relaxing, studying and chatting inside. I ordered a hazelnut latte paired with a pistachio muffin. Both items were good. I had never had a pistachio muffin before, so that was a first. The brightly colored muffin paired nicely with the latte. I didn't stay for too long though. Wouldn't mind dropping by again but it's quite far from where I live. Overall I enjoyed the smooth taste of the latte. It's good to have a nice selection of unique coffee houses in Houston and Beans is definitely one of them.

title: Review: Bella Coffee & Gelato — 2012-09-12
summary: I tried out this new gelato cafe a few days ago and enjoyed my stay. There isn't much seating, but the interior environment is comfortable. I came in here after I ate at Bombay Pizza Company, which is next door to the gelato cafe. Both places are owned by the same folks, so the good news is that you
body:
I tried out this new gelato cafe a few days ago and enjoyed my stay. There isn't much seating, but the interior environment is comfortable. I came in here after I ate at Bombay Pizza Company, which is next door to the gelato cafe. Both places are owned by the same folks, so the good news is that you get 10 percent off any item at the gelato cafe after dining at their pizza restaurant.
As much as I love pannacotta and a few other classic Italian gelato flavours, I was in the mood of trying an exquisite flavor. I love anything with spices, so I opted for the cardamom salted caramel gelato. Although different from one another, the flavours blended well together. I enjoyed the aroma and taste of the cardamom in my gelato. It is one of my favourite spices and it hits home. Overall, the gelato was good, but I do feel it could have had a smoother texture.
I love the fact that Bella Coffee and Gelato have fusion flavors for their selection of gelato. I hope that they can continue serving up some unique concoctions. I would love to see more South - Asian inspired gelato flavours. I haven't tried any of the beverages yet, but I am looking forward to sipping a warm drink when the weather starts cooling off.
I also forgot to mention the wonderful customer service I experienced when I came into this cafe. Just the service and hospitality in itself kept me there longer. It is these little things that matter, and I believe the folks at Bella Coffee and Gelato have polished their skills in making it happen.

title: Review: bellagreen — 2013-01-06
summary: I had been wanting to try out Ruggles Green for awhile, since I heard rave reviews about their original spot in Houston. Its exciting that a location has opened up in the city of Sugar Land. We're pretty much complete with a variety of restaurants! I came in here a few days before Christmas with a g
body:
I had been wanting to try out Ruggles Green for awhile, since I heard rave reviews about their original spot in Houston. Its exciting that a location has opened up in the city of Sugar Land. We're pretty much complete with a variety of restaurants!
I came in here a few days before Christmas with a good friend of mine. Upon entering, I noticed how elegantly displayed the restaurant was. I love the organic appeal of the restaurant. There is a tree placed within a corner and several paintings of nature and works of art all around. The layout of the restaurant is open and airy, with several seats being inside the restaurant, as well as outside the patio.
I wasn't that hungry, considering all the food I had eaten during the holidays, so I opted for the vegetarian minestrone soup, as well the side of quinoa tabbouleh salad. My friend and I sat in the outdoor patio, it was a nice and quaint experience. Both of my meals were nourishing and flavourful. I do feel that the portion of the quinoa salad was a bit small. Other than that, I liked the flavour of the salad. It had a crisp and lemony taste. The minestrone was light and tasty which consisted of fresh vegetables. My friend ordered the veggie nut burger, and he enjoyed his meal. The burger was quite huge and looked filling. I will definitely try that next time around. Several other dishes on the menu sound amazing, and I know that will keep me coming back for more.
Overall, I had a nice experience at Ruggles Green. As mentioned, im looking forward to future visits and trying out their other items. I cant say much about the dessert since I didnt try any, but im sure they are fresh and delicious as well. This is definitely a great place to bring friends and family. The menu consists of meat dishes, as well as many vegetarian dishes. Its nice to have a restaurant in town center that offers seasonal and locally sustained foods. That is always a plus.

title: Review: Bering’s — 2025-08-30
summary: I stumbled upon a potato cookbook at Berings which will be perfect for bébé and I. Gotta love a good and hearty potato recipe, especially with cozy autumn around the corner. body:
I stumbled upon a potato cookbook at Berings which will be perfect for bébé and I. Gotta love a good and hearty potato recipe, especially with cozy autumn around the corner.
The colorful wall of cookbooks is such a delight. To be fair, I visited today in hopes of finding a spicy salsas & moles cookbook, which I found on their website. But it was nowhere to be found within the brick and mortar shoppe. Alas, we settled for the savory potato book.
The autumnal kitchen aprons piqued my attention and I may revisit pretty soon. Everything is becoming gold and orange within the shoppe.
The large green parrot at the shoppe is quite amusing and adorable. We love interacting with him.
It's always fun to visit Bering's, they have something for everyone. They often have deals as well, talk about sweet! Oh and don't forget the coffee and chocolates. They have handmade chocolates, biscotti and local coffee. The culinary equipment here is quite nice, whether you're looking for a new teapot, knife set or mugs, bowls. They often have food sample displays during the weekend as well, in particular, Saturday morning. Come check it out!

body:
Berri Blends is a tidy yet simple yogurt shop.
There are four different yogurt flavours to choose from. A great factor about this place is that you get to customize your own treat, as well as pick whichever toppings that you fancy.
I`m really into tart flavours, so I chose both the homemade tart & four berri flavours. For my toppings I chose :: shredded mango, strawberries, blueberries, and blackberries.
I enjoyed my creation, as well as my toppings. Although, I believe they could add a bit more variety for their fresh fruit toppings. This is a yogurt bar isn't it? I wasn't pleased to see so many candy/chocolate options. I never put those on my yogurt. I wasn't really interested in shredded mango either. I like my mango with bite & chunks.
All in all, Berriblends is just about good. It`s a simple spot to come check out in the neighbourhood. The interior is nice and comfortable. A good place to hangout with friends.

summary: I'm usually never in the Meyerland area... but by chance I had made a visit to the shopping plaza. Their are many stores and outlets to wander around and about. body: I'm usually never in the Meyerland area... but by chance I had made a visit to the shopping plaza. Their are many stores and outlets to wander around and about. I was thrilled when I noticed a Berripop in the vicinity. My two favorite locations (Sugar Land & Rice Village) no longer exist. It was a big deal for me when the stores closed.. simply because I always enjoyed and craved their fresh and tart yogurt. I'm more into tart yogurt rather than sickly sweet yogurt (ie: Menchies & Swirll).This existing location is much smaller with tight seating booths and little to no leg room. I made an order for the pomegranate yogurt with fruit on top. What I almost always liked about Berripop was the endless and fresh amount of fruits to choose from. I'm not the type of person who likes to stack candy on my yogurt. Unfortunately the "fresh fruit" was unappealing and looked rather dried out. Who knows how many hours or even days it had been sitting out. The worker behind the yogurt bar happened to have another container of fresh strawberries which he took out for me. Had I not mentioned anything.. he would have given me the old batch of rotten looking strawberries. Eh. Nonetheless, I still enjoyed my crisp yogurt on a rather cold day. I just don't know if this particular location is worth the visit a second time around. If only they can work on bringing fresh items to the bar. Oh Berripop.. you were my one stop shop for yogurt. But too bad most of your locations have shut down.

title: Review: Berripop Frozen Yogurt — Sugar Land — 2010-07-26
summary: Love, love, & love the yogurt at Berripop! Tart, and fruity flavours, just the way I like it! Berripop has a unique variety of flavours, such as watermelon and black cherry. body:
Love, love, & love the yogurt at Berripop!
Tart, and fruity flavours, just the way I like it!
Berripop has a unique variety of flavours, such as watermelon and black cherry. Both, which are equally good. I have sampled all of their flavours and have realized that they are all so great. The workers are friendly, sweet, & patient. They let you sample up to however many you want to try.
I also like the fact that I do not have to self serve myself. You see, I end up getting into a sticky situation when I try to pump out the yogurt myself. Here in Berripop, the yogurt is taken out for you, and displayed nicely.
The interior of the yogurt shop is cute and colorful. A variety of seating arrangement's are nicely displayed. I have enjoyed myself here with my sister and a friend.
The yogurt is creamy, tangy, and delightful. A nice smooth consistency followed by a punch of fruity flavour.
Whats not to like about Berripop?

title: Review: Bevers Kitchen & Gifts — 2023-03-30
summary: What a wonderful and cozy homestyle kitchen in the countryside. I loved it here and loved everything about Bevers Kitchen & Gifts. body: What a wonderful and cozy homestyle kitchen in the countryside. I loved it here and loved everything about Bevers Kitchen & Gifts. Arrived here close to one hour before closing and had enough time to snack on some pie and a bit of savory food. Had decent leftovers because I just wanted a light bite to eat that mid-afternoon. I loved their beef chili! I typically can't stand chili without beans, I don't want to eat beef bolognese! But theirs? Even without the beans the chili was darn good. Lots of savory and deep earthy spices. I decided to pair my chili with a side of wild rice. The wild rice was great! Earthy as well, with a tone of ground thyme and diced celery as well as carrot. Paired well with the spicy beef chili. Yum. I liked their beef brisket sandwich as well, which I got to try a bite from my partner. The service was friendly and chill, so was the environment. It's also nestled within a cozy street full of little shops that are unique to the area. Having a sweet tooth, I was impressed with the pies at Bevers kitchen. Hadn't had buttermilk pie in eons. Coconut cream pie with meringue.. good stuff. I was afraid the meringue would be sickly sweet. Nope. The meringue was piled high and cut well with the creaminess of the coconut cream. The pie crust? Absolute crisp. They shine with their sweets and I'll definitely revisit to try another pie when in the area. This spot is recommended by Sara the pastry gal. Go!

title: Review: Bijan Persian Grill — Sharpstown — 2010-05-19
summary: Kebabs and Rice! As simple and yet so flavourful as it can get. That is all I need when I come to Bijan Persian Grill. The location is right on Hilcroft, towards the entrance. You can`t miss it. The balcony juts out, and the place is quite big. Once you enter, immediately the staff seats you promptl
body:
Kebabs and Rice!
As simple and yet so flavourful as it can get.
That is all I need when I come to Bijan Persian Grill.
The location is right on Hilcroft, towards the entrance. You can`t miss it. The balcony juts out, and the place is quite big.
Once you enter, immediately the staff seats you promptly. This has to be some of the best service I have received at a Persian restaurant. The waiters are calm and assuring, as well as helpful when deciding on the menu.
I have enjoyed the Koobideh as well as the Chicken Kebabs. The stews are delicious and slow cooked as well. The meat is perfectly cooked and juicy. One thing I love about Persian (Irani) food is that it does not need an overwhelming amount of spices and flavourings. It is just simple and so darn good.
The food is served with a platter of fresh herbs and feta cheese. The bread is rustic, crispy, and always warm. Tear a piece of bread, and wrap it around some herbs and cheese. Its like having pizza without the sauce.
On the table is this "mystery spice" everyone is unsure of. I will tell you right now what it is! The spice is actually a dried berry called Sumac. Dash it on top of your rice for a tart and pleasant surprise.
The saffron ice cream is exotic and rich. Its a change from regular flavoured ice cream. Do try it!
End the night with some sweet and relaxing Persian tea. It is aromatic, cardamom flavoured Earl Grey. Ah, splendid..

title: Review: Black Bear Diner — 2024-01-16
summary: BBD... aka Black Bear Diner.. such a cozy spot that reminds me of GoldiLocks and the three bears... except this bear theme is originating from Nor'Cal. Hence the theme of all the northern trees and Nor'Cal Diner Vibes.. and yes.. some of my favorite diners are in California (my HomeState). On with t
body:
BBD... aka Black Bear Diner.. such a cozy spot that reminds me of GoldiLocks and the three bears... except this bear theme is originating from Nor'Cal. Hence the theme of all the northern trees and Nor'Cal Diner Vibes.. and yes.. some of my favorite diners are in California (my HomeState).
On with the food. This spot has been tucked away within the land of Sugar since 2019.. I've been visiting since then and have always enjoyed the grub at BBD. Albeit, their are some days when the foods perfectly on par, and then on some days when its just okay. Within my most recent visit... lines were out the door, frigid air was kickin' in and groups of folks were simmering within the cozy diner. Thankfully a group of us were seated promptly and found good seats closer to the entrance. Due to the fact they were busy.. it seemed the food was just okay this time. I ordered a beef patty melt with fries and coleslaw. Fries were blonde in color, cold, and such few. Patty melt was okay. Pancakes were warm and tender as they typically are. With such a huge crowd on the weekends, food can be subpar at times. Other than that, I have always appreciated BBD's expansive menu. Their hot chocolate is sweet, warm and creamy, and their desserts are quite nice as well. Savory hot items such as their omelets and other sandwiches are typically good.
Dining experience and service? Great. BBD has a nostalgic, woodsy, Nor'Cal feel that will make any nature enthusiast appreciative of their whimsical theme of all things bears and forests. They even sell a few bear plushies, socks, and all cuddlesy stuff at the front (where you pay). Service has always been warm and appreciative. Servers almost always check up on you. Though, they ought to put table numbers or order numbers on the table. At least twice during the weekend rush they brought out wrong food orders to our table.
All in all, this is a spot that many cherish. Perf for families, friends and groups of folk that wanna chat over coffee, pancakes and all the sweeter things in life. Until next time!

body:
I too, am picky with my tapioca. The pearls should have an 'al dente' texture, which literally means bite to eat. They should not be too soft or too hard, just right in between, where there is a chew.
Anyways, I have tried two drinks at Blenders on separate occasions. I have tried the Cafe Su Dau, which is Vietnamese iced coffee. The drink was fantastic! The coffee was made just right, sweet and intense. Unfortunately, I had my tapioca coffee on an empty stomach, and felt jittery afterwards. Recently, on such a hot day, I decided on the Thai iced tea with tapioca. Sadly, I did not enjoy my drink as much as I did on my previous trip. The drink and the pearls were right on, but my cup was filled with too much crushed ice! I felt as if the drink contained less tea and more ice. I had so many tapioca pearls left that were stuck in between blended pieces of ice. It did not make my occasion any fun trying to suck in the tapioca pearls that were jammed in between ice pieces. Maybe next time around I visit Blenders, I will tell them to hold the ice, or keep it minimum. Personally I don't like the taste of chewy delectable pearls with sharp ice in between.

title: Review: BlendIn Coffee Club — 2018-01-18
summary: I first visited BlendIn Coffee Club two months ago when they had just opened. It's a new cafe in Sugar Land thats tucked away in a quiet neighborhood. We are seriously lacking good coffee houses in this part of town and BlendIn steals the spotlight in this case. I really like the unassuming building
body: I first visited BlendIn Coffee Club two months ago when they had just opened. It's a new cafe in Sugar Land thats tucked away in a quiet neighborhood. We are seriously lacking good coffee houses in this part of town and BlendIn steals the spotlight in this case. I really like the unassuming building and it might have been a bank in its past life. The parking is plentiful and the vibes are minimal. Both the exterior and interior have a crisp and clean look. Upon entering, you'll notice a lab room where they have coffee sampling classes. There is also a wall that contains different kinds of coffee products (siphons and coffee blends). Judging by the atmosphere alone.. you can tell that they take their coffee seriously here. Love the style of this place.. with its unique pod shaped seating and different styles of tables. There's an art gallery towards the back of the cafe as well. Brings upon artistic and minimal vibes. In terms of their coffee.. I recommend the caffe latte with honey. The beans are quite strong and aromatic here. The honey cuts through and brings in a smooth and sweet taste. If you're not into strong coffee then I really wouldn't recommend BlendIn. I've left with a "coffee buzz" a few times around. Mind you, I drink all kinds of coffee but this is truly the rich and dark stuff. I've tried their iced latte as well and its also great. I recommend their iced vanilla latte on a warm day. They also have a lovely white tea with pear. Its fragrant, soothing, and comes in a cute Japanese style tea pot. A good friend of mine ordered their hot cocoa. It looked good and she enjoyed her beverage. They basically have something for everyone here. Pastries/desserts are far and few. I have tried the french macaron and it was crisp and fresh. They also serve up crepe cakes which are hard to find in cafes. Overall, I recommend Blendin for their simplicity and all things coffee. Just don't show up after 6:30 p.m... they are closed by then! :)

title: Review: Blue Fish House II — 2010-05-09

I am not fond of those ultra loungy type of sushi bars. I have tried the splendid 'Udon it' noodle soup. It is a deep sea of exotic goodness.
body:

The sushi here is nice as well. I have tried their avocado roll. The morsels are small, but tasty. I like my sushi light, nothing fattening or deep fried. Isn't it supposed to be healthy in the first place!? Just kidding. You can go for whatever you like. That`s my opinion. :)
I believe they have happy hour sushi as well. Haven`t dropped by in awhile... I think those thick slurpalicious udon noodles are calling me back...

title: Review: Bombay Pizza Express — 2012-09-12
summary: So ive known about Bombay Pizza Company from the very beginning, when they opened their original location in downtown Houston. I remember even having stepped inside their main location and having browsed throughout their menu. At the time I wasn't hungry, but I knew that I wanted to try the place ou
body:
So ive known about Bombay Pizza Company from the very beginning, when they opened their original location in downtown Houston. I remember even having stepped inside their main location and having browsed throughout their menu. At the time I wasn't hungry, but I knew that I wanted to try the place out in the near future. That never happened due to the distance and proximity of the location..
Fast forward two years later, and they opened up a second location in Sugar Land. I finally got to try this place out last week and absolutely loved it. In fact, I ate there twice last week and tried out different foods during my stay. I wont go much into detail, but all I can say is that these folks mastered the art of fusion cuisine very well. I have enjoyed the pizzas, kati rolls, and their veggie burger. The spices and flavours infused within the food were just right. I made the right decision of having ordered the sweet potato fries with my veggie burger. The fries had a subtle hint of spice which went well with the natural taste of the sweet potato. A spicy ketchup relish was served along with these fries which I enjoyed. I'm not much of a french fry person, but these were darn good! The veggie burger was bursting with spices and flavor. It was quite strong actually, and I do believe that horseradish must have been mixed in that burger.
I like how their is a wide selection of items to choose from the menu, but there isnt too much going on, which is a good thing. The pizzas are nice and crispy, and the kati rolls are huge and filling. I ordered the tandoori paneer roll, as well as the tandoori shrimp roll, and enjoyed both. The naan wrapped around these rolls were fresh and crispy. A small side of chutney is served with these rolls which give them extra flavour.
Overall, I enjoyed my stay in this casual pizza restaurant. The place was crowded with families coming in and out. With a warm and friendly environment, mixed in with decent prices, I'm not surprised that this place was packed. I can only hope the best for this restaurant. I'll definitely be visiting again soon, the location is so convenient.

title: Review: Bombay to Beijing — 2010-05-28

body:
I ABSOLUTELY love the idea of Indian and Chinese fusion food! Pretty much makes sense, they are neighbouring countries! I believe this is the only restaurant in town that has stuck with this unique theme.
The decoration inside is beautiful! One side panel has an Indian flair, while another panel has an Oriental feel. The colours of the walls are bold and rich with beautiful paintings.
The menu caters to a unique variety of both Asian foods that are usually not found at other places. I love how they serve up North Indian style food which is famous for their creamy and mild curries.
I recommend Bombay`s Chicken Tikka Masala. It`s the King of Curries in my book! The naan served up is fluffy and warm.
My sister tried out the Wonton Noodle Soup from the Oriental section of the menu. It was decent. I can`t say much about that part of the menu, as I have not tried any of the items.
Another item from the Indian section I favour is the Chicken Tikka Salad. The grilled meat is shredded and served on top of a creamy and crunchy salad. Pretty good. I may order it next time I come around, and use it as leftovers for a sandwich. How`s that for a twist on a good ol` chicken salad sandwich? ;)
This place is a bit on the pricy end. What do you expect? It`s located on the plaza of Sugar Creek.

title: Review: Bonchon — 2017-12-14
summary: Had the chance to try out Bonchon about two weeks ago with a good friend of mine. Its tucked in a nice and quiet plaza near WholeFoods Sugar Land. Bonchon means "home" in Korean, and this is a casual South Korean restaurant. There are quite a few locations spread out in the U.S. so its nice to have
body: Had the chance to try out Bonchon about two weeks ago with a good friend of mine. Its tucked in a nice and quiet plaza near WholeFoods Sugar Land. Bonchon means "home" in Korean, and this is a casual South Korean restaurant. There are quite a few locations spread out in the U.S. so its nice to have them in the neighborhood. My friend and I were seated immediately upon entering and the staff were all smiles. This joint has a unique and airy layout to it. Many tables to choose from and large windows towards the back of the place. I've only tapped into Korean cuisine earlier this year, so I was definitely intrigued by the menu. Mind you, i've had fusion Korean food, but this is more like fast food Korean. The menu is short and simple -- nothing confusing. This place is known for their fried chicken -- so thats an option that many choose from. My friend and I ordered the salmon avocado ball, shrimp shumai, chicken katsu, and a side order of kimchi. I enjoyed every dish for its own flavour, color, taste and texture. The salmon avocado ball reminded me of sushi. The texture of the salmon and avocado were smooth and creamy. There were a few different sauces on top and some crispy topping. Enjoyed the steamed shrimp shumai with honey dijon dressing. My friend wasnt too impressed with the dressing, but I liked the overall taste of this appetizer. The chicken katsu was crunchy, crispy and breaded. It was topped on long grain rice and served with broccoli. It was good but not my favorite. Pairing the chicken katsu with kimchi helped to bring out some flavor. Overall, the dishes were unique.. but I dont think I would specifically crave them again.. maybe the salmon avocado ball. Will definitely have to return and try something new off the menu.. such as the glass noodles and udon soup. The portions are alright.. and the prices are high. So this place has potential but lets hope the food and quality remains consistent. Would recommend at least giving it a go and trying it once.

body: Lovely and quaint little shoppe tucked in Rice Village. I had always wanted to visit this shoppe and finally made the time to do so. Upon entering, you will notice many gifts and novelties of all sorts. As a big tea drinker, I absolutely enjoyed the selection of tea's offered at British Isles. I also adored the many colorful teapots scattered around the shoppe. All sorts of mugs and canisters were lined against the shelves as well. As far as the snacks and treats go.. there are many here. There are various biscuits, jams, syrups and fruit curds. I picked up a package of custard biscuits, Lyle's golden syrup, and cadbury hot chocolate mix. As someone who bakes often, I know that i'll be putting Lyle's golden syrup into good use. There is even a section of frozen items in a little freezer in the corner. Although the store isn't massively large, but somehow they were able to truly create the British essence here with quality products. I could spend hours in here curiously exploring through all of the products. Its a nice spot to get a thoughtful gift for a loved one, or just for yourself!

body:
This is just a simple and quick grab n go Buc-ees.
If you're randomly craving for their in store snacks and treats, you'll find that here. They have the usual assortment of hot coffee, deli items and baked goods. I like their coffee! Strong, piping hot and far from bitter. I'm more of a pour over gal these days. No complaints. It's tastes just like their other locations. Granted, this location is much smaller than their other store fronts; but you'll find many of their products here. It has less bells and whistles though. If you're looking for souvenirs and actual gifts, you'll find it at their much larger locations. This one has an attached gas station and carwash just like the other ones. I've heard good things about their car wash so will definitely revisit. I was able to grab my favorite banana pudding and their coffee. Service was quick and simple. They've got plenty of cold bottled beverages and other random necessities such as milk, eggs, etc. This location isn't too far from Sugar Land so I frequent it every once in awhile. Parking is a bit tight but again, this it totally a grab and go location. Toodle-oo!

summary: I came in here last night with a group of friends. It was helpful to have a buddy of mine that frequents Bellaire. He was able to recommend us to some nice places. One word: Cute! body:
I came in here last night with a group of friends. It was helpful to have a buddy of mine that frequents Bellaire. He was able to recommend us to some nice places.
One word: Cute!
As soon as we stepped in, I noticed the brilliant colours and design. I love the decor of this cafe.
I was very much in the mood for pearl tea, so I was pleased to find out they have a diverse menu full of drinks. What made me even more content was the fact that they serve lychee - green tea. I cannot find it at any other boba places. So I immediately ordered my lychee pearl tea drink, and was very much pleased with my decision! It was downright flavourful, fragrant, and exotic. The boba was chewy, firm, and sweet :: perfect. I love the glass they served it with as well.
Now on to the f o o d ...
My dish was tasty and flavourful. I decided on the Udon Shrimp with Vegetables. The noodles were steaming and soft. The vegetables were crispy and fresh. Shrimp were fresh as well, with an al dente bite to them. The meal was served on a cute box tray, with a sample of tapioca pudding as a small sweet treat. The pudding was made with coconut milk, and served with red beans. Mm! :)
Overall, I enjoyed my experience at Cafe 101. We came on a Thursday night, and the place was bustling with liveliness. I will definitely come back again with my friends.

body: I specifically came for the Illy coffee today. Needed a boost of caffeine and warmth from my latte while taking a stroll inside the Galleria. Illy is one of my favorite coffee brands emerging from Italia. I often visit Cafe Dolce Gelato for their Italian coffee. The caffe latte has a warm, smooth and delightful taste. There are far and few decent options for coffee in the Galleria. I often drop by here.. they've been around for ages. So this little gelateria is tucked in a corner near Nordstrom. I wasn't in the mood for gelato but sampled it anyway and was disappointed. The consistency was off and the gelato was dry and stiff. This place was always a great little spot for some fresh and creamy gelato. I viewed each and every case and it seemed all of them were dry and lack luster. I'm hoping they can get their consistency back. Many of the flavors are traditional and very italian. The pistachios are directly from a farm sourced through Sicily. Other than that, the sandwiches and crepes are tasty. I have tried the caprese panini in the past and it was decent. They also serve up fresh waffle cones to accompany the gelato. As for now, I think i'll just continue sticking to their coffee. It's a nice little cafe to satisfy the sweet tooth when in the midst of a shopping jungle. Until next time..

title: Review: Cafe Marrese — 2023-08-25
summary: What a gross spot. 1 star breakfast experience. The saving grace for 2 stars? The London fog latte. That's the only item we enjoyed during our stay here. Strange breakfast concept with skimpy items that are tasteless and just straight up weird. I ordered a side of hashbrowns to go along with my brea
body:
What a gross spot. 1 star breakfast experience.
The saving grace for 2 stars? The London fog latte.
That's the only item we enjoyed during our stay here.
Strange breakfast concept with skimpy items that are tasteless and just straight up weird. I ordered a side of hashbrowns to go along with my breakfast taco. What came out on my plate was a freaking joke. A tiny skimpy amount of lifeless hashbrowns that were cold and greasy. No crisp, no taste, no "umph" this is hearty and wholesome! The breakfast taco was unappealing as well. The tortilla was bitter and gross, reminded me of the "Mission Tortilla" brand. The filling inside of the taco was just okay as well. When I think of a breakfast taco, I imagine it coming out with salsa or some type of hot sauce. Nothing. Bland. The breakfast hash that was ordered came in a tiny bowl. When you typically think of breakfast hash, you imagine a hearty and large portion of beef brisket dripping with eggs and all the good stuff.
If you're going to overcharge customers, you'd better use fresh tortillas and better ingredients in general. This place was also counter service, so you have to fetch for every single thing. We're spoiled within the inner loop of Houston and appreciate the cafes over there. Service here was just okay, as lukewarm as the food they're serving up. Won't be revisiting and thankfully have no reason, since we're typically not in the area.
Maybe you have to look and behave a certain way in order to receive actual food on your plate and better service. But this? This place just ain't it. Bye-bye.
Edit: I never asked for a "hashbrown" taco. I asked for a regular egg and cheese breakfast taco with an addition of avocado inside the taco. As well as hashbrowns on the side. And that it be served as a side item. I made that clear to the cashier but I guess she didn't catch that for some reason. Communication goes a long way.

All surrounded in the heart of downtown. Caffe Bene is a unique Korean style coffee shop. I definitely recommend you try this place out if you get a chance!

summary: Cozy, comfortable and non-pretentious. Just the way I like my coffee and coffee houses. It was a relaxing evening on a cloudy & rainy day. I looked at my watch and three hours had passed by. Upon entering the cozy "coffee home" you'll notice ample seating and many different types of chairs and couch
body: Cozy, comfortable and non-pretentious. Just the way I like my coffee and coffee houses. It was a relaxing evening on a cloudy & rainy day. I looked at my watch and three hours had passed by. Upon entering the cozy "coffee home" you'll notice ample seating and many different types of chairs and couches to cozy up on. Campesino truly felt like visiting the house of an old friend. Comfortable, quiet and non-distracting. I was able to work on my laptop without disturbance and I was also able to chitchat with friends upon their arrival. The folks at the front register were super friendly and talkative. They led me through the uncomplicated and unique menu. I already knew what I wanted - cafe de olla. The flavour, smoothness, and strength of the coffee was delightful. It wasn't too strong or held too heavy of a taste such as the standard European style coffee's. If anything, I was tired beyond this point of consuming latte's and the cafe de olla was refreshing and suited my palate. I did ask for steamed milk in my cafe de olla but it still remained different then a regular latte and was not as heavy. They also have fresh juice, tea, and other coffee beverages here. Pastries are delightful as well. Might try the savory snacks next time around. I just know that i'll become a regular and will visit more often than not. Thank you Campesino, for inviting me to your "coffee home". I enjoyed my stay and looking forward to visiting again.

body:
Que ricoo! :)
Carmelo`s dishes up authentic burritos, tacos, enchiladas, and so forth.. you name it.
A friend suggested that a group of us try this place out. After mentioning it several times, and how much he liked it... we decided to give it a try.
I ordered the vegetarian burrito. Whoah, was it good! I`m never looking back at Chipotle! Well... unless.. I am craving a hand size type of burrito. You see... at Carmelo`s the burritos are so huge that you have to eat it with a fork and knife. How`s that for grande style! You simply cannot hold it by your hands and eat it. This is strictly a fork and knife burrito.
My burrito was generously filled with so many delicious ingredients. The tortilla is crispy and toasty, which I like. All of my friends enjoyed their dishes as well, which were also pretty huge. We munched on a basket of thin crispy corn tortilla chips accompanied with a mild garlicky salsa. I had leftovers for a good two days.
It`s a spot that I want to take all my burrito loving family and friends. I`m going to try out the other items on their menu next time.
You`ll end up leaving full, comforted, and satisfied with this home cooked style joint.

title: Review: Carter’s — 2024-09-26
summary: This is such a wonderful location of Carter's; from the warm customer service to the vivid selection of clothing they've got for tots and babes. I don't typically find brick and mortar locations of Carter's unless they are tucked away inside some mall or Galleria type location. The physical presence
body:
This is such a wonderful location of Carter's; from the warm customer service to the vivid selection of clothing they've got for tots and babes.
I don't typically find brick and mortar locations of Carter's unless they are tucked away inside some mall or Galleria type location.
The physical presence of this stand alone Carter's makes it worth visiting. They have a good online selection, but in all honesty, it is better to visually see and try the clothing in person for your little one. Sometimes what you see online is what you don't get.
Children typically grow out of clothing rather quickly. Carters clothing can shrink in size and is not of the splendor variety that will hold its shape and structure forever. Therefore, size up and wash those clothing in cold water! Oh and not everything can be thrown into the dryer, depending on the type of fabric or style of clothing. As mentioned earlier, the customer service here is great and you can ask them anything in regards to their products.
I am already loving their autumn and winter apparel. Prices are excellent, patterns are plenty, and they have so many styles and colors for the little one. Loving their beanies, socks, bibs and other niknaks in between.
This is a great retail shop, their hours are good and their selection is massive. One could easily take an hour just browsing their variety and trying it on their little bean. I have already picked up beanies and jumpers for autumn.
Google might say that this Carter's location is closed, but it is definitely open. If you are in the area, go check it out and see for yourself!

title: Review: Casian King Food Truck — 2015-05-16
summary: Pretty tasty cajun + asian food! I ventured out and tried Casian King today at the Asian festival. The lines were long and the weather was hot. That didn't stop me from trying some unique fusion food. I think my favorite was the lobster fries. Full of flavor and topped generously with fresh lobster,
body: Pretty tasty cajun + asian food! I ventured out and tried Casian King today at the Asian festival. The lines were long and the weather was hot. That didn't stop me from trying some unique fusion food. I think my favorite was the lobster fries. Full of flavor and topped generously with fresh lobster, sauce and kimchi. I also ordered the shrimp scampi with rice and a fried egg. The shrimp were good but my only complaint is that all the flavor was on the shell of the fried shrimp. I don't eat shells or tails, so all the flavor was plucked away. My dish was not topped with the crunchy garlic sauce as pictured by other reviewers. Not sure why? Maybe they got really busy with the orders and forgot to top mine. Most of the garlic butter sauce in my dish was in the bottom of the bowl mixed with the lettuce. All in all the meal was good but quite messy to eat. Will stick with the fusion fries. They were great.

title: Review: Cedar Coffee Company — 2023-07-07
summary: This place was awesome! All huddled and cuddled within a quiet corner of two harbors. I love that city and it was pretty neat finding this coffee shoppe on a whim whilst traveling through the north shores. Coffee was great as well as their matcha latte. I've been digging warm matcha latte and asked
body: This place was awesome! All huddled and cuddled within a quiet corner of two harbors. I love that city and it was pretty neat finding this coffee shoppe on a whim whilst traveling through the north shores. Coffee was great as well as their matcha latte. I've been digging warm matcha latte and asked for it to be sweetened with cardamom syrup. Absolutely phenomenon. Cardamom pairs sooo well with matcha - what a matcha made in sight! No pun intended. Everything is practically made in house here, including their house made syrups, baked goods and savory food items. I loved their in house made scone.. warm, buttery and tender. They had a few scone selections to choose from, but we went for the blueberry coconut scone. Tasty and paired well with our beverages. We were also hungry and grabbed their chicken sandwich as well as their Thai style wrap. The wrap consisted of curried veggies, spicy Thai style peanut sauce wrapped up in a toasted lavash wrap bread. Yum. The roasted veggies had an Indian style flavor and paired well with the peanut sauce tucked in, very fusion style wrap. It was nice to eat a flavorful vegetarian lunch item that day, whilst traveling through the city. Indoors seating was plentiful but it was nice to sit outside in their backyard, immersed within a grove of many trees. Weather was refreshing in regards to MN style summers and a perfect little spot to visit before venturing out to a hike. I recommend Cedar Coffee if in the two harbors area. It's lively and adds a splash of coffee color before journeying towards your next adventure. Until next time!

title: Review: Celebrity Cupcakes — 2012-03-19
summary: Overpriced cupcakes with an average taste. The flavours aren't striking, and they don't hit home. This cupcakery is tucked in a small corner near the Rice Village shopping district. I had my first encounter with Celebrity's a few months ago, and have opted to never go back. I ordered a random assort
body:
Overpriced cupcakes with an average taste. The flavours aren't striking, and they don't hit home. This cupcakery is tucked in a small corner near the Rice Village shopping district.
I had my first encounter with Celebrity's a few months ago, and have opted to never go back. I ordered a random assortment of cupcakes to take home. None of the flavours were tasty, and some of the frosting's had a strange pale green colour. Both the red velvet, and the vanilla cupcake had this green frosting. It didn't make sense, and it only made me not want to eat the cupcakes.
I understand the concept of wanting to bake light, fresh, and organic cupcakes. But these little treats just didn't taste like cupcakes. They were too light, and not sweet enough. The typical red velvet cream cheese frosting didn't even taste like the tangy cream cheese that I am familiar with.
Did I mention that I bake amazing cupcakes at home? From now on, I think I will stick with my own delectable delights.

title: Review: Chai Shai — 2015-05-30
summary: The ambiance of this place is completely lacking... but its also because its inside of an old grocery store. I mostly came in here to grab a hot cup of tea so I decided on the Kashmiri chai. body: The ambiance of this place is completely lacking... but its also because its inside of an old grocery store. I mostly came in here to grab a hot cup of tea so I decided on the Kashmiri chai. Well the Kashmiri chai was good. Although it did come in a small foam cup.. the chai was steaming and fresh. The taste was authentic as well. As far as the food goes.. I ordered the beef paratha roll. It was okay. What I liked about the roll was that it was fresh.. but it didn't taste like a beef paratha roll. The inside of the roll was stuffed with strips of beef, cilantro and tomato. This is not how its usually prepared. They also have Mexican food on their menu.. so I feel like they just made a fusion style wrap. I'm more used to the original taste of a beef roll without the fixins. My family ordered the chaat but they complained that it was too sweet. Chaat should have a nice blend of sweet and spicy flavors. I'm not sure if I would come back here again unless im in the area. If I do visit in the future I would probably get the Kashmiri chai and something sweet to go along with it.

title: Review: Chang’s Chinese Restaurant — 2017-12-09
summary: I recently ordered food from Chang's via Yelp's Eat 24 app. Had never used the app before and had never ordered food from Changs before.
