body: I recently ordered food from Chang's via Yelp's Eat 24 app. Had never used the app before and had never ordered food from Changs before. I was delighted with Yelps delivery service and the taste of my food. Chang's has been around Sugar Land for awhile and they have quite a large menu. I ordered vegetable fried rice.. it was warm, fresh and not that salty. The fried rice was loaded with broccoli and other vegetables. Tasty! Also ordered shrimp curry and egg drop soup. The shrimp curry had a strong yellow curry flavor and paired well with the fried rice. It wasn't my favorite dish, and I'll probably have to try another seafood item off the menu.. such as the Hunan shrimp. Lastly, the egg drop soup had an odd yellow color and was rather too salty for my liking. It lacked flavor but was brimming with eggs. Maybe the hot and sour soup is better. But who knows. I'm just glad that the food didn't make me sick. All in all, I enjoyed my order and the food was delivered, hot fresh, and on time. The portions of the items were generous as well. I totally recommend Chang's when the "American Chinese" craving kicks in.

I tried their cuban con leche.. a somewhat strong and sweet milky coffee with a nice taste. I am glad I went with this choice.. as I could grab a great tasting latte from another coffee shop.. but the cuban con leche really stood out. I also recommend their breakfast tacos. I ordered just one and became very full from it.. Made by own breakfast taco with eggs, mushrooms and spinach and asked for cilantro lime rice on the side. The rice wasnt anything special and truly lacked flavor. But nonetheless, I still enjoyed my meal. I look forward in visiting next time when in Austin.

title: Review: Chez Beignets Quan Ong Tre — 2016-02-08
summary: Yum! Such crispy and fresh beignets at this location of Chez B. I think I've become a fan of this stuffy yet busy location in China Town. On a Saturday night, my friends and I stepped inside and were startled with the liveliness of the cafe. Might have had something to do with Chinese New Year's, or
body: Yum! Such crispy and fresh beignets at this location of Chez B. I think I've become a fan of this stuffy yet busy location in China Town. On a Saturday night, my friends and I stepped inside and were startled with the liveliness of the cafe. Might have had something to do with Chinese New Year's, or maybe its always busy here. There was a lot of movement, laughter, and crowded tables. This is the complete opposite image of the location in Sugar Land. You see.. the Chez location in Sugar Land has some of the nastiest employees. I stopped visiting that particular location two years ago when they pushed my mother and I out the door (just because she didn't order anything). My mother had simply wanted to join my company as it was a quiet weekend night and I felt like I wanted to be out. To make a long story short.. that location in particular is not worth the visit. The employees are stiff and unfriendly. Maybe that's why its often empty inside. So back to my review on this location in China Town.. its far busier and livelier. My friends and I were lucky enough to find a small table to situate ourselves in. The beignets came quick and piping hot to the table. They were larger and crispier in size as well. Yum! What I love most about the beignets at Chez is that the dough is mixed with nutmeg. The dough is also perfectly fried and isn't too chewy in the middle such as Crescent City. The experience makes for a better tasting beignet in all. The hot chicory coffee is also nice and strong. The second refill of chicory coffee is on the house. I was satisfied with one serving and enjoyed it with the beignets. It was the perfect way to end a chilly Saturday night. Their are quite a few people I know that have never tasted a beignet. I like them better than doughnuts. I'll definitely be back and bring out of towners here.

title: Review: Chipotle Mexican Grill — 2010-07-01
summary: Due to the overwhelming HUGE size burritos Chipotle`s has to offer, I find myself coming here only once a year or so. Why? body:
Due to the overwhelming HUGE size burritos Chipotle`s has to offer, I find myself coming here only once a year or so.
Why? Partly due to leaving very well satisfied and insanely stuffed like a burrito that I do not crave it for a very long time.
I do wish Chipotle`s had their burritos in different size options. But oh well, it`s alright, that`s what gives this place its charm.
This location gives a whopping generous portion, which I truly appreciate. The selection is always fresh and in abundance. I simply cannot resist the gem coloured guacamole and peppers. The salsas are mild yet flavourful. I usually ask for a mix of salsas for a burst of zesty-goodness taste.
By the time I unwrap and eat my burrito, I simply amuse myself in realizing that it weighs the same as a newborn baby. Hah! Chipotle`s napkins even demonstrate the correct way in eating their burritos. Clever gimmick. Its true though, once I ended up eating my burrito in a monstrous way in such the seams ended up tearing and all the filling came out! No one wants a damaged burrito, now do they?
I love me my Chipotle. I believe a burrito from this spot has been long overdue . . .

title: Review: Christina's Donuts — 2017-03-07
summary: Randomly spotted this place from across the street. It was glowing and taunting me to come inside. I was actually pretty hungry and realized that I hadn't eaten in awhile - so I decided to stop in and grab a few donuts with my sister. It was night time and I seriously thought they would have ran out
body: Randomly spotted this place from across the street. It was glowing and taunting me to come inside. I was actually pretty hungry and realized that I hadn't eaten in awhile - so I decided to stop in and grab a few donuts with my sister. It was night time and I seriously thought they would have ran out of most of their selection. But that wasn't the case. So I picked up the apple fritter, cake donut and crueller. All three are my favorite and I was happy to eat a bite of each - yummy! The donuts were fresh, crisp and not too large. They are dirt cheap so the small sizes did not bother me. I liked how the donuts weren't too sweet. They satisfied my craving and kept me a bit full until dinner. These are just standard donuts - nothing fancy. We didn't experience any rude service - I think the man behind the counter was working as fast as he could. Donuts were around $3.30 in total.. again.. super cheap and simple. I'll definitely be back if in the area. They seem to serve up sandwiches are cold drinks as well. But i'll probably just stick to the donuts.

title: Review: Cillie’s Cakes — 2015-08-02
summary: Cillie's cakes have always been lovely, but I have noticed they have become way too sweet as of recent. In the future, I would most likely pre-order a cake and have them cut down on the sugar. With the cakes being too sweet, the flavour becomes lacking. We've been having their cakes for years, but I
body: Cillie's cakes have always been lovely, but I have noticed they have become way too sweet as of recent. In the future, I would most likely pre-order a cake and have them cut down on the sugar. With the cakes being too sweet, the flavour becomes lacking. We've been having their cakes for years, but I just wasn't fond of the mini cakes up front. The cheesecake and the mousse cake are quite nice though. Not as sweet, but rich, smooth and creamy. Overall, I do like how their cakes are made with light ingredients. Rather than heavy buttercream frosting, most of the cakes here are light and made up of whipped cream. I also like how most of the cakes are moist and incorporated with fresh fruit. Its a nice cakery shoppe if you're looking for something different. They have spicy and salty snacks as well - such as their sandwiches and wraps. I have not tried them before but I may do so next time around. The location is convenient and the bake shoppe is located in a quiet corner. Will drop by soon and grab a few other items off their menu next time around. Always nice to support local business as well - give Cillie's a try!

title: Review: Cinnamon’s Bakery — 2015-11-15
summary: Cinnamon's is a simple and quaint bakery established within a well known neighborhood in Sugar Land. It's quite old and a bit outdated from the inside of the shoppe. This bakery has been around for many years, yet I finally had the chance to drop by recently. The shoppe closes every day at noon. I h
body: Cinnamon's is a simple and quaint bakery established within a well known neighborhood in Sugar Land. It's quite old and a bit outdated from the inside of the shoppe. This bakery has been around for many years, yet I finally had the chance to drop by recently. The shoppe closes every day at noon. I happened to be around the area early at that time. I like how the main theme is all about cinnamon rolls! I absolutely enjoy doughnuts, but its quite nice to have a bakery that specializes in cinnamon rolls and sticky buns. They also have various fruit flavored strudels and kolaches with only meat options. I knew what I wanted so I opted for both a cinnamon roll and sticky bun. They were still slightly warm when I got home to eat them. Both products were nice yet way too sweet for my liking. I believe all that glaze on the cinnamon roll made it strikingly sweet for me. I prefer cream cheese icing on cinnamon rolls over powdered sugar icing. The sticky buns were way too sweet as well. It was a nice little roll though, as it was something new for me. I liked the crunchy and glazed pecans scattered all over the sticky bun. It kind of tasted like a pecan pie to me in some ways. Overall, the products were decent. I also believe both of the buns could have been softer in texture. I wouldn't mind dropping by every now and then. I think i'm just put off by products with way too much sugar. But if its your thing, than you may like it.

title: Review: Cliff’s Hamburger Grill — 2017-12-14
summary: Cliffs Old Fashioned Hamburgers.. where has this place been all my life? Thank you to Mike M. for introducing it to me! I was just here over the past weekend that went by.. & had the opportunity to meet my fellow Yelpers. Had a grand ol' time and enjoyed burgers in good company. Upon entering the bu
body:
Cliffs Old Fashioned Hamburgers.. where has this place been all my life?
Thank you to Mike M. for introducing it to me!
I was just here over the past weekend that went by.. & had the opportunity to meet my fellow Yelpers. Had a grand ol' time and enjoyed burgers in good company.
Upon entering the burger dive.. there was a friendly old man inside the place who said its probably older than my mom. Maybe. I felt like I was transported back to the good old days. Didn't feel like eating beef as I had eaten it a few times during the week so I opted for a chicken sandwich. This native California girl specifically chose the California chicken sandwich.. & let me tell you.. it was good! Its a popular item and a safe bet with so many selections on the menu. Food took quite some time to arrive.. but the weather was lovely and so many people were seated inside and outside the restaurant. Its plain to see how popular this burger joint is.. all kinds of folk were there on a Saturday afternoon. The folk running the restaurant are super friendly and kind.. we were delivered some of the best service.. and it was appreciated. Everyone joined their food.. it was fresh, hot, crispy and tasty. My California chicken sandwich consisted of a juicy marinated chicken breast, creamy avocado, melty white cheese, mayo, tomato, bun, etc. It was a tasty meal and wasn't salty or anything. Portion was quite decent.. felt quite full after eating half of the sandwich. Tried an onion ring from a friend... and it had a flavorful and crispy texture. I'll most definitely try something different off the menu when I visit next time around.. they have such a diverse menu and there is surely something for everyone. Might try their black bean burger or salmon burger next time around. The crispy fish sandwich looks good as well. I'm definitely bringing my family to this popular old joint. It was a well spent Saturday with my Yelp friends. Try it out and bring your friends a long as well. Think you'll like it too. :)

title: Review: Cloud 10 Creamery — 2013-09-29
summary: My 100th review goes out to Cloud 10 Creamery! This place has some awesome ice-cream flavours. body:
My 100th review goes out to Cloud 10 Creamery!
This place has some awesome ice-cream flavours. If you're bold enough to try eccentric and unique frozen treats, then you're going to love this place! Cloud 10 Creamery has ice-creams, sorbets, sundaes, soda pop floats, and more! My favourite flavours are the toasted rice, dulce de leche chamomile, and the black sesame milk chocolate. These are flavour combinations that you typically would not experience in the form of ice-cream! That is what makes Cloud 10 Creamery stand out from the crowd. Once you savor the tantalizing treats featured at this cafe, you'll be wanting to come back for more! I particularly love the gingersnap sundae. The sundae is loaded with gingersnap ice-cream and plentiful of tasty toppings. All of which are made from scratch. Its a seasonal treat featured at this time, so come and get it while it lasts!
Oh, and one more thing.. the frozen-treat cafe is located in Rice Village, which makes for a nice hangout with family and friends. The environment is chill and the staff and chefs are friendly. It all makes for a great experience when you come on by and treat yourself to this place.

summary: This place is still good mind you. Although I do wish it were a little bigger inside. I came recently on a weekend night with my relatives. body: This place is still good mind you. Although I do wish it were a little bigger inside. I came recently on a weekend night with my relatives. To our luck, the largest table was empty so we got to situate ourselves there. I tried the crepe Suzette for the first time. It was good, but the orange reduction sauce was undesirable. The cafe could also use a little help on the weekends (with more staff) when it gets quite busy and bustling inside.

title: Review: Coco Crepes, Waffles & Coffee — 2015-12-02
summary: This location of Coco's Crepes is tucked in a quiet little corner of Rice Village. Having been to the original Coco's in Midtown many of times, the new location in the village was a nice change of scenery. Upon entering, I noticed how clean it was inside and preferred the layout and space of the new
body: This location of Coco's Crepes is tucked in a quiet little corner of Rice Village. Having been to the original Coco's in Midtown many of times, the new location in the village was a nice change of scenery. Upon entering, I noticed how clean it was inside and preferred the layout and space of the new cafe. My family and I decided to share a creme brulee crepe and ordered our own coffee beverages. The creme brulee crepe was a flavour that I had never tried before. Let me tell you this.. It was delicious! The crepe was large, fluffy and chewy. It was big enough for my family and I to share. The creme brulee crepe was filled with a decadent smooth pastry creme and sliced strawberries. The outside of the crepe was bruleed, which created a crispy texture, and was drizzled with chocolate sauce. The presentation was beautiful and we were all satisfied. Unfortunately, our coffee beverages that we ordered (cafe au lait & latte) never arrived to our table. I went up to the cashier/barista and reminded her of our order. In which case she looked confused because she had completely forgotten about our coffee! I was surprised that she had forgotten about our drinks, in regards to our small and simple order. She quickly made our drinks and brought it to our table. The girl was friendly yet seemed quite out of it. Maybe it had been a long day for her? Anyhow, my family and I still enjoyed our experience here. This location serves up waffles and a few other items as well. I may try a sweet waffle next time around. Coco's is always a nice little spot to visit for some good desserts and to bring family, friends, or out of town guests.

body: Pretty decent Taiwanese style milk tea with tapioca. I can't say much about the food but it was packed inside on a weekend afternoon. I don't think I would come here for the food anyways, but it's a simple little spot if you want some decent tapioca. I happened to drop by after I got a haircut at the salon next door. They do give a large cup for the size of their milk tea, which was made fresh. Might also try another drink on the menu next time around.

title: Review: Coffee Mill — 2023-08-08
summary: I like this spot! It's a bit of a hole in the wall. It's super quick to pass by and you can easily miss it. All these years I thought this place only sold coffee beans but it's actually a sit down cafe. What's unique about Coffee Mill is that it's connected with Kolache Factory. You can order coffee
body: I like this spot! It's a bit of a hole in the wall. It's super quick to pass by and you can easily miss it. All these years I thought this place only sold coffee beans but it's actually a sit down cafe. What's unique about Coffee Mill is that it's connected with Kolache Factory. You can order coffee right up at the corner, then turn around, and order kolaches from the other side of the cafe. Kolaches are many in flavor and are filling in size and always warm. Service is good and they always warm up the kolaches for customers. My favorite is the chicken enchilada kolache as well as the spinach kolache. Both look small in size but they're actually packed with filling and flavor. I've never had any products from any other kolache factory, so I can't compare... But I like the selection this location has. These days I adore their iced caffe latte. It's creamy, fragrant and light. It's not like those iced coffees that are super strong and bitter in flavor. I ask them to make it half sweet with vanilla and it's perfect in flavor. They use Katz coffee here and the beans are local which is something I always support. Go for the local! So glad to have to spot close by within the Galleria area to grab a snack and some type of coffee. If you visit earlier in the day, you'll get a better selection of their baked goods. They also serve up cream cheese kolaches, sweet fruit kolaches and cinnamon rolls. Will revisit when needing an iced caffe latte and a bite to the eat in this heat. Until next time!

title: Review: Common Bond Bistro & Bakery — 2024-12-30
summary: This is such a cozy and lovely location of Common Bond Bistro & Bakery. In fact, this location is probably my favorite within the greater Houston area! It is so open, colorful, warm and inviting with the café. Nestled within the vibrant and upbeat neighborhood of Tanglewood. They've got plenty of in
body:
This is such a cozy and lovely location of Common Bond Bistro & Bakery.
In fact, this location is probably my favorite within the greater Houston area! It is so open, colorful, warm and inviting with the café. Nestled within the vibrant and upbeat neighborhood of Tanglewood. They've got plenty of indoor garage parking that is steps away from the café. Perfect. No need to fight for parking. A quiet and serene location that surrounds itself within the grounds of an apartment building. This location in particular opened up over the previous summer season, and until then, it remains clean with friendly and cordial customer service. I love the decorated atmosphere with the hues of blue, pink and yellow. The décor brings upon a soft and inviting atmosphere, perfect for catching up with friends or reading/working.
Santiago and fellow crew members are wonderful. This bistro location of Common Bond has a decent selection of both savory and pastry items. I have tried a few of their savory items, and they were all delectable. Their soups in particular are some of my favorite. Pair it with a baked bread? Lush. Their pistachio croissants, as well as their macarons, brownies and cookies are the repeated sweet items you will find at any of their bakery locations. Just as tasty, sweet and memorable. I enjoy their café lattes and look forward to their seasonal latte menu. Cappuccinos? Perfect. Those go straight to my heart.
Give this location a try, you will love it. They also have a quiet section upstairs where you can chat over coffee and conversations... you get what I'm sayin?
Until next time! ;)

title: Review: Copenhagen Bakery & Cafe — 2015-05-16
summary: My favourite bakery when visiting California! I love the unique array of Scandinavian style desserts at Copenhagen Bakery. My favorites are the princess cake, cinnamon rolls and cheesecake. I love how each dessert is uniquely its own. Copenhagen has a great selection of breakfast and lunch items as
body: My favourite bakery when visiting California! I love the unique array of Scandinavian style desserts at Copenhagen Bakery. My favorites are the princess cake, cinnamon rolls and cheesecake. I love how each dessert is uniquely its own. Copenhagen has a great selection of breakfast and lunch items as well. They have a nice array of tea, coffee, smoothies and hot chocolate. The baked loaves of bread look tempting here as well. There is something for everyone here. Just about everything is lovely about this bakery and it is totally worth the stop when visiting the city.

title: Review: Cornelius Nursery — 2023-04-17
summary: What an awesome flower nursery! This spot has it all and more! Its quite a large and extensive flower wonderland, haha. But its totally worth a trip if you're within the Sugar Land area and love all things nature, flowers and plants. I had spotted Cornelius Nursery so many times in the past but fina
body: What an awesome flower nursery! This spot has it all and more! Its quite a large and extensive flower wonderland, haha. But its totally worth a trip if you're within the Sugar Land area and love all things nature, flowers and plants. I had spotted Cornelius Nursery so many times in the past but finally ventured out within the past week. It's totally worth a trip because it's a refreshing spot that uplifts your spirits - even if you don't end up purchasing anything. An evergreen spot to visit with fams and friends on a bright, sunny day. There's a whimsical little gift shoppe nestled right by the nursery as well. They have plenty of gift products and items to choose from such as candles, lotions and fragrance items. Going back to the foliage, they have various plants to choose from. Doesn't matter your expertise on gardening, you'll be sure to find yourself something that's best suitable for your needs. I love fresh herbs and greenery so I picked up mint and rosemary. They also have unique bird houses here and plant pots to choose from. I'll be sure to revisit to create an ever-growing bundle of fresh gourmand herbs. Decent service as well, kind folk rummaging through the garden. Until next time!

title: Review: Corner Bakery Cafe — 2011-09-29
summary: Finally got to try Corner Bakery today on a rainy evening. It is quite noticeable for those who pass by the city often, you cant miss it. The atmosphere of the cafe is spacious and comfortable. I enjoyed my time here at night, since it was raining and the interior of the cafe has a nice dim lighting
body: Finally got to try Corner Bakery today on a rainy evening. It is quite noticeable for those who pass by the city often, you cant miss it. The atmosphere of the cafe is spacious and comfortable. I enjoyed my time here at night, since it was raining and the interior of the cafe has a nice dim lighting at night. The food itself is standard, and the portion is a bit small. I ordered a half soup and half panini combination. I felt as if the half panini sandwich was a bit small for its size. Nonetheless the sandwich was good, but could have had more filling. I decided to try the coffee to see it would be any good, and it was. I ordered a small mocha coffee and it was sweet and intense. I haven't tried any of their desserts, but I do feel more variety could be added in their bakery selection. The cinnamon pound cake looks yummy, and I will definitely try that next time I visit. I also like the fact that free wifi is provided. All in all, its a nice place to relax and grab a simple bite to eat. I am sure I will be back soon enough, as it is on the way to my campus.

title: Review: Couscous a Gogo — 2017-03-23
summary: My sister and I enjoyed a delicious and memorable meal here as we ate outside on a cool weekday night. Both the concept and ambiance are totally unique. Anis (the owner) made us feel welcomed and comfortable. He made my sister and I feel like family, as we happily chatted with him about Mediterranea
body: My sister and I enjoyed a delicious and memorable meal here as we ate outside on a cool weekday night. Both the concept and ambiance are totally unique. Anis (the owner) made us feel welcomed and comfortable. He made my sister and I feel like family, as we happily chatted with him about Mediterranean/North African cuisine. I totally dig that kind of food - from those warm and rich cultures full of hospitality. That is what we received here at Couscous a Gogo. I was craving a warm and hearty plate of couscous with meat, so I ordered the beef couscous plate. The stew was tender with succulent pieces of beef and hearty chunks of root vegetables. Served on a bed of steamed couscous. I asked for a bit of harissa (hot sauce) which totally complimented the meal, and you cant go wrong with harissa and couscous! My sister enjoyed her rosemary chicken sandwich. The grilled chicken was tender and full of flavor. Fries were my least favorite. They were lukewarm and thin - didn't remind me of pomme frites. Anyway, I often eat vegetarian, but the meat is exceptional and of good quality. Meatless items are also served up on the menu - if ya swing that way. They use fresh and local ingredients in the food and you can simply taste it in every bite. Yummy! Wish I could eat some couscous right about now. It is so comforting and I totally left with satisfaction and a warm happy belly. Please give this local establishment a chance. The whole staff is so welcoming and super kind. They are crafting up some light, healthy and innovative food that will tickle your tastebuds! I will definitely be back when visiting the area and will try something new. Until then. Au revoir!

title: Review: Cravers’ Corner — 2013-01-04
summary: Came here two months ago, back in November. The cafe had recently opened around that time. Craver's corner is a decent spot which serves up tapioca drinks, ice cream, and pastries. I had the craving for a nice tapioca drink, so I settled for the lychee green tea with tapioca. Unfortunately, I felt a
body:
Came here two months ago, back in November. The cafe had recently opened around that time.
Craver's corner is a decent spot which serves up tapioca drinks, ice cream, and pastries. I had the craving for a nice tapioca drink, so I settled for the lychee green tea with tapioca. Unfortunately, I felt as if the tapioca was too soft for my liking. The taste of the drink itself was good, but the texture of the tapioca was lacking. That said, I did appreciate the customer service. The young man working in the front was kind and friendly. He even allowed me to sample the tapioca pearl before purchasing my drink. After sampling the pearl, I knew it was soft, yet I still settled for the drink, to see its overall taste. I may come back again, sometime soon, and try another drink. I did see other drinks such as smoothies there as well. I hope this little spot can do well, and improve the taste of their drinks. I may try their ice cream next time around. They seem to have a unique selection of flavours for their frozen treats.

title: Review: Crescent City Beignets — Upper Kirby — 2011-09-23
summary: I finally got to check out Crescent City over the summer! There used to be a location in SL back in the day, but was shut down years ago. My only concern is the long distance to get these sweet treats. Actually, I should be content that this location is far from me. Otherwise I would be splurging ev
body:
I finally got to check out Crescent City over the summer! There used to be a location in SL back in the day, but was shut down years ago. My only concern is the long distance to get these sweet treats. Actually, I should be content that this location is far from me. Otherwise I would be splurging ever so often. Haha.
My craving for beignets had been long overdue. There's just something about fluffy fried pillowy-goodness dough! Words cannot explain my love for beignets! I came here with a group of friends. The sweet fritters came promptly to our table with a huge dousing of powdered sugar. I would warn you all to not dive in right away! These pockets are burning with a bunch of steam inside of 'em. Give yourself a few minutes before munching on them. Seriously. My mouth almost burned when I excitedly decided to tear up one beignet. As far as the drinks go, the cafe au lait is a great addition along side a basket of beignets. The coffee was sweet and creamy. My friend ordered the hot chocolate drink and was upset to find it disgusting! I tried one sip and found it to be old and odd-tasting. We came here at night, they must have left the milk inside for too long. I don't know, but I wouldn't ever try ordering the hot chocolate after that incident.
Nonetheless, its great to have a NOLA style cafe in Houston. I haven't tried their savoury items, but one thing is for sure, their beignets are delicious and what will keep me coming back for more.

title: Review: Crescent City Beignets — Houston — 2015-12-02
summary: Rather than completely vanishing, I am glad that CCB decided to re-locate their business. The new location is tucked in a small plaza strip on Westheimer. The parking is quite tight though and you may have to park at the plaza located next to the cafe. At least that is what I had to do on a busy Fri
body: Rather than completely vanishing, I am glad that CCB decided to re-locate their business. The new location is tucked in a small plaza strip on Westheimer. The parking is quite tight though and you may have to park at the plaza located next to the cafe. At least that is what I had to do on a busy Friday night. It is not my favorite part of town, but it is closer than the old location. This part of town does get quite lively throughout the week with many different shops open until late at night. The environment is dimly lighted as the previous location, and the interior space is stuffy with little to no space to move around, especially near the coffee station and ordering section. The folks working here are friendly and move as fast as possible with many orders coming their way. I have tried both the regular beignets and the strip beignets. My favorite will always be the regular beignets. I did notice the beignets were chewier and dense than usual. Maybe they should be fried a bit longer, or the dough should be rolled out smoother. The beignets at the previous CCB location were my favorite. I used to stuff my face with so many beignets at one time! Those were the days. I'll definitely be dropping by again and I'm hoping the beignets will have improved by then. But other than that, I am glad that CCB is still around and I am looking forward to bringing out of town guests here!

title: Review: Croissant-Brioche — 2013-07-26
summary: Croissant-Brioche is probably the cutest name a Parisian-style bakery could ever have! Upon entering, I was greeted warmly by the staff. I came here on a mid-afternoon day, & was lucky to grab a few of the remaining desserts behind the case. I opted for the almond croissant, chocolate croissant, and
body: Croissant-Brioche is probably the cutest name a Parisian-style bakery could ever have! Upon entering, I was greeted warmly by the staff. I came here on a mid-afternoon day, & was lucky to grab a few of the remaining desserts behind the case. I opted for the almond croissant, chocolate croissant, and the almond-chocolate croissant. There was only one of each left, so I was quick to chose what I wanted. I enjoyed each croissant, but my absolute favourite was the almond-chocolate croissant. The blend of both almond marzipan & a nice filling of chocolate squeezed together inside a croissant was marvelous. I love both flavours, so having them together in one pastry was delectable. The filling wasn't too sweet, it was just right. I'll definitely be back here again to try out the other pastries as well.

title: Review: D’amico’s Italian Market Cafe — 2013-04-06
summary: D'amico's is a nice and rustic cafe situated within the Rice Village shopping district. The market serves up some hearty and authentic Italian style food. body:
D'amico's is a nice and rustic cafe situated within the Rice Village shopping district. The market serves up some hearty and authentic Italian style food. I came in here recently on a weekend night and it was quite busy. Luckily, the service was prompt, and it didnt take too long to get a seat. My sister and I were greeted kindly and were offered thick slices of bread which we doused with some olive oil.
I had a craving for gnocchi, so I went ahead and ordered the potato gnocchi with pesto. My sister ordered the angel hair with eggplant and capers which was served with a hearty tomato sauce. I forgot the exact name of her dish, but it was tasty. I enjoyed my gnocchi as well. It was served with a brilliant green pesto sauce that complimented the dish nicely. I love the feel of the market and how it is packed with goodies and food ingredients from Italy. The environment is stuffed with people and stacked with items all around. Nonetheless, the market is comfortable and warm inside. I'm looking forward in trying out the gelato and various other desserts next time around. Overall, this cafe offers a variety within their food selection and its definitely a place worth trying.

title: Review: Daiso — Sugar Land — 2022-03-08
summary: Clean, new, Daiso shoppe! I'm liking this new location in the burbs' even more than the original in the city. This location of Daiso is sparkling clean & super organized. body:
Clean, new, Daiso shoppe!
I'm liking this new location in the burbs' even more than the original in the city. This location of Daiso is sparkling clean & super organized. They pretty much have every random item that you're looking for. Items that you might not even need, but eventually grow accustomed to! Daiso has quality products that are shipped from Japan, which is why I was surprised that this location was stocked up to the brim. Although much smaller than the location in the city; it's basically compacted and has the same products. This location is situated in the heart of Sugar Land, specifically within the mini Asian plaza. The plaza has grown so much in the past few years and it's a warm welcome to have Daiso in the burbs'. A colorful spot full of random niknaks, food products and home furnishings. You'll basically find something for everyone in this little shoppe. It's a neat spot for practical gift giving ideas. I brought my toddler nephew here, and he was thrilled to find toy cars. They have awesome toys for the youngins' and cute kitchen items for the older folk. Most products are $5 & under. You'll be able to pinch pennies & save quite a lot. All in all, this fun little shoppe always comes through. It'll definitely be a spot to revisit again whenever in the S.L. area.

title: Review: Dandanah Cafe & Grill — 2013-12-07
summary: Dandanah Cafe serves up Mediterranean and Egyptian food. The latter is more difficult to find in Houston, even with all the diversity the city has to offer. My sister and I came in here just to try the Egyptian food. Having knowledge on the cuisine, I knew exactly which dishes pertained to the cultu
body:
Dandanah Cafe serves up Mediterranean and Egyptian food. The latter is more difficult to find in Houston, even with all the diversity the city has to offer. My sister and I came in here just to try the Egyptian food. Having knowledge on the cuisine, I knew exactly which dishes pertained to the culture. My sister ordered the Hawawshy (meat pie) and I ordered the Goulash. Both of our dishes were stuffed with ground beef. Mine was wrapped with a pastry dough and my sisters meal was baked inside of a bread. Her dish was much tastier and warmer than mine. My dish was cold and came with a simple salad without any dressing. Given the price.. it wasn't worth it. My sisters dish was a buck less and was more substantial. It came with a side of veggies and a salad dressing. Our server was friendly and checked on us many of times. He was helpful as well. I also ordered a cafe latte, which was four dollars. It was a bit pricy, but at least they used Lavazza coffee.
All in all, our meals were decent. I may try another savory Egyptian dish the next time I drop by. Perhaps the Koshary, or the Pasta with Bechamel.
They also serve dessert such as Kanafeh and Umm Ali which i'll order with coffee the next time I come around. There are also large cakes within their display case. My sweet tooth will make its way here quite soon again.
PS- I cant stand the smell of hookah. Given this weather, all the hookah smokers decided to smoke inside the cafe. The smell gives me a headache, but I came in just to try the food. I let my server know, and he allowed us to sit in another spot of the cafe. He even turned on the heater because I mentioned that it was cold inside. Yep.. good customer service matters!

title: Review: Dandelion Cafe — 2017-12-29
summary: I've been to Dandelion Cafe twice now and I definitely like the concept of this place. The outside and the inside of the cafe are nicely decorated and inviting. Its cute and cozy to have this little cafe tucked in Bellaire Blvd. I think its wise to say that we need more coffee houses in that part of
body: I've been to Dandelion Cafe twice now and I definitely like the concept of this place. The outside and the inside of the cafe are nicely decorated and inviting. Its cute and cozy to have this little cafe tucked in Bellaire Blvd. I think its wise to say that we need more coffee houses in that part of town. I live out in Sugar Land.. but I enjoy venturing out and supporting local business. Service is warm and friendly. Nice place to hangout with friends and family. The coffee here is great. They use Greenway Coffee, which also happens to be a local Houston favorite. The beans are smooth and aromatic. I've tried both the pumpkin spice latte & gingerbread latte. Enjoyed them during this holiday season. The syrups are handmade and you can certainly taste it in the beverages. The coffee is definitely what I see myself coming back to. The food? Not so sure about that. I've tried the veggie delight sandwich on both occasions when visiting Dandelion. First time around, the sandwich was loaded with the good stuff: marinated eggplant, caramelized onions, red pepper spread, grilled asparagus, mushrooms, etc. Served with a small cup of watermelon. Its a tasty vegetarian sandwich.. and it came with a lighter tasting bread the first time around.. kind of like french bread. The second time upon visiting, the sandwich was much smaller in size and the bread was darker. Didn't pair well with the roasted veg. Served with a little cup of pickles. Well. I wasn't impressed. If the portion size is going to get smaller.. so should the price. The prices are steep for whats offered on the menu. I did enjoy the stuffed french toast, and the bagel dots stuffed with vegetable cream cheese. They also serve soup, salads, and dessert here. There is a variety of drinks for everyone and not just coffee. Think i'll just stick to a cafe latte and something sweet off the menu. Simple cafe vibes. I recommend checking out this place.

title: Review: Darband Shishkabob — 2015-07-16
summary: Not sure what happened to the food.. but the quality has gone downhill. My family and I occasionally order "to-go" from here. The food has always been quick and standard. Nothing with a wow factor here. Just quick and authentic food that you can order on the phone and comfortably eat else where. I'm
body: Not sure what happened to the food.. but the quality has gone downhill. My family and I occasionally order "to-go" from here. The food has always been quick and standard. Nothing with a wow factor here. Just quick and authentic food that you can order on the phone and comfortably eat else where. I'm not much of a fan of dining inside. Our usual order of the beef kubideh was scrawny and thin looking. The beef kubideh was not plump and full of flavor as it used to be. We also ordered hummus this time around. It was too sour and grainy for my liking. Most likely made with canned chickpeas. The bread that came a long with my order was hard like a rock. It was pale, chewy, and not so edible looking. Anyways, I don't mind giving Darband a chance again.. But in the meanwhile i'll visit other familiar restaurants that actually put in effort in their food.

title: Review: Diego’s Cantina — 2012-07-02
summary: I have been to Diego's Cantina twice so far, and have enjoyed my stay. The quality of the food is fresh and delicious. The menu serves up a unique and lighter fare of Mexican cuisine. The tri-colored tortilla chips served here are awesome, along side with the salsa that is paired with it. I have onl
body:
I have been to Diego's Cantina twice so far, and have enjoyed my stay. The quality of the food is fresh and delicious. The menu serves up a unique and lighter fare of Mexican cuisine. The tri-colored tortilla chips served here are awesome, along side with the salsa that is paired with it. I have only had good service during my two trips here. The inside of the restaurant reminds me of an art museum. Their are beautiful paintings inside as well as a unique interior ambiance.
So ive ordered the vegetarian tamales here twice during my stay. It is by far my favourite item on the menu. I love the fact that there are roasted corn kernels topped on top of the tamales. The meal sits on top of fresh veggies and is garnished with mole sauce. I have not tried the enchilada's, but I do remember my sister ordering them, and noticing that the topped corn was missing on her dish. Other than that, my experience has been well here. I do hope they keep their service and food fresh as always, because its a nice place to have in town when you're looking for something different and on the lighter fare.

title: Review: Dish Society — 2015-09-07
summary: Having brunch here yesterday was not bad.. but not my favorite either. I had ordered an omelette and it was too flat and crispy for my liking. I prefer more of a fluffy and softer egg. body: Having brunch here yesterday was not bad.. but not my favorite either. I had ordered an omelette and it was too flat and crispy for my liking. I prefer more of a fluffy and softer egg. The eggs had a smell to them as well. I have had better omelettes at other restaurants. The skillet potatoes were okay as well. The nutella french toast was unique and different. I had shared it with my family. It was too sweet and more of a dessert for me. The place was packed and there were many people. I do feel more vegetarian options should be included on the menu. I can see myself coming back and trying another item or two. The neighborhood of the restaurant is nice as well. Will perhaps be back in the near future, maybe for dinner.

title: Review: Dolce & Cafe — 2022-05-02
summary: Oh gosh, such stiff and awkward service upon stepping into this local cafe. This cafe is quaint and whimsical inside. The interior is quite dark though. The seats are plentiful and decently comfortable. The service? Not so much. The young lady just stared at us bleakly as we stared at her right back
body: Oh gosh, such stiff and awkward service upon stepping into this local cafe. This cafe is quaint and whimsical inside. The interior is quite dark though. The seats are plentiful and decently comfortable. The service? Not so much. The young lady just stared at us bleakly as we stared at her right back. No hi, hello, or anything. Not even a smile. I uncomfortably ordered an iced coffee. I then paused and asked if she could add 2% milk to it. Then she finally, yet bleakly responded. Hallelujah, I guess. My friend ordered an iced tea, along with a pastry. Our orders came quietly onto our table, followed by the pastry that was getting toasted a bit in their oven. The iced coffee was by far the worst tasting coffee I have ever had. It had zero flavor, aroma or anything that could even remind you of coffee. It was completely flat and bitter tasting. Nothing. It was a warm day out - but I'm thinking their warm coffee is better tasting, given their reviews. The pastry was warm and crisp, flaky and lightly sweet. I may revisit & try a crepe or their french toast. But I'm having mixed feelings. The city of Houston has plenty of memorable cafes to offer. This might have just been an off day. Other than that the cafe was busy with folk enjoying their crepes and savory items. The menu is quite extensive. Dolce means sweet in Italian; and our experience was quite the contrary. May bump up the review if a more pleasant experience is encountered on a prospective visit.

title: Review: Don Cafe — 2013-06-11
summary: I absolutely love banh mi sandwiches! It's great to finally have a banh mi restaurant not too far from Sugar Land. You dont have to drive all the way to the city, or get lost in Midtown! (Not that I dont love the city, but sometimes I get lazy to drive out there). This place is fairly new, so its ul
body:
I absolutely love banh mi sandwiches! It's great to finally have a banh mi restaurant not too far from Sugar Land. You dont have to drive all the way to the city, or get lost in Midtown! (Not that I dont love the city, but sometimes I get lazy to drive out there). This place is fairly new, so its ultra clean and shiny inside. The interior of the restaurant is spacious with many areas to sit.
I ordered the vegetarian tofu banh mi, that came with all the fix-ins. The tofu pieces were fried and crispy. I'm not a fan of fried food, but didnt mind it too much in my sandwich. The tofu was plain and bare-naked. Most places I go to, they spike the tofu with spices or lemongrass. I didnt mind it much that the tofu was plain, I simply dashed a bit of hot sauce and soy sauce in my sandwich. I did notice that the essential mayonnaise was missing from my meal. That is what binds a Vietnamese style sandwich! I'll make sure that they put it into my meal next time. I even asked the waiter if the mayo they serve is vegetarian, and he told me that it is. So i'm not sure why they forgot to add it, but it's all good. I also tried the soft rolls with shrimp. The rolls were fresh and soft and came with a hoisin style dipping sauce.
I also loved the fact that I was greeted kindly by the owner. He checked up on me often. The family that owns this cafe are courteous and caring. I'll be back soon enough to get my crispy sandwich fix!

title: Review: Double Trouble Caffeine & Cocktails — 2013-11-10

There's plentiful of seating inside and outside of the cafe. My friend and I sat on the barstools and just hung out
body: Came here on a Saturday morning.. it was quite early at the time. The environment was chill and quiet. Decor was the first thing I noticed upon entering. Its laid back, in a good way. There's plentiful of seating inside and outside of the cafe. My friend and I sat on the barstools and just hung out while my coffee was being made. I ordered a latte which was about four dollars. The price here of the coffee is a bit steep. But its a given, due to the area and the quality of the coffee. The barista put in some coconut cream into my latte, but I could barely taste it. The latte itself was good -- not too hot and not too sweet. The coffee beans weren't overpowering either. The taste of the beverage was smooth and silky. It was a great pick me up at the time and I wasn't left with an after crash feel. I'll probably come back again sometime soon. My school is nearby. The variety of the coffee beverages are few and simple. I appreciated the beautiful latte art that was crafted on my drink. They also have dessert here that's made by a local bakery. Will grab something sweet next time with a steaming latte.

title: Review: Droubi’s Bakery & Deli — 2010-06-06
summary: A bit out of reach, but I still come down to this location time to time. I must say, Droubi`s makes the best darn Chicken Shawerma`s! I`m not saying that 'just cause. body:
A bit out of reach, but I still come down to this location time to time.
I must say, Droubi`s makes the best darn Chicken Shawerma`s! I`m not saying that 'just cause. It must be that I`ve had good experience eating it more than two or three times. The Shawerma is layered with juicy succulent chicken. The yogurt sauce is tangy and garlicky. If you are not into tangy food, then don`t bother with complaining about the food. Most Mediterranean style yogurt is almost always on the sour/tangy side. A long with that factor, the sandwich is stuffed with thin slivers of pickles! How`s that for more sourness? I don`t mind it though, because I love pickles and anything tart. If you are not into that, then just ask for it to be removed.
The other foods that Droubi`s has to offer are good as well. I have enjoyed the Grape Leaves and the Kibbe. A long with that, the dessert`s are also nice. Try the Mamoul. Its basically like a fig newton. But instead its the real deal pastry! Big cookie, buttery, and stuffed with fruit.
The Market section of this place is huge. I always find it wonderful to eat, and then shop for the ingredients of what I just happened to eat! Makes it easier to remember what I had eaten on mind. There are a variety of fresh baked breads just been wrapped, as well as fresh cheeses, olive oils, and spices to purchase. It`s great to be able to find a variety of items.
I have enjoyed my experience at this location. I just wish that the Droubi`s in my city had not been closed down.

body:
I`ve been coming to this boba/tapioca/pearl tea spot for quite sometime. I`ve even received my tenth free drink after finishing up the deal card. Yay! Though, it took me forever to receive that free drink. I wish it was after trying out five drinks. Oh well!
This place is cute. I love the interior and designs. I always get to cozy myself up on their couch, while enjoying my refreshing drink. I`ve pretty much tried all of their juice tea selections. They are all great. From their creamy selection I have tried almond milk tea, Thai tea, as well as the simple but flavourful milk tea. I always get my drinks with the jumbo pearls. Those are the best! This place really knows how to make the pearl chewy, but firm. That is the best consistency in my opinion. I also like how the ice inside the drinks is not overly crushed up. Otherwise that would get in the way of enjoying the pearls.
Do give this cute spot a try! I`m sure you will enjoy it. Those hot day`s are coming up!

title: Review: Dumpling And Noodle House — 2016-03-29
summary: This place is not bad.. Rather its a little hole in the wall spot to visit when in the Vegas Strip. I'm not too fond of fast-food, and Vegas seems to be cluttered with those sort of options. I enjoy piping hot Asian food, and that is what I found in this little Chinese restaurant. It seems a bit lon
body:
This place is not bad.. Rather its a little hole in the wall spot to visit when in the Vegas Strip. I'm not too fond of fast-food, and Vegas seems to be cluttered with those sort of options. I enjoy piping hot Asian food, and that is what I found in this little Chinese restaurant. It seems a bit lonely and run down. But once you enter, you're greeted warmly by the servers. Their werent that many people inside, but it didnt really matter to me. I went ahead and ordered the crispy scallion pancakes, hot milk tea, and pad thai with tofu.
The best item from my order was the scallion pancakes. They were crisp, hot and fresh. It's more of an appetizer item, but scallion pancakes have always been a favorite of mine so I was pleased by their appeal and flavor. I already knew that ordering pad thai at a Chinese restaurant was not the best idea, but luckily it wasnt too bad. The flavor was not authentic, but it still tasted fresh. The tofu was soft and crisp, and the noodles were tender. I would give it 3 stars. The Chinese style hot milk tea did not taste good at all! I would give that beverage a 1 star. I am a big fan of milk tea, but this drink did not deliver the taste that i was craving. They also have tapioca here, but im glad I did not order that. I'm not too sure if it would have been any good.
Anyway, the menu is quite large. I was hoping their would be a vegetarian option for dumplings, but their wasnt. This place doesnt have the best food on the strip, but its not awful either. I would maybe try other items off the menu if I were to visit again. Nothing to write home about. Just hot food without all the junk.

title: Review: Dumplings & Noodles by Cooking Girl — 2025-01-22
summary: I wish I could've liked the food here but it was just okay. We ordered the fried chicken today as an appetizer and it literally came out as crumbs. Almost "bottom of the bag" crumb type. It was like pecking with crumbs with a chopstick, terrible. A bad rendition of Taiwanese style popcorn chicken. T
body:
I wish I could've liked the food here but it was just okay. We ordered the fried chicken today as an appetizer and it literally came out as crumbs. Almost "bottom of the bag" crumb type. It was like pecking with crumbs with a chopstick, terrible. A bad rendition of Taiwanese style popcorn chicken. The lunch portions are decent but the food is just okay as mentioned. I liked the crispy veggie egg roll and the hot and sour soup was filling and warm. These were the items I enjoyed within our lunch hangout. These 2 items are complimentary when you dine in for their lunch menu deal. The beef and broccoli lunch choice was decent. It was fresh and warm, not that salty. Paired well with steamed rice. I appreciated the flavors but I would try something else next time around from their main menu item. I like food on the spicier side and would try one of their pepper based items. I have had their hot diving fish in the past and it's decent, similar to other Cooking Girl locations. But, this location is a little different with the emphasis of "dumplings and noodles"
Steamed beef and onion dumplings are good, I suggest that item if you're looking to dine-in.
I have to admit that I like the food at their other locations better. I have always enjoyed dining in or getting "to-go" from most Cooking Girl locations. But this location is subpar at best. They do have nice and cordial customer service and it's conveniently located within the Houston Galleria area. This part of town doesn't have too many options for this style of cuisine. I hope y'all can improve in some aspects. Their iced milk tea/boba drinks look good. Perhaps I'll revisit and grab an go' a drink and a small item.
Toodles and see ya next time!

title: Review: Dunkin’ — Houston — 2021-11-02
summary: Dunkin donuts serves up some decent hot coffee, always crisp and tasty. Whether hot or cold, the coffee here is a good alternative from Starbucks. body: Dunkin donuts serves up some decent hot coffee, always crisp and tasty. Whether hot or cold, the coffee here is a good alternative from Starbucks. Grabbed an iced coffee today with just half amount of pumpkin spice flavoring. Paired it with a pumpkin spiced cake donut which wasn't bad. But it could have been fresh. It was oily to the touch. Maybe earlier in the morning it would taste different. I don't know. The donuts here are not that fresh which is my biggest gripe. We don't have that many locations of Dunkins here in the city, wish this location was better. The donuts have a bit of an smell to them, and taste a bit artificial. Other than that, this location has a drive thru which is convenient. Service has always been good. Can't complain. Recently I visited a Dunkins location in Alabama and tried their donuts. Flavor and freshness of the donuts were better. Hope they can improve within the state of Texas, otherwise may have to visit Shipley's for better quality products.

I don't think I would ever find the need to go through the drive thru. It's quite small and simple inside the shop which makes getting out much faster. Their is still quite a lot road construction going on in the area. Nonetheless this Dunkin Donuts is parked in a nice part of town. Their is much to see and do after grabbing a sweet little donut from here!

summary: I came in here recently on a Sunday night and it was empty. My older sister wanted to try out their burger here, so she ordered one with a side of french fries. body: I came in here recently on a Sunday night and it was empty. My older sister wanted to try out their burger here, so she ordered one with a side of french fries. I wasn't in the mood to eat a burger at the time, so I decided on the grilled cheese sandwich. My sister sampled the special elevation sauce, but wasn't too pleased with it so she left it out. She said that it tasted like thousand island dressing, and that it wasn't all that great. It didn't take too long for the orders to get through. I took a bite of my sisters burger and I thought it was okay. The burger was a bit flat and small, especially given the price of it. My grilled cheese sandwich was just okay as well. The buns had a sweet taste to them, which wasn't really my thing. The french fries were decent though. This may be a nice place to drop by if you're into burgers and french fries. I'm not, so I probably wont be back for awhile. Nice concept though.. good quality beef is a must when creating burgers, so that's a plus.

title: Review: Epicure Café — 2015-06-02
summary: Epicure is a quaint little gem in the River Oaks neighborhood. I find myself coming here often these days. Upon entering you'll notice paintings all around the cafe. body: Epicure is a quaint little gem in the River Oaks neighborhood. I find myself coming here often these days. Upon entering you'll notice paintings all around the cafe. These are beautiful paintings done by local artists. I believe they are for sale since there is a price tag on each painting. The artwork really pops out the environment here. The display of colorful desserts are eye catching as well. What im most tempted to get here are the cakes. So far I've tried both of the chocolate cakes, pistachio cake, and the apple pie. All of the desserts have their own unique taste. What I like most about the desserts here is that they are not overly sweet. The cafe au lait and the caffe latte are nice to pair with the desserts. I have tried both coffees and they are nice and strong. As far as the tea goes, I definitely recommend the lemongrass tea. It has a refreshing taste. I wouldn't recommend the hot chocolate though. It was pretty mediocre and tasted like Swiss Miss. The prices are a bit steep here. One slice of cake and a hot chocolate cost $8.92. I cant say much about the savory food, but there are a variety of items on the menu. Think of sandwiches, soups and omelettes. The food sounds good, but i'm always tempted by the sweets. Overall, Epicure Bakery is a charming little place to visit if you're in the area.

title: Review: Fadi’s Mediterranean Grill — 2011-10-24
summary: Fadi`s dishes up some incredible and flavorful Levantine cuisine. The food here is fresh and warm. Every item has its own distinct taste, and just about every dish here is amazing! I came in here yesterday and had the urge to plop as many side dishes on my plate. Let me tell ya, each and every item
body: Fadi`s dishes up some incredible and flavorful Levantine cuisine. The food here is fresh and warm. Every item has its own distinct taste, and just about every dish here is amazing! I came in here yesterday and had the urge to plop as many side dishes on my plate. Let me tell ya, each and every item was wonderfully delicious! Don't be afraid in trying something new. The cuisine here is simple and friendly. The warm pita bread's churning out of the oven are soft and chewy. The breads compliment the food well, so make sure to grab some bread with your meal. I was eyeing the desserts that were close to the cash register. I haven't tried the sweet items yet, but will definitely do so in my next return. Overall, I had a great experience at Fadi's, and will be dropping by soon again. I heard that this is the original location, and serves up the best food. I do know that a location in Sugar land is on its way, and I hope the concept and taste will be the same!

title: Review: Fanoosh – Burgers & Biryani — 2018-03-21
summary: I don't see the hype. I happened to be in the area so I dropped by and ordered two chicken biryani's to-go. The menu selection that's offered here is quite minimal. Not that many choices. You have the option to choose between biryani or burgers. I'm not much of a burger person so I ordered the 'whol
body:
I don't see the hype.
I happened to be in the area so I dropped by and ordered two chicken biryani's to-go. The menu selection that's offered here is quite minimal. Not that many choices. You have the option to choose between biryani or burgers. I'm not much of a burger person so I ordered the 'whole chicken bone-in biryani'. The vegetarian biryani didnt seem appealing and I love vegetarian food. Chicken seemed to be the right choice. But I was wrong.
So let me just say that I have high standards in judging any kind of biryani. I have great access to some of the best biryani through my aunty and mother. So its an item that I normally don't order at restaurants. Fanoosh so to speak specializes in biryani.. but it was a complete let down. The chicken biryani was bitter, dark and the chicken was completely dry. I had a tough time cutting through the poor dry chicken. Biryani is a speciality item within Pakistani/Indian cuisine that is known for its fragrance, color and flavor. The biryani here was lacking any of these qualities. It didn't hit the mark and tasted like a simple chicken curry that was baked with rice. I don't even know if the cooks behind the counter are aware of this. The flavor was under salted and it wasnt spicy. I'm not sure what a few of the reviewers mentioned in terms of spicy food. It was probably their first time trying biryani. What can they say? The raita was strangely sweet. When is raita ever sweet? Granted, i've tried tangy raita through the addition of buttermilk. But this raita only made the basic meal worse.
I wouldn't mind giving this place a second chance and trying their burgers. But then again, I saw a picture that made me feel sick. A beef burger that was completely raw in the middle. A reviewer mentioned how he was sick in the gut afterwards. No bueno. Guys.. get it together and work on your biryani and burgers.

body:
Brillante!
Fellini Caffe offers various authentic Italian style pastries, beverages, and savoury items. I absolutely adore the layout of this cafe as well as the ambiance it portrays. I came here with my friend about a month ago -- overdue yelp review!
The lady who I met was kind and showed me around. She gave me a detailed tour around the pastries which I was quite fond of. I was pleased to find out that the pastries are made by an Italian Chef. Given the aesthetic appeal of the desserts I could easily believe that. My friend and I ordered various pastries, savory items and the creme espresso. I enjoyed the creamy espresso, but it was too sweet for my liking. Other than that, I appreciate how there are several coffee items on the menu. Many of them are unique and sound exquisite since they are of an Italian profile. Same goes for the desserts, which I enjoyed every bit of. This cafe is truly a work of art and a gem that's located in Rice Village. I am looking forward to trying out more items the next time I come around.

body: Small selection of seafood items. I came in here for dinner with my family. Everyone ordered something different, but they enjoyed their meals. My mother chose the blackened tilapia fish sandwich and my sister opted for the fish and chips. Both of their items were decent and cooked fresh. The french fries were nice and crispy and so was the fish. I'm not into fried food, but the fish and chips were made well. I had ordered the jumbo lump crab cake sandwich which was quite big. It came with a side of french fries as well. The crab cake sandwich was decent. It was a bit salty for my liking, but I noticed that most seafood dishes at restaurants can be salty. The dish was heavy and kept me quite full as well. Other than that, I still enjoyed my meal. Fish City Grill is a good place to checkout if you feel like grubbin on some heavy duty seafood. For dessert, the bread pudding is sweetly decadent and warm. I doused the dessert down with hot cup of community coffee. It all paired well to end the cold winter night.

body:
Portions have drastically decreased at this restaurant... I ordered the mother earth bowl and only had 2 pieces of sweet potato in the bowl. I remember eating this specific item a few years ago and having more volume in the meal. They used to add more avocado and sweet potato.
Today, all I had was a measly 1 sliver of avocado and 2 chunks of sweet potato. How does anyone get full from that? Especially when it's a vegan meal to begin with... What happened flower child?
This restaurant was absurdly busy today, I'm assuming they're cutting corners and just not providing great meals as they used to. Everyone else enjoyed their food today; but they all agreed that it was just an 'okay' experience. Flower child should consider opening up more locations. Maybe that could help.. I don't know. All I can say is that meals should be provided with ample substance and not appear lackluster. Overpriced and it's mostly a self-serving restaurant. Fetch your own drinks and cutlery. Totally left feeling hungry.

summary: Such a lovely little gem of a bakery tucked in a nice little neighborhood! I happened to be walking in the area and the shoppe simply caught my attention. body: Such a lovely little gem of a bakery tucked in a nice little neighborhood! I happened to be walking in the area and the shoppe simply caught my attention. The outside of the cafe is painted with a beautiful mural of cake and all things cute. Selling pretty flower's in a bakery? It's not anything new.. its so "European-ish!" I've always dreamed of opening a cafe with such a concept as my own. Seeing this concept in reality was lovely. Who wouldn't want to buy a bouquet of flowers to go along with a cake? It was a delight entering the cafe and noticing the pretty little cakes and pastries. The breakfast and lunch menu were intriguing, and I decided to settle for a savory crepe. To my surprise, it was amazingly delicious and one of the best crepes I ever had. The crepe was slightly sweet and salty, consisting of roasted vegetables and cheese. It was a flavorful vegetarian crepe that wasn't missing any meat. The meal itself was quite filling and my belly was delighted. I paired my meal along with a caffe latte, which in all honesty, wasn't the best that I've had. They also have morning buns, which had run out by afternoon. Haven't explored the pastries in depth but will try them next time around! I hope Flower Flour continues to do well.. they display a lovely presence in a quiet neighborhood. Go try them out for yourself!

body:
I recently tried out Freebirds for the first time and I enjoyed my experience. Upon entering, I noticed how colorful the restaurant was. The environment and interior decoration give off a hippyish vibe. The colors of the walls are bold and saturated. It gives this place a warm feeling. This joint is also spunky and full of character. Now as for the food, there are plenty of more options here then at your other typical burrito joint. You have the options of having a burrito, quesadilla, taco's, burrito bowl, and nachos. I love the fact that you have the option of choosing which size of a burrito you want. There are also more choices on which tortilla flavor you prefer. I opted for the vegetarian burrito and I chose the smallest size on the burrito chart. My meal was so filling that I couldn't even finish it. Overall, the flavour and freshness of my burrito were spot on. I enjoyed the different textures and flavours within the burrito. I do wish there were more salsa options in the front and maybe more veggies that could be added into the vegetarian option. A spicier and smokier salsa could be incorporated for those people who like a zesty kick to their food.
Freebirds is settled within my neighborhood and it happens to be in a convenient location. I do see myself coming back again soon. Its definitely a place where you can bring friends and kickback with some tasty casual food. I also like the music they play here. It blends well with the seventies vibe that they capture here. Oh, and another thing... the management and customer service is great! Ernie is a sweet manager who takes proper care of this location. His staff of young employees are friendly and active. I noticed that several of the employees came up to my table and checked up on my family and I. Awesome customer service is a great addition when dining out and I experienced it here at Freebirds.

body: Tried out Fresh Boba this evening.. It's a small bubble tea shop located in the Kroger's shopping center near Kempner HS. It wasn't too busy when I stepped in. Their are many "cream tea's" to choose off the menu. Had a feeling that the cream tea's were made with the powdered stuff, so I changed my mind. I'd much rather visit a bubble tea shop that has milk as an option as opposed to the non-dairy powdered stuff. Anyhow, I changed my mind and ordered the grapefruit green tea with tapioca. Their are many flavored tea's to choose from, but I was in the mood for a citrusy flavor. Not that its any healthier, but at least it didn't have any powder in it. My order was made super quick. The drink was chilly, crisp and very sweet. I would have liked less crushed ice as they mixed into the tapioca pearls. The pearls themselves were nice and chewy but much sweeter in taste than other places. I used to be really big on these types of drinks when I was younger so it was definitely a hit of nostalgia for me. They also have stamp cards per each visit if you're into that type of thing. Overall, my drink was decent and if in the neighborhood i'll be back to try the other juice tea flavors.

summary: What the pho? This place wasn't too good. A friend and I dined here on a chilly Sunday night. It was freezing so we decided upon something warm after having coffee at Fioza. We had no plans on having dinner out.. but got hungry after having a nice chat at the nearby cafe. Came here upon convenience
body:
What the pho?
This place wasn't too good. A friend and I dined here on a chilly Sunday night. It was freezing so we decided upon something warm after having coffee at Fioza.
We had no plans on having dinner out.. but got hungry after having a nice chat at the nearby cafe. Came here upon convenience and it was quiet and empty inside. It's supposed to be a Vietnamese cafe.. yet we didn't see any Vietnamese chefs nor customers inside. I mean.. this gave away an unauthentic feel. My friend and I ordered the "skinny pho", which means you get a smaller bowl.
By "skinny" they meant "skimpy".. we barely had any meat in our pho. My friend got up and paid an extra two dollars to have more meat in our soup. They used grilled chicken in my pho ga, which gave a dry feel and texture. This is the kind of chicken you'd have in the vermicelli bowl.. not the pho! The broth was lacking in the typical soothing and deep flavors you'd find in pho. The notes of Vietnamese cinnamon and star anise were lacking. We mostly tasted garlic in our broth. Adding condiments and peppers only masked away the flavor that we tried to get from our meal. The fried crab wontons were nice and crisp. They were better than our main meals. A few customers dropped by to pick-up their to-go orders. The staff started cleaning midway our meal. We finished our meal promptly and left.
This place caters to the bland palette. I doubt I'll be dropping by anytime soon. We have a great selection of Vietnamese cafes in Houston and this one in particular isn't one of them.

body:
I had no idea that this place has been around for a few months now.. I recently checked out Fruit Frenzy a week ago and thought the place had just opened. Guess I never noticed it before..
Luckily my sister and I stopped by in the afternoon when the place wasn't busy. There was only a small group of students studying at the time. We didnt encounter any slow service. The manager was kind and friendly with us. I ordered the almond milk tea with tapioca, and my sister ordered the original milk tea. Both drinks tasted good in their own way. The tapioca pearls were nice and firm with a chewy texture. Its hard to come across a cafe that concocts a good tapioca drink.
This place definitely has what you're looking for. They serve up a variety of different beverages here. They also have a few desserts that i'm interested in trying when I visit again. Fruit Frenzy is a nice and colorful spot to hangout with friends. I also love the fact that they have happy hour throughout the weekday from 10 - 4 p.m. Basically if you purchase two drinks, you get the third one for free. Thats literally a sweet deal.

I`ve been wanting to check out this self serve fro ~ yo spot for quite sometime! I love the area that it`s situated in. The location of this place is considered the Asian district of Sugar Land. All around are Asian cafes, and noodle shops.
Anyways, on with the yogurt..
I found this place to be much better than Swirll, which is located in Sugar Land town center. The yogurt has a better consistency, as well as flavour. I went for raspberry pomegranate, as well as mango. They also have creamy flavours, such as cake batter, and red velvet. I wanted to go for something fruity, as well as tart. The cashier lady had an attitude, and was quiet refrained. She only gave me one teeny ~ tiny sample cup. Can you believe this? What if I really did not know what to choose? Thankfully, I had a $1 off coupon for this place, which I clipped out from a Sugar Land Magazine. That made me feel much better. You`re able to choose how much yogurt, as well as toppings you want. I chose mochi, mango, sliced almonds, raspberry and blackberries. I very much enjoyed my selection. If you`re looking for a refreshing treat to please your palette, I suggest you check this place out. Though, hopefully, you`ll be treated with better service.

body:
I came here on opening week, and was quite pleased to notice they had itty bitty cupcakes for samples. I sampled the milk chocolate cupcake which had crunchy white pearls on top. The pearls added a nice crispy texture and the frosting was thick and creamy.
My sister ordered the Princess Cupcake, which is a strawberry cupcake with cream cheese frosting. The cupcake was good, and the strawberry flavour was nice. My only problem was that the cream cheese frosting became a tad too sweet after eating a few bites.
Overall the cupcakes here are nicely displayed, and there is a variety of flavours to choose from. They are overwhelmingly topped with so much frosting, they resemble icecream on cones! If you are the type of person who enjoys an extra shot of frosting, than this is the spot for you. As someone who is into lightly sweet desserts, I thought the cupcakes were too sweet for my liking. Its definitely a spot that kids will enjoy, I will most likely bring my little cousins here.

body: Golden Dumpling House seems to serve up some rather mean, or should I say, cute and authentic dumplings. They are quite doughy and chewy; yet filled to the brim. Upon tucking into the dumplings you'll find a rather large sized meatball brimming with flavor. The texture of the dumplings are rather old world and are super boiling hot when you nosh on them. Fresh at it's best. Judging by the reviews this spot seems to have gotten better over time. It's too bad that dine in is closed for now. But when it comes to dumplings, to-go orders are quick and reliable. My favorite are the steamed chicken dumplings as well as the pan fried beef dumplings. They are sealed in with flavor and the texture is great as well. The chili sauce has way too much oil and less spice. The black dumpling sauce (vinegar) is good though. I wish they had a plain shrimp and chive dumpling, as not everyone eats pork. Seafood dumplings would be a great addition to this spot. Other than that, the scallion pancakes are crispy and house made as well. Better than the flat and chewy ones you'll find at any freezer section of a market. Place your order ahead of time as it takes time to prepare the dumplings. Approximately 20-25 mins. Make sure to order by 7:30 pm the latest if you're arriving at evening. Other than that, the service was chill and prompt. Cash only. They have many other items on their menu besides dumplings. Will definitely revisit and try a few other goodies. Until then, continue supporting local mom and pop shops! These folks put soul into their craft.

body: This is such a neat little mom and pop game store that is tucked in a quiet and cozy little part of town. This is a fun little store where you can really be yourself and tap into your imagination. Dressing up in costumes is allowed and you can play the role of any character that comes to mind. summary: I have passed by Got Banh Mi & Pho many of times. I finally made a trip to eat there before heading to work.
