body: I have passed by Got Banh Mi & Pho many of times. I finally made a trip to eat there before heading to work. I had a feeling that this little spot on Westheimer would be tasty and authentic.. Well guess what? It totally was! The Vietnamese food here is fresh and flavorful. I have only tried one item so far.. but that ensures me that the other dishes are probably just as good. I'm a big fan of vermicelli bowls. They are light, crispy and fresh. Nothing greasy whatsoever about it. So that is what I had here for lunch. I placed an order on the tofu vermicelli bowl. It didn't take long for them to cook it up - and it came piping hot to my table. The waiter was kind and friendly.. she checked up on me a few times. I appreciated her service. Anyways, back to the food... my tofu bowl was crispy, savory, garlicky and full of flavour. Most Vietnamese joints do not cook their tofu the way this place does. It was out of this world good. I felt like I was eating chicken, in which case i'm sure their chicken and beef dishes are tasty as well. The portion of the rice noodles was not as large as other Viet places, but the savory tofu made up for it. Their were large slices of vegetables stir fried with the tofu, consisting of celery and carrot. I would have liked more fresh herbs on top of my meal as well. But all in all, I really enjoyed this dish. I'm looking forward to coming back and trying other items on the menu, such as the soft tofu rolls and seafood items. The cafe su da frappacino looks nice as well. Places such as this really define the diversity of the Houston culture. Until next time!

title: Review: Grady Park — 2025-03-15
summary: This is a chill, quiet and clean park within the inner loop/galleria area. An urban park situated on Yorktown Drive. A bit of a green nature escape among the concrete plazas of inner loop Houston. Decent walking trail, kids play area and tennis court. I have mixed feelings about this park at evening
body: This is a chill, quiet and clean park within the inner loop/galleria area. An urban park situated on Yorktown Drive. A bit of a green nature escape among the concrete plazas of inner loop Houston. Decent walking trail, kids play area and tennis court. I have mixed feelings about this park at evening though and it's rather dark at evening. Barely any lights at that time. Be cautious at your own risk and visit the park during daylight hours. It's non discrete and far from pretentious. A good place to get in fresh air and a few laps around the trail. The play area for kids isn't that big, but it's fun enough with various trinkets and slides. The swings for the kiddos and babies are available as well. Lots of joy and a spot to take photos. Grady Park is chill, I've taken the bebe here and we've captured some fun moments of his first experience on the swings and slides. Be careful with your possessions while visiting any park and as I mentioned, visit during daylight hours. Toodles!

summary: Beautiful market studded with lively handmade art, global food, and enthusiastic vendors. Greenwich Market is truly a hole in the wall kind of market. body: Beautiful market studded with lively handmade art, global food, and enthusiastic vendors. Greenwich Market is truly a hole in the wall kind of market. Its nestled inside a passageway in between buildings and its very unassuming. I had a wonderful time visiting this market on the weekend. It just so happened to be a weekend and the market was bustling with all kinds of people. I went on a Saturday afternoon and ended up revisiting on Sunday as well. All of the local artists are incredibly friendly and charming. I tried many samples of local foods and ended up consuming a few snacks and hot coffee. I highly recommend the Jamaican ginger cake -- it's fantastic! The young vendors behind the stand were very friendly and talkative. We chatted for a bit and I decided on the ginger cake after taking a sample. The market has a great selection of desserts, fresh fruit juice, coffee, vegan and non vegan items. You will find many food trucks parked in the open area of the market as well. There are many displays of local art that you can purchase. Inside the market, you will find many galleries showcasing paintings, pottery, and botanical art. This is the place to visit when purchasing or deciding on gifts for loved ones. There are a few coffee houses located right outside the market as well. Red Door, Peyton & Byrne, etc. I definitely recommend visiting any of these cafes while browsing throughout London on a chilly day. Visit this market - you'll be in for a treat in a multitude of ways.

title: Review: Guru Burgers & Bowls — 2012-09-23

Its a savoury crepe which consists of minced salmon and shredded crab. I was a bit unsure how seafood would taste in a crepe, but I wen
body:
Awesome fusion cuisine done right. Ive been to Guru's twice so far and have enjoyed my dining experience. The first time I came in here, I ordered the shaggy crepe. Its a savoury crepe which consists of minced salmon and shredded crab. I was a bit unsure how seafood would taste in a crepe, but I went ahead and ordered it anyways. I'm never afraid in trying out new food concoctions. Overall, I was satisfied with my decision, because the crepe was amazing. I loved the exotic taste of my meal and how the seafood blended well with the flavours. An organic bed of salad was also included with the crepe which had a light and crispy taste. I enjoyed the salad greens which were also included with a grilled lemon. The taste of this lemon was juicy and flavourful. The sriracha sauce that was drizzled on top of the crepe gave it a nice and spicy kick.
The second time I came in here, I ordered the salmon burger. Another great decision! The flavour of the salmon burger was delicious. The meal was freshly prepared which consisted of a citrus aioli and paired with guacamole on the side. I was curious about trying the yucca fries on the menu, so I went ahead and ordered them. The fries were pleasantly tasty and filling. The yucca fries are different than your ordinary russet potato fries. They are more starchy and fibrous. The fries came with a roasted red and green bell pepper relish, which was light and smoky. Overall, I have had good experiences here at Guru's Burger and Crepes. I will definitely come back to try new dishes and experience their sweet items on the menu. The mascarpone crepe is calling to me and im excited to try it in the near future!
PS - You should support this joint because they believe in serving their customers healthy, local, organic, and gluten free foods. Those options are always a plus!

body: Wow such stellar street cart food! The owners are originally from New York and that says it all. I remember bumping into similar bright yellow street cart food vendors in New York. The truck also features fresh juices. I suddenly felt as if I was transported back to the Big Apple. The cravings for chicken and rice with white sauce were accomplished at Gyro King! I'm waiting until the madness dies down at the new "Halal Guys" in Houston. But until then, this little joint is pretty good and they deliver some solid tasting food. It's all in the experience as well. Their are a few tables conveniently situated behind the food cart in which I sat and patiently waited for my hot food. When said food was delivered I opened the container and it was brimming with chicken and lamb (mix combo). The rice was killer! Perfectly cooked with an al dente texture. The cumin spiced rice was steaming and perfectly complimented the juicy meat. My favorite was the chicken among the two. The gyro meat was a bit salty for my liking. The white sauce was creamy and loaded with flavour. The crisp bite from the lettuce and cucumbers complimented the entire meal as well. I ate my heart out - and I usually can never finish my food! My mum ordered the fish over rice. It was also enjoyable and I liked how the fish wasn't salty and overly seasoned. This cart is NOT located in a sketchy area. It's situated at a Chevron gas station near the medical center. If you're still terrified of visiting a hole in the wall then just visit this place in the afternoon. I enjoyed my lunch here and happily ate it at the table behind the truck. It's located in the midst of a neighborhood and not anywhere random and empty. The owners were warm and welcoming. I'm looking forward to coming back to this place and continuing my ventures supporting local businesses.

title: Review: Harvest Organic Grille — 2013-07-26
summary: Organic, vegetarian, vegan, raw and gluten free options? Awesome. Harvest Grille has a brilliant concept that is relevant to what the Houston crowd is looking for these days. When it comes to dining out, a restaurant that is able to appeal any type of diner/eater is a major plus for me. Some people
body:
Organic, vegetarian, vegan, raw and gluten free options? Awesome.
Harvest Grille has a brilliant concept that is relevant to what the Houston crowd is looking for these days. When it comes to dining out, a restaurant that is able to appeal any type of diner/eater is a major plus for me. Some people have food restrictions or are intolerant to certain food ingredients. At Harvest, you'll be able to find a meal that is suitable for just about anyone. The interior environment of the restaurant is warm and rustic. It would be equally lovely to dine in here during winter and enjoy a nourishing meal. There are several Mediterranean food items that are unique and flavourful. I have tried the Red Lentil veggie patties that consist of red lentils and bulgur (cracked wheat). It is a dish that is hearty and plentiful. There is an extensive juice menu that is worth looking over. I tried this green detox juice which was quite refreshing. I could feel the vitamins seeping through my body. If you're looking for which soup to eat before your entree, I recommend the Artichoke soup. It is creamy and has a subtle yet comforting taste. For the appetizer, I tried the stuffed mushroom, which had a mashed potato topping, spinach, and cheese on top. It is quite filling as mushroom tends to have a dense flavour. As my main entree, I had the sock-eye Salmon with a side of Broccolini. I thought the Salmon was just okay. It was a bit dry for my liking -- and had a tough appeal when I ate it. I had to chew quite thoroughly when eating the Salmon. The flavour of the Salmon was very plain as well. There was a lemon butter sauce that came on the side, which I poured over the Salmon. The sauce helped somewhat to give the Salmon a bit more flavour. The Broccolini were plainly steamed and had no flavour to them as well. I didnt mind too much about my main entree. I know the dish was meant for its simplicity, so it didnt bother me too much. For dessert, I tried the vegan cake, which mostly consisted of nuts, some agave nectar, and a fruit sauce. It was different -- but I liked it. A vegan cake such as that is worth trying, especially if you've never tried a vegan dessert, and are curious about it. I doused my meal with some relaxing chamomile tea. All in all, I enjoyed my time spent at Harvest Grill. I'm looking forward to trying out the other dishes as well.

body: Haute Pets Mobile Grooming Salon offers some great service! Using their service is the perfect solution for a spoiled and finicky pet that deserves the best care! I used Haute Pets mobile service a couple of months ago. The company is located in the heart of Houston, yet they are accommodating to anyone's demands and can drive out to different parts of town. Not all mobile grooming salons offer to drive out to the burbs'. I live out in Sugar Land, yet they were able to drive out and accommodate my needs. Such is the advantage of a mobile service. My Himalayan cat is truly a home body and will never be seen outdoors. He is a pampered little prince who fears being outside of his bubble. Often times I would take him to the local vet and he would give me a hard time in the car. He would be scared and shaky after his grooming service, where many dogs and loud machines would reside. As far as the grooming service goes for cats - they are excellent. My cat was trimmed, shaven, nails cut and ears cleaned, etc.(basically the usual grooming package). They took their time on offering their service and made sure my cat was clean, fresh, and well groomed. They have a state of the art service and the best tools used in their grooming mobile. My sweet kitty was happy once he was back home and he looked great. Overall, they offer service to both dogs and cats, but my review was solely for my cat. Haute Pets is pricey $$, but they offer reliable and convenient service in your own neighborhood. Best of all, your pet is comfortable and taken in with love and care. I definitely recommend their service, check them out!

You can't miss it if you're shopping and browsing within the area. Try it for yourself if you have a sweet tooth. Here's hoping you have a sweeter experience.

body: Hippo Ice has been opened for a little over a year. Tucked away in a quiet neighborhood in Sugar Land. I finally made my way over there just a few days ago. I cant compare Hippo Ice to any other place because it was my first time trying shaved ice. I love the concept! At first, I literally thought the product would be plain shaved ice. But I was wrong. The kind young lady at the register explained everything to me. The ice actually has flavor and pieces of fruit in it as well. I opted for the coconut ice with strawberries and watermelon chunks. For the sauce, I opted for the mango puree. The combination of the flavors went well together. The coconut ice literally tasted like fluffy snowflakes. Very creamy, delicate, and with a unique texture. A nice change from ice-cream and frozen yogurt. I definitely see myself coming back and trying their other flavors as well. This place closes late which a nice addition from all of the other spots that close early in the 'burb's.

summary: Nam Nam Nam! This is true Hong Kong style food (mind you, HK style food is nothing like Chinese food, it has its own twist and flair). This is a good restaurant to try out when wanting something different than typical Oriental fare. I enjoy visiting HOB on a quiet weekend night when theirs not much
body: Nam Nam Nam! This is true Hong Kong style food (mind you, HK style food is nothing like Chinese food, it has its own twist and flair). This is a good restaurant to try out when wanting something different than typical Oriental fare. I enjoy visiting HOB on a quiet weekend night when theirs not much happening... I have tried a few of the noodle dishes: Shrimp Chow Fun (wide rice noodles tossed with shrimp and egg sauce) & Singaporean noodles (thin vermicelli noodles cooked with curry spices and vegetables). The rice dish such as the curry shrimp fried rice is delicious. Unique and fragrant, unlike regular fried rice. The shrimp chow fun is creamy with a silky egg sauce and tenderly wrapped with soft flat rice noodles. The Singaporean noodles are great here - not too salty but has a good curry taste. I actually get nice and full when eating the grub here. Their are no msg like symptoms after eating here, atleast I havent experienced it. Lastly, ordering the hot milk tea is a must here! Its nice and strong with a good tea taste. Pair it with the HK style french toast and you're set to end your meal! The french toast is eggy, soft and creamy at the same time. You'll get loads of butter and condensed milk in between your bite - but its all goood! Try it if you're a fan of french toast but want something a bit unique. I've been here twice so far and have been pleased with good service and hot fresh food. Big portions of food with a low price. The menu is quite large and can be overwhelming. I'll definitely be visiting soon again and trying other items that I have experienced yet. I'd say HOB is a casual spot when looking into having a relaxed meal with family or friends. Until next time!

Some of my friends went on the rides. The carnival area was very loud. So much noise emitting from each ride. The main thing is that my friends enjoyed and that I was in good company. I did like the boutiques and shopping display inside the nrg center. Would I ever go back again? Most likely not. But it was something out of the ordinary and made for good times with friends. It was a unique cultural experience. I suggest visiting the Rodeo early during the weekday.. due to the parking issues. Unless theres a specific concert/event that you want to attend.

body: Juicy, delish and fresh burgers. Ordered a regular cheeseburger and was quite delighted with my meal. body:
HTeaO on the go!
This cool little spot has a large variety of chilled teas. Simple & classic Southern style teas ranging from fruit flavors, as well as plain dark and deep black tea flavors (sweet regular). I'm a huge fan of iced tea; it doesn't need to be doused in milk or sweeteners. At this spot, you're able to mix up tea flavors & customize it just as you'd like. It's a little playground full of flavors to mix & choose from. They even have a bevvie named Ryan Palmer which is pink lemonade mixed with their sweet regular.
"The chain uses double-pass reverse osmosis water as a canvas for 24 flavors of sweet and unsweetened tea, as well as pink lemonade and a "Ryan Palmer," an iced tea and lemonade mix named for a professional golfer from Amarillo." (Via Star-Telegram.com)
My favorite was the black tea with mint. It's crisp, refreshing and sweet. They have an unsweetened version as well which I was able to mix with their original sweet mint tea flavor. Choose the cup size you want and fill it up with some pebbled ice. I do believe most of their teas are made up of clean ingredients. At least I know this about their black tea with mint, because I saw the ingredients at the front register. They sell their teas in dry form as well, if you'd like to brew it at home yourself. All in all, the tea flavors are quite aromatic and juicy. They even have fruit cups for a small price if you'd like to mix fruit into your tea. The shoppe has cute looking gear such as baseball caps and tea shirts as well. See what I did there? Lol. I'll definitely be back and revisit to get another iced bevvie, warmer days are coming up anyway. PS - they have a drive thru as well. Grab an iced beverage & head towards Oyster creek park for a walk. You'll thank me later.

body: The Imperial Farmers Market is literally in my neighborhood - yet I hadn't visited the market in a couple of years. I finally made the visit last weekend and was impressed as to how much its grown since my last visit when they had first started. Their are now several vendors selling baked goods, pastries, fragrances, soaps, tea, coffee and fresh fruits/vegetables. The prices of the products aren't too bad either. I was able to purchase a large blueberry pie made with natural ingredients only for 10 dollars. I absolutely enjoyed the pie, as it is a product that is difficult to find here (made with fresh tasting blueberries). I also enjoyed my iced coffee made right in front of me by Fort Bend Coffee roasters. They have some great coffee beans. It was a hot early afternoon and rather a nice way to cool myself down. The Imperial Market also boasts some local and handmade jewelry. There are a few foodtrucks as well. All in all, i'm looking forward to visiting again and picking up new products each time I visit! Support your local farmers and purchase seasonal items!

summary: This is such a great location of In and Out. Fast service and friendly folks just waiting to take your order. Menu is quite simple and easy. body:
This is such a great location of In and Out.
Fast service and friendly folks just waiting to take your order. Menu is quite simple and easy. Food is always fresh and stellar at this location. Warm and full of flavor, considering how simple the ingredients are. I typically just get their classic hamburger, with one beef patty and no cheese. I'll ask for grilled onions and peppers as well. The chopped peppers are great and definitely enhance the experience of this burger. When asking for fries, I'll usually request them extra crispy so they'll have that golden flavor and crunch. Otherwise, their default fries are pale and chewy in texture. Let's face it; most people know this spot is better with their burgers and not so much their fries. Which is probably why their animal style fries are so popular, in order to mask up the flavor. Shakes are good here as well, cold and creamy. I don't typically order those, but you can order them as neapolitan flavor as well. (secret menu)
Can't say much about this classic west coast spot. It's solid and it always delivers the random cravings for a burg. I'm glad we have one here in the Stafford area. It definitely brought a lot of light, color and movement in this part of town. Always busy and always growing. A great spot to grab a late night meal, especially in this cozy season.

body: I've always wanted to try frozen custard -- so I was excited when Inside Scoop finally opened! This place is great and has amazing customer service. The family that owns this business are kind and welcoming people. I was greeted warmly upon entering, and was pleased by the colorful atmosphere. They gave me samples of their three frozen custard flavours right away. They have chocolate, vanilla, and taro for their selection. I liked all three, but opted for the vanilla frozen custard. There are various toppings to choose from as well. I sprinkled my frozen dessert with toasted almonds and strawberries. My experience with the frozen custard was lovely -- it stayed soft and firm at the same time. The dessert didnt melt easily and was creamy and cold. Its nice to be able to choose between the two options. I'm going to try the frozen yogurt on my next trip to Inside Scoop. :)

title: Review: International Wolf Center — 2023-07-07
summary: Such a cool little spot to view wolves in their natural habitat! Service was great and informative upon entering the wolf center. Staff was helpful in regards to the history of the wolves within the area and the pack of wolves that currently live at the center. It was a display they held and staff s
body: Such a cool little spot to view wolves in their natural habitat! Service was great and informative upon entering the wolf center. Staff was helpful in regards to the history of the wolves within the area and the pack of wolves that currently live at the center. It was a display they held and staff showed a few artifacts that were quite helpful in understanding wolves and their current living arrangements. Everyone got to view the current wolves behind a glass wall and saw them in their natural wild sanctuary. It was pretty neat seeing how they interact in their daily life and how they are common to spot in the city of Ely. They even have a museum section with further information and artifacts to learn from, as well as a small cinema to view a video. The video pertains to the lifestyle and the habits of the wolves and gives a general brief history of the wolves being introduced to the area. I love how interactive this spot was, they had plenty of things to see and do. They also have a small gift shop to purchase items from. I can definitely see myself visiting this spot if in the area. Just seeing all the wolves within the city of Ely was neat. It's a great place to visit when venturing through the area up north MN. International Wolf Center is a must if bringing friends or family up north. Into the wild you go!

body: I was thrilled to spot Joe & The Juice recently within my Minneapolis airport excursion whilst running to my gate in time. Hadn't been to a Joe and the Juice cafe in a few years. Throughout my travels in Europe (particularly within Scandinavia) I would frequent this cafe. They had em all over Norway. I do recall visiting a location or two within New York as well a few years back. Needless to say, it had been a while since I had a Joe fix. The menu still looked the same as it does throughout the world and their sandwiches looked decent as well. I did not opt for coffee or food, rather I opted for their iced matcha latte. I know.. this spot is known for their "joe" but they're just as popular for their "juice" hence the name!! & Various other bevvies. Felt the need to cool down so an iced matcha latte did the trick. It was creamy, lightly sweetened and refreshing. Just the right hue of bright green within the cup and I sipped away while on my excursion. The service was just OK though and they seemed super busy. Yeah I know it's the airport but they really weren't fixating on the details. I initially ordered a medium beverage, but they gave me a small one instead. This caught my eye immediately and I told them to remake my drink. They did without any hesitation. I was glad to have my medium sized iced drink as I was sharing it with my favorite person. Mm crisp matcha moments! Something different than Starbucks, thank goodness. This might be their only location in MN? Not sure. It was busy. I'll revisit in the near future. Just glad this airport has a few options besides SB -- what a refreshing change. To the workers that work at this location, please focus on details and keep this place clean and non-disheveled. Bbyes.

title: Review: Jus’ Mac Sugar Land — 2012-06-13
summary: I finally had the chance to try Jus' Mac a few days ago. I have known about this mac and cheese eatery since the original location was developed in the Heights. Fast forward two years, and I am sitting in a location that is tucked away in my neighborhood. It's good to know that this eatery has expan
body:
I finally had the chance to try Jus' Mac a few days ago. I have known about this mac and cheese eatery since the original location was developed in the Heights. Fast forward two years, and I am sitting in a location that is tucked away in my neighborhood. It's good to know that this eatery has expanded and is now in close proximity to me. My friend and I randomly went the other day, and had a nice experience. The interior of the restaurant is cute and casual with an urban feel. I like the simplicity of the restaurant, and how it showcases various concoctions of macaroni and cheese. There are even panini's featured on the menu, which is wonderful, as not everyone is a fan of mac and cheese.
So I tried the popeye mac and cheese, which consisted of a creamy white cheese, tossed with baby spinach, mushrooms, and onions. The order arrived as soon as possible, and the mac and cheese was crisp and golden to perfection. The dish was served in a small cast iron skillet, and the meal was hot and bubbly. As a huge fan of mac and cheese, I happily finished my meal without any guilt. The flavours were perfectly seasoned, and well balanced. I appreciated the fact that my dish was not too salty, as most other restaurants serve a rather salty mac and cheese.
Overall I had a good experience at Jus Mac, and will be back soon again. Its nice to have a unique restaurant in town that showcases an American classic. This place defines that sort of image, and will definitely do well during the fall season, when people are looking for warm food that's nourishing and comforting!

title: Review: Kabob Korner — 2013-12-07

body:
I really should have tried the Pakistani food when I came here.. The cuisine seems to be quite popular among the customers.
I dont live in the area where the cafe resides.. but I wanted to have a nice and filling meal before checking out the mall in that part of town. Upon entering around lunch time.. the restaurant was bustling with people dining in. I couldn't decide what I wanted to order, so I went ahead with the chicken shawarma. My sister ordered the chicken kebab wrap with paratha bread. It took quite some time for our meal to arrive to our table. My chicken shawarma was seasoned with Indo-Pak seasonings. The tahini sauce inside the wrap was thin and watery. Most of it leaked out of the other end of my wrap as I ate it. The french fries that came with my meal were cold. I dont eat french fries that often, so I barely ate them. I was looking forward to a Levantine style Chicken Shawarma.. but that is not what I got. I should have realized this in the beginning, due to the restaurant being of South Asian influence. Other than that.. my meal was still decent. It was healthier than the other options and not spicy. I ordered Pakistani style chai to end my meal.. and it was good. The steaming cup of chai was made with fresh milk. It was simple and not spiked with spices as Indian chai usually is.
If I ever have a chance to come around this spot again, i'll definitely try the hardcore Pakistani dishes such as the Chicken Karahi or the Nihari.
Customer service was great. The young lady at the counter was friendly and helpful. So was the other gentleman. Another great factor was that the restaurant was clean and simple. Nice place to drop by for lunch.

summary: Super soft and fluffy breads! I enjoy the selection here at Kamalan bakery. I came here on a Sunday evening yet there were still a few items available. body: Super soft and fluffy breads! I enjoy the selection here at Kamalan bakery. I came here on a Sunday evening yet there were still a few items available. The hours of the bakery are appreciated.. it doesn't close too early and it makes for a convenient walk-in. Clean and organized as well, in the heart of China town. Kamalan place boasts a variety of baked goods ranging from sweet to savory. There are several types, textures and flavors of breads. My most favorite is the vanilla cupcake. Its not an actual cupcake, rather its a soft vanilla flavored sponge cake in the shape of a large muffin. The crushed almonds on top of the vanilla cupcake make for a nice taste as well. Its super fluffy, airy, and I cant stop eating it! I would pair this with the milk tea at the teabar cafe next door. They have a pandan cupcake as well but the taste of the pandan flavor is too strong and makes for a bitter tasting bread. My second favorite is the raisin milk bread. The raisins are tucked all the way at the bottom of the bread, mixed with some sort of custard. The raisin bread does not have a sponge texture but its still light and airy. The taste of the products ensures that proper ingredients are used. All of the items against the shelves are nicely presented as well. Overall a good place to drop by when you're looking or a baked treat. I'll probably visit again soon on an afternoon day when the bakery carries more selection of items.

body: Unique and vintage coffee shoppe within the EaDo district of Houston. This part of town isn't too far off from the novelty of hanging out, or heading towards downtown htx. I have known about Koffeteria right when they were opening in this part of town. Loved the antique interior - the cupboard, cabinets and little trinkets. The coffee table was dirty though and so was the floor around where we sat. Staff might have gotten busy since they were 30 mins til closing. Ah well. A little hyped. May visit earlier next time around and grab a different bevvie. Have heard quite a lot about their eclectic croissants. I'm not usually in the EaDo district of town, as it's a bit ways out. Definitely an urban exploration, but will certainly revisit when given the chance.

body: Tucked in a cozy corner on Greenway... Kolache Shoppe is a nice option for a quick and warm breakfast experience. They close at 12pm, so get there before then!! This is a nice spot to visit and venture off to your weekend hangouts or errands!

body:
So I had a nice experience here on a busy Saturday night. Went with some friends and surprisingly the line wasn't too long. If anything, the line was quick and efficient. At almost any tapioca joint, my go to order is the iced milk tea with tapioca. Sometimes i'll order hot milk tea, but for the most part, in this hot city - I usually opt for the iced version.
The milk tea with tapioca was made rather quickly! Everyone's order was delivered at the same time. My beverage was crisp, creamy and frothy. The tapioca pearls themselves were perfect - firm, chewy and sweet. The milk tea here is pretty good, it has the light floral scent of jasmine. I opted for the small size and the ice to milk ratio was just fine. The sweetness level was just right for my liking, I didn't have to adjust or anything. I believe the machines they use create a light and frothy beverage. Sure the prices might be a little steep, but I don't drink tapioca beverages as often as I used to. Far too many calories and amount of sugar personally - haha! Although, I definitely know where to head when i'm craving a crisp and sweet milk tea with tapioca. They have a large menu and I may try something new next time around. This is a nice spot to bring friends as their are many tables spread across the cafe, ranging from small tables to large. Can get quite noisy on the weekend though, but that didnt bother us too much. Customer service was just fine and we werent bothered. They were even closing but didnt push us out or anything. Check out this place if you're ever in the area!

Bit of a small spot with few gelato flavors to pick from.. The gelato was just okay... even worse... the alfajores was downright awful. I would stay away from the cookies though and focus on their frozen treats. Here's hoping our next encounter will be a sweeter one.

title: Review: La Baguette French Bakery — 2013-12-07
summary: Came here early on a Saturday, around 10:45 a.m. It was freezing that day and I needed a good filling meal. All the other cafes were closed at the time, so I decided to try out this place. It was my first time here at La Baguette and the environment was a bit off. The cafe was dark lit and the menu
body:
Came here early on a Saturday, around 10:45 a.m. It was freezing that day and I needed a good filling meal. All the other cafes were closed at the time, so I decided to try out this place. It was my first time here at La Baguette and the environment was a bit off. The cafe was dark lit and the menu did not have any prices on it. The old lady in the front didnt know English so she called another lady to take my order. I believe this lady was the manager or cook.. not sure. I decided upon a vegetarian banh mi with tofu. I had been craving a banh mi for sometime, so was hoping for a good meal. As my meal was being prepared, I noticed that there were several desserts in the glass display. The cakes and croissants looked good.. but what was baklava doing there? I'm not saying that a Vietnamese-French inspired cafe shouldn't have baklava, but it was a bit random seeing it. Previous reviewers said that the baklava wasn't good. I'm not surprised. Its a dessert that is quite intricate to make and should be served in the best manner. There were coffee and latte drinks on the menu as well.. but im picky with my coffee so I didnt order any.
Thankfully, the banh mi sandwich was tasty. It wasn't amazing, but it was good. I was charged 3.50 for the sandwich, and luckily it was filling. Although the tofu was fried, it wasn't too greasy. It was soft and tender to eat. There was alot of shredded carrot and cilantro stuffed in the sandwich, but only one strip of cucumber. The amount of mayo in the sandwich was generous and the hoisin sauce made it nice and savory. The French bread was fresh and crispy. The inside of the bread was soft and chewy. It hit the spot.
All in all, I wouldn't mind dropping by again at La Baguette. Maybe for a quick bite to eat. It's nearby by campus, so it makes for a convenient place to grab a meal. But until then, im going to explore a few other places in that part of town.

body: LA Crawfish - not to be confused with Los Angeles, y'all - this is all about Louisiana style grub. The food here is coated with spice and heavy handed with salt and oil. But that's typically the palate of Cajun style/Crawfish cuisine. Mind you, I never nosh on crawfish because that's not my thing. But they have plenty of other food options here. The food isn't bad, it'd give it a solid 3.5. The ingredients seemed fresh and the portions were decent. I liked the bite sized chicken bites that were flash fried with basil. The cajun spiced waffle fries were salty yet warm and crisp. My friend ordered the crawfish and mentioned they were small in size. The season for it just started so perhaps that could change. The cajun style fried rice was spiced up with a lot of seasoning yet salty in taste. The flavor wasn't bad but the sodium levels could have been less. Maybe SaltBae would disagree. Other than that, the dark and savory fried rice paired well with the other food items. All in all, the food was decent and the service was warm. This spot is tucked inside a corner of 99 ranch market. I may revisit when passing through the market. They also have pho if you're craving for something warm and soupy. Did I just say soupy? Yes I did. It's the season for some warm grub.

body:
I'd been wanting to come here for sometime.. and I finally made it happen! Les Givrals is tucked in a cute little corner in midtown. I have been to a few of the cafes right across this restaurant.. but all this time I mainly had my eye on this gem. The quiet cafes that are in the same plaza as Les Givrals are just okay. Meaning the food and the ambiance were not that great.
Les Givrals was quite busy and bustling on a Friday afternoon. I had errands to run, so I made a to-go order of their shrimp fried rice. The decision was a great one. The fried rice was savory, garlicky and aromatic. Probably the best fried rice I've eaten in a long time. The shrimp was generous, steamy and plump. I loved how the dish was garnished with fresh cilantro as well. The order took some time, but I didn't mind the wait. I ordered soft shrimp rolls while my order was being made. The soft shrimp rolls were nice and healthy. Juicy pieces of shrimp and tofu were tightly tucked into the roll and came with a traditional hoisin dipping sauce. Vietnamese food is definitely a favorite. I love how each dish is fresh and has its own appeal. I'm looking forward to trying the banh mi next time i'm here.. as well as the cafe su da (Vietnamese coffee) for a nice pick-me-up. Good service and a clean cafe with many tasty and authentic food options. Will definitely be back soon!

I ordered the shrimp fajitas and they were rubbery and over cooked. The beans and rice that were included were nice and simple. The usual that your would get at most Mexican restaurants. I was more looking forward to an authentic style restaurant. Lopez did not deliver that. Its quite a large restaurant and had plenty of seating. Mostly large groups of folks with their family and friends. It was my first time here, so I was expecting something a bit different.

title: Review: Luce Ave Coffee Roasters — 2018-01-30
summary: Minimal.. clean.. sleek atmosphere. I had the chance to visit Luce Ave Coffee Roasters last month with a friend. This little coffee shop is centrally located within the inner loop and makes for a nice place to hangout. Upon entering, you'll notice how small and narrow the cafe is. There are a few ta
body:
Minimal.. clean.. sleek atmosphere.
I had the chance to visit Luce Ave Coffee Roasters last month with a friend. This little coffee shop is centrally located within the inner loop and makes for a nice place to hangout. Upon entering, you'll notice how small and narrow the cafe is. There are a few tables lined up against the wall. Towards the back, you'll notice some colorful artwork and a coffee roasting machine. Gives the place some unique aesthetics and modern feel. Due to it being the winter holidays, I ordered the peppermint mocha latte. Along with my latte, I picked up the chocolate chip cookie which I think they make in house. They also serve up muffins and a few other pastries. Anyway, the baristas were incredibly friendly and answered all of our questions. They even brought us water to our table once we sat down. The peppermint mocha latte had a murky green color to it.. but nonetheless the flavor was strong yet smooth. We both enjoyed our coffee and the chocolate chip cookie was nice as well. The cookie was very chunky and chocolaty, but it was hard and seemed overbaked. Overall, the atmosphere is light and quiet. I enjoyed my time here at Luce Ave and would definitely revisit and try something new. The earl grey latte seems intriguing and is hard to find at most cafes. I'm a big fan of tea, so its great to see different options available. It's a nice cafe to drop by when in the midst of the inner loop. Until next time!

title: Review: Luna Pizzeria — 2015-08-04
summary: Luna is such a stellar little spot for some satisfactory pizza! When the craving for such food exists.. this is the place to go. I don't eat pizza that often.. but this spot comes to mind first thing when i'm craving a nice cheesy slice. I have only tried two varieties of their pizza - the mushroom
body: Luna is such a stellar little spot for some satisfactory pizza! When the craving for such food exists.. this is the place to go. I don't eat pizza that often.. but this spot comes to mind first thing when i'm craving a nice cheesy slice. I have only tried two varieties of their pizza - the mushroom & the vegetarian and both were simply delicious. What I enjoy most about the pizza here is that it's fresh and not too heavy tasting. The pizza was quite large and they surely did not skimp on the ingredients. I like the location of this place as well. Its in a nice and clean neighborhood with ample parking. Whether you visit for lunch or dinner, you will surely be satisfied with the pizza's here. Overall, Luna is a great little spot to visit with family and friends.

title: Review: M&M Grill — 2012-11-09
summary: All of my family and friends have raved so much about this place! I finally got to try it out. My relatives love this joint, so we all came here last weekend. Its a shabby hole in the wall type of restaurant, with limited seating. The walls are painted red, and it somehow reminds of the Rockets bask
body:
All of my family and friends have raved so much about this place! I finally got to try it out. My relatives love this joint, so we all came here last weekend. Its a shabby hole in the wall type of restaurant, with limited seating. The walls are painted red, and it somehow reminds of the Rockets basketball team. Another reason as to why it reminds me of basketball, is because many of the youngsters were watching basketball when I came in. The restaurant has a simple and casual vibe. The service here is decent, as they prepare the food fresh once you order.
This restaurant has good Mexican food. I ordered the chicken soft taco plate, which had nice and moist dices of chicken tucked inside two flour tortillas. The plate came with a side of creamy beans, and flavourful Mexican rice. My sister tried the enchiladas, which were also good. I liked how the enchiladas weren't overly salty, and had a nice cheesy bite to them. My relatives ordered different burgers, which were also tasty. This place serves Arabic food as well, but I have not tried it, so I cant say anything about it. For my next visit, I will most likely try the Arabic food and see if it's also as good as the Mexican and American food that they offer.
All in all, this place offers good and hearty wholesome food. I'll definitely be back again, perhaps with my friends next time around.

title: Review: Maggie Moo’s Ice Cream & Treatery — 2011-09-23
summary: Colorful and cute! Maggie Moo's has been apart of Sugar land for ages! Its truly a historical spot in the city. I am glad that they have been doing well after all these years. I can remember the days when I used to come here as a child. The flavours of the ice cream are unique and scrumptious. Hones
body:
Colorful and cute! Maggie Moo's has been apart of Sugar land for ages! Its truly a historical spot in the city. I am glad that they have been doing well after all these years. I can remember the days when I used to come here as a child. The flavours of the ice cream are unique and scrumptious. Honestly, I have not been here in a long time, but will make sure to head out there during these long and hot days.
Maggie Moo's is totally kid friendly! I have brought my little cousins here and they have enjoyed their frozen treats. This cutesy ice cream parlour is a family favorite and I would recommend trying it out if you seek something different than the usual ice cream franchises.

title: Review: Magic Cup — 2016-07-07
summary: Super crisp and creamy milk tea! I stopped by today after noticing the new cafe on my drive to the dentist. It was such a hot day and I needed a cold and refreshing drink. My go to drink is always milk tea anywhere I go. Magic Cup serves up some standard milk tea that isn't too watery or too sweet.
body: Super crisp and creamy milk tea! I stopped by today after noticing the new cafe on my drive to the dentist. It was such a hot day and I needed a cold and refreshing drink. My go to drink is always milk tea anywhere I go. Magic Cup serves up some standard milk tea that isn't too watery or too sweet. So it isn't the best I've had, but as I mentioned, its standard, which isn't a bad thing. The drink was nicely sweetened, creamy and not too strong tasting. Shop workers were nice enough to let me try a small sample before deciding. Tapioca is included so I went ahead with it. But personally, I asked for 1/2 boba and 1/2 ice. The drink was a nice pick me up on this sweltering day. The inside of the cafe is clean and spacious. Plenty of chairs and tables to situate yourself upon. The menu is quite large and extensive. Magic Cup has plenty of smoothies and fresh fruit juice options as well. I'll definitely visit again and try something new. The parking is a bit small and strangely situated, but I was able to get decent parking in the afternoon. They've got some snack food options at Magic Cup as well. Always nice to have new cafe choices in the area. Try it and see for yourself! Oh, and good customer service is always appreciated. Thanks guys!

title: Review: Magnol French Baking — 2024-02-12
summary: Incredibly tasty, very buttery and authentically French. Magnol Bakery is a true hole in the wall spot. This spot is located within a discrete and rather industrial part of town. You'll be sure to miss it if speeding past the area. I did not even know this bakery existed until a good friend brought
body:
Incredibly tasty, very buttery and authentically French.
Magnol Bakery is a true hole in the wall spot.
This spot is located within a discrete and rather industrial part of town. You'll be sure to miss it if speeding past the area. I did not even know this bakery existed until a good friend brought up within a conversation. TY for sharing a piece of mini France in Houston, otherwise I would have never known about this place! It's best to arrive early, as baked goods run out quick. To my surprise, many items were disappearing from shelves around 8:45 a.m. Should I have visited even earlier in the morning? Most likely. This place is packed and quite popular.. basically if you're within the know, so you'll know. The pain aux raisins (flaky puffed pastry rolled with raisins and vanilla crème) was an absolute delight.. great crisp and texture. The madeleines (shell shaped butter cakes) were quite nice as well. Their cozy and warm tea lattes as well as coffee was quite fragrant and paired well with the baked treats. This spot isn't too big from the inside so the line was literally wrapped within the interior of the cafe. The interior is light and airy, as opposed to the outside of the building. Tucked within one small shelf.. they have a few food products for purchase that are imported from France.. (ie; fruit jam, honey, etc.) I would love to revisit again.. (even earlier in the morning) and try their various croissants, linzer cookie and cute little cakes. They have a few other caffeinated drink options as well to warm up your day. No better moments than visiting during winter or spring season! Thanks Magnol for brightening up my morning.. i'll be sure to visit again. Until we meet again -- Au Revoir!

title: Review: Mai Colachi — 2015-10-06
summary: Authentic and flavorful Pakistani cuisine served in an elegant manner. The ambiance and environment complement the theme as well. My family and I enjoyed our dinner here at Mai Colachi. I am quite picky with Pakistani cuisine and I normally do not eat it at restaurants.. Because food at such restaur
body: Authentic and flavorful Pakistani cuisine served in an elegant manner. The ambiance and environment complement the theme as well. My family and I enjoyed our dinner here at Mai Colachi. I am quite picky with Pakistani cuisine and I normally do not eat it at restaurants.. Because food at such restaurants tend to create heavy dishes full of oil with just one note of flavor. But the cuisine here was nice, presentable, and tasty. Every dish had its own unique appeal to it. The bread served was fluffy and soft and the passion fruit drink and ice-cream dessert were nice as well. Will definitely be back again with my family. The restaurant is located in a nice and convenient little plaza in Sugar Land. Will be sure to drop by one day when i'm in the mood for spicy and unique food.

title: Review: Maiberry — 2011-09-23
summary: It's refreshing to have Maiberry inside the mall. Literally. I love the fact that they use all natural ingredients in their products as well as pure cane sugar. The yogurt is creamy and has a nice thick consistency. It keeps me full as I stroll around the mall. Its also great to finally see a health
body:
It's refreshing to have Maiberry inside the mall. Literally.
I love the fact that they use all natural ingredients in their products as well as pure cane sugar. The yogurt is creamy and has a nice thick consistency. It keeps me full as I stroll around the mall. Its also great to finally see a healthy option inside the mall. I have been visiting Maiberry for sometime, and was excited to see that they were finally serving up tapioca drinks. I ordered my first tapioca drink and was disappointed. The pearls were overly cooked and too chewy. The drink itself had a nice flavour, they just need to work on their pearls.
Other than that, I have been content with their yogurt. Next time around, I may try out their shaved ice and smoothies. Love this cute and colorful addition to the mall. Its quite eye-catching, you cant miss it!

title: Review: Mama Yu — 2013-08-21
summary: The Indonesian food is tasty over here.. It is flavourful and not too spicy. Every dish has its own unique appeal to it. The family that owns this restaurant are very friendly and welcoming. The only downside is that there are no descriptions or pictures on the menu. So it makes it a bit difficult o
body:
The Indonesian food is tasty over here..
It is flavourful and not too spicy. Every dish has its own unique appeal to it. The family that owns this restaurant are very friendly and welcoming.
The only downside is that there are no descriptions or pictures on the menu. So it makes it a bit difficult on choosing what to order. If you're not familiar with Indonesian food and are not sure what to eat here, you can always ask the staff for suggestions. They are great at giving suggestions and know what will please their customers. I'm quite familiar with Indonesian food, so I didnt have a hard time choosing what I wanted to eat. I ordered the chicken satay that came with a luscious peanut sauce. It was probably the best chicken satay that ive ever ate. It was moist, chewy, and full of flavour. I also ordered the nasi goreng which came with chunks of lamb. It was a stir-fried rice dish that was full of fragrance and spice. Another dish I ordered was the meatball soup which was chock full of spinach and thin rice noodles. It was hearty and nutritious. The last dish was the beef rendang entree that came with a stewed beef dish, steamed rice, egg with chili, and stewed vegetables. I enjoyed the beef rendang, but wished that there was more beef on the plate. Other than that, the beef was fragrant and full of flavour. The vegetables had a similar taste and were good as well. All in all, I enjoyed my meal and my experience at Mama Yu. I'm looking forward to trying their other dishes as well. :) Perhaps the mei goreng (stir fried egg noodles) Think of ramen, but a more exotic version of it.

title: Review: Marble Slab Creamery — 2021-11-30
summary: I had not visited this location in years. This particular location of Marble Slab Creamery is tucked away in the corner of a large shopping plaza. It's in a busy and yet frequently visited part of Stafford. I used to frequent this spot much over a decade ago when it was a Cold Stone Creamery locatio
body: I had not visited this location in years. This particular location of Marble Slab Creamery is tucked away in the corner of a large shopping plaza. It's in a busy and yet frequently visited part of Stafford. I used to frequent this spot much over a decade ago when it was a Cold Stone Creamery location. That place was awesome. This shoppe of MS creamery is just OK. The servers were friendly and let me try a few samples of ice cream. The flavors were just alright though. Many of the flavors were quite artificial in taste. But that's typically a given for a large chain spot such as this. I opted for the coconut flavor because it looked fresh in comparison to the other flavors. Creamy in taste and not that sweet. Mixed in some almonds as well into it. They serve cookies here but they are not that fresh. I picked up a red velvet cookie and it didn't taste good at all. Most of their cookies are just standard and all artificial. You can create a cookie sandwich. They also have large ice cream cakes. Lots of frozen delight's to choose from. Other than that, this spot is better for just a simple flavor of ice cream. You can't go wrong with flavors such as: chocolate, vanilla, or cake batter. Any mixins (toppings) are included with your ice cream. They also have waffle bowls and regular cone waffles. I'm glad this ice cream spot still exists in the neighborhood. The place was clean and the servers were kind. Hope they can continue to serve up decent sweet treats.

title: Review: Marco’s Pizza — 2013-12-10
summary: Pretty decent pizza joint tucked within my neighborhood. The place is literally a few minutes down the street so I decided to have my pizza delivered. There are many good deals on the main website. I chose the 15.99 deal that comes with a specialty pizza of your choice and a side of their cheesy bre
body:
Pretty decent pizza joint tucked within my neighborhood. The place is literally a few minutes down the street so I decided to have my pizza delivered.
There are many good deals on the main website. I chose the 15.99 deal that comes with a specialty pizza of your choice and a side of their cheesy bread. The size of their cheesy bread is about the size of a medium pizza. It comes with a side of both marinara sauce and ranch sauce. As for the pizza, I was craving for something without tomato sauce, so I ordered the specialty white cheesy. I thought it would take some time for the pizza to be made and delivered, but it didnt take that long. The pizza arrived earlier than expected and I quickly devoured a slice. It was hot, cheesy, and delicious. The 4 cheeses on the pizza were nice and creamy. But for my taste, the crust was too chewy and soft. I toasted a slice for my mum in the toaster oven until it got nice and crispy. It looked and tasted much better after that. May ask them to bake the pizza a little longer if I order in the near future. Other than that, their pizzas would come in handy when having a large group of friends or family over.

title: Review: Market Place Antiques & Collectibles — 2021-10-25
summary: Decent and quite a large market place to explore on a random weekend afternoon. I am not an "antiquer" but its nice to visit old spots such as this that take you down memory lane. Albeit many of the items here are way before my time. They have super old grandfather clocks, vases, paintings, etc, fro
body: Decent and quite a large market place to explore on a random weekend afternoon. I am not an "antiquer" but its nice to visit old spots such as this that take you down memory lane. Albeit many of the items here are way before my time. They have super old grandfather clocks, vases, paintings, etc, from eras gone by. It's dusty and eccentric in here as you sprawl through the warehouse. There are a few vendors that have set up their own shops inside the marketplace. Many of them are quite talkative and will try to suggest items that may appeal to you. I haven't bought anything from here yet, but some of the wooden furniture caught my eye. In particular the wooden ottoman tables and dresser cabinets. The vintage tea cup sets are nice as well, most likely post Victorian era. Some of the items are dainty and would make for nice decor around the house. Other than that, many of the items are things that you may not particularly need. It's still nice to appreciate vintage stuff and the delicacy/craft of how they were made. Items were built to last back then. I recommend visiting the shop on a cosy weekend afternoon. They're only open Fri-Sun anyway. Rain or shine most likely.

title: Review: Masala Munchies — 2015-05-16
summary: I love the potato samosa's at Masala Munchies! They are smaller than the samosa's that you'll find in the area - but they pack a punch of flavor. I actually prefer the size of these samosa's in comparison to the larger ones. You can easily eat a samosa or two and not feel overwhelmingly stuffed. The
body:
I love the potato samosa's at Masala Munchies! They are smaller than the samosa's that you'll find in the area - but they pack a punch of flavor. I actually prefer the size of these samosa's in comparison to the larger ones. You can easily eat a samosa or two and not feel overwhelmingly stuffed. The samosa's are filled generously with diced potato, carrots and pea's. The spices are just right as well.
Masala Munchies is quite small and its more of a grab and go type of spot. Upon entering, I noticed many folks waiting around for their orders to be complete. On the menu, they have sandwiches, chaat, and many other snacks. There are a few desserts packaged in the cooler as well. Its a vegetarian friendly spot and for those looking for something new. I'm looking forward to coming back and trying a Bombay style sandwich. Anything full of flavour is worth the hype and Masala Munchies delivers that.

title: Review: Mazajj Organic Coffee — 2024-09-17
summary: Absolutely wonderful interior, lots of indoor lighting as well as natural lighting pouring in through the windows. Great customer service and warm hospitality, thanks guys! This Mazajj is a lot closer within the inner loop of Houston compared to their Katy location. Their Katy shoppe is just as love
body:
Absolutely wonderful interior, lots of indoor lighting as well as natural lighting pouring in through the windows. Great customer service and warm hospitality, thanks guys!
This Mazajj is a lot closer within the inner loop of Houston compared to their Katy location. Their Katy shoppe is just as lovely though, with similar interior deco and piping hot tea.
Choices for teas and beverages are plenty. Want coffee? They've got it. Want tea? They have different styles. My favorite being the Adeni chai. It's not too strong as other spots make it. A bit of a lighter and creamier flavor. I always opt for half sweet and it's perfect. You can get it by the cup or as a teapot. I love their teapot and glassware. Adorable and makes for a cozy morning or evening spent sipping on chai. Warm and exotic music playing in the background makes for such an international vibe. I'm loving how they're situated within the Galleria area. We really needed a spot for authentic chai and Mazajj delivers! They just had their grand opening 2 days ago & already got it down in terms of customer service. Thanks for the complimentary desserts today. So sweet.
Y'all, check out Mazajj and thank me later. Support local and support chai that's made from scratch with true warmth and passion. Try their desserts, viral Dubai chocolate and milk cakes. So good and so worth it. Welcome to the neighborhood!

title: Review: McAlister’s Deli — 2012-03-19
summary: I'm glad McAlister's exists on campus. This is your one stop deli where you can grub on sandwiches, soups and salads. Ive had their vegetarian bean chili, which was decent. Its nice and filling, which gets the job done when you have an empty belly on campus. Ive also had their creamy mac and cheese,
body: I'm glad McAlister's exists on campus. This is your one stop deli where you can grub on sandwiches, soups and salads. Ive had their vegetarian bean chili, which was decent. Its nice and filling, which gets the job done when you have an empty belly on campus. Ive also had their creamy mac and cheese, which was nice and comforting. They also have these huge overstuffed baked potatoes that I want to try next time. McAlisters also has a variety of desserts that I have not tried yet. Their enormous cookies look good, and so does their cheesecake. I think I have my eye on them and will try the sweets next time I visit this deli..

title: Review: Menchie’s Frozen Yogurt — 2012-09-12
summary: Wow. This yogurt cafe is not worth the hype. I came in here recently as I was excited in trying out a new frozen yogurt spot in town. Upon entering, I noticed the odd layout of the cafe. This place is a self serve cafe in which you create your own mix-ins, however you want. The yogurt bar was right
body:
Wow. This yogurt cafe is not worth the hype.
I came in here recently as I was excited in trying out a new frozen yogurt spot in town. Upon entering, I noticed the odd layout of the cafe. This place is a self serve cafe in which you create your own mix-ins, however you want. The yogurt bar was right behind the counter, making it difficult to move, as many people were trying to sample and create their mix-ins. Some of the flavours had ran out, and others had an odd taste. I felt as if the sugar was not natural, and it must have been some sort of diet sugar mixed within the yogurt. The flavours were overly sweet for my liking as well. If hello kitty had a yogurt cafe, this would be it. There were stickers, pencils, and lunch bags for sale inside. I believe this place is geared more towards children. All I know is that the yogurt and the ambiance didn't leave much of an impression on me. It isnt a place that I'll be frequenting anytime soon.

title: Review: Mercantile — 2015-09-07
summary: One of the better selections of coffee within Rice Village. (Aside from Salento's and Croissant Brioche). Starbucks does not cut it for me. Anyhow, I thoroughly enjoyed my iced vanilla latte on a hot mid afternoon day. I had dropped by Mercantile in the past to look around their shelf items, but thi
body: One of the better selections of coffee within Rice Village. (Aside from Salento's and Croissant Brioche). Starbucks does not cut it for me. Anyhow, I thoroughly enjoyed my iced vanilla latte on a hot mid afternoon day. I had dropped by Mercantile in the past to look around their shelf items, but this time around I finally grabbed a drink. The shop was about to close within 10 minutes and Graham (the Manager) was cleaning the coffee station. Although it was time for closing, he was kind enough to whip up a drink for me. I thoroughly appreciated that as I had always wanted to try the coffee here. Love how the product is local - They use Boomtown's beans and pastries from local vendors. My iced latte was smooth and creamy, just the perfect drink I needed to cool myself off. Nice shop and concept. I can see myself dropping by again in the near future.

title: Review: Milk Mustache — 2025-07-02
summary: Yummy cookies galore. I have always liked this sweet gem of a spot. When you walk into milk mustache, you smell all things butter and sweetness. The aroma wafts in the cute little shoppe. It is every so colorful, cute and whimsical in here. I love this cozy yet nonchalant cookie shoppe right on foun
body:
Yummy cookies galore.
I have always liked this sweet gem of a spot. When you walk into milk mustache, you smell all things butter and sweetness. The aroma wafts in the cute little shoppe. It is every so colorful, cute and whimsical in here. I love this cozy yet nonchalant cookie shoppe right on fountain view. Milk Mustache honestly has some of the best cookies in the city. That says a lot, cause' we've got quite a few cookie/dessert spots in the city. But I'm picky and I truly believe these are some of the best cookies I've had in Houston. They are warm, crispy and yet gooey as well. They have that classic texture and flavor that a cookie should measure up to.. and they are crag like. I love how this spot has a few new flavors throughout the year and they also have dessert beverages and soft serve as well. Service is always nice and prompt. The dessert's here are quite sweet but full of flavor, which keeps me revisiting every now and then. Try it for yourself, you'll be in for a treat. Nothing dry and nothing boring about these cute cookies. Until next time!

title: Review: Minuti Coffee — Galleria — 2018-02-07
summary: Warm and glowing aesthetics within a clean environment. I like this small and cozy Minuti coffee house. There is plenty of seating within the cafe.. even with the limited space. They have a variety of beverages to choose from and several baked goods. This location also serves up some Italian gelato.
body: Warm and glowing aesthetics within a clean environment. I like this small and cozy Minuti coffee house. There is plenty of seating within the cafe.. even with the limited space. They have a variety of beverages to choose from and several baked goods. This location also serves up some Italian gelato. I normally order a cafe latte, which is very creamy and milky at Minuti. The flavor is smooth and delicate. I like how their coffee doesn't keep me jittery and wired. Some of these posh coffee house's have strong beans and high acidity content. But at Minuti, the coffee has a medium strength. I've had their vanilla and hazelnut latte. Both are good. Curious to try their affogato next time. Baristas are kind and friendly. They prepare each drink incredibly quick and answer all questions. I recommend this particular location.. I'm glad it's no longer a Starbucks. This cubical space has a quiet and laid-back vibe.

title: Review: Minuti Coffee — Sugar Land — 2010-05-07
summary: I love the masculine - Italian feel of this coffeehouse. I feel as if, suddenly I have been transported to Italia. Ahh, viva Italia. I haven't been here in awhile. There is just something else about coming here in the winter, and holding dearly on to a mug of ciocco de leche. What is that you ask? I
body:
I love the masculine - Italian feel of this coffeehouse. I feel as if, suddenly I have been transported to Italia. Ahh, viva Italia.
I haven't been here in awhile. There is just something else about coming here in the winter, and holding dearly on to a mug of ciocco de leche. What is that you ask? It is the BEST hot chocolate I have ever tried! It is only for those you can appreciate the intensity of chocolate. It tastes more like pudding. The drink is very thick, and best eaten with a spoon. Unless... you want a chocolaty mustache.
The staff here is kind and friendly. I have came here before, and played a game of chess with friends. It is a calm and quiet atmosphere. I wouldn't come here to study though. If you want that, then go to a library. This is the place to be for a good chat with friends, and just plain ol` having a good time.
The variety of teas here are quite nice as well. I like the fact that their coffee is imported from Modena. I can taste a rich bold flavour in the beans. I like coming here when I want a change from Starbucks.
PS - Check out Minuti's fan page on facebook. The profile picture is of a snap shot I took. ;)

title: Review: Mission Burrito — 2010-07-26
summary: I finally had a chance to eat back at Mission Burrito after almost a year! I was in the mood for a burrito, it had been several months since I had dropped by here. . I`m SO glad that I opted for a burrito rather than a bowl! The fact that Mission Burrito has a variety of selection keeps this place f
body:
I finally had a chance to eat back at Mission Burrito after almost a year! I was in the mood for a burrito, it had been several months since I had dropped by here. .
I`m SO glad that I opted for a burrito rather than a bowl!
The fact that Mission Burrito has a variety of selection keeps this place first in mind when I am craving a burrito.
There are several different tortillas you can select from: flour, wheat, tomato, or spinach.
I chose the spinach tortilla with cilantro rice, shrimp, beans, vegetables, sour cream, and guacamole.
I love how their are several different salsas to pick from. I usually pick two salsas which ends up giving my burrito a spicy and zesty kick. I also had corn in my burrito which gave a mellow sweet taste mixed in with the spicy savoury-ness. It paired so well! The grilled shrimp were delicious! Fresh, plump, and perfectly seasoned. I also decided on the guacamole (extra charge) which was flavourful and savoury. My burrito was huge but quite satisfying!
They also have these mega-sized chocolate chip cookies in front of the cashier counter. I think I have my eye on them & will definitely try them next time. Cant go wrong with a huge cookie. .
Despite the calorie and carbohydrate bomb that Mission Burrito throws at you, I recommend coming by once in awhile when you are really in the mood for this place. Its a casual spot which is great when hanging out with friends.

title: Review: Mitchell's Ice Cream — 2015-05-16
summary: THE ICE-CREAM AT MITCHELL'S IS SO GOOD I FORGOT TO TAKE A PICTURE! Yep... it was that good. I came in on a random weekday night.. around 9 pm. The brick and mortar was packed with folks coming in left and right. This is probably the first ice cream shop in which I had to grab a ticket and wait for m
body:
THE ICE-CREAM AT MITCHELL'S IS SO GOOD I FORGOT TO TAKE A PICTURE!
Yep... it was that good. I came in on a random weekday night.. around 9 pm. The brick and mortar was packed with folks coming in left and right. This is probably the first ice cream shop in which I had to grab a ticket and wait for my number to be called. I felt a bit helpless in deciding on which flavors to settle upon. I was totally in the mood for a warm and decadent brownie fudge sundae. But to my dismay, they didn't have that on the menu. I also didn't want to continuously sample every flavour in the bin. So I made the brave decision and settled upon the toasted almond ice cream and the espresso toffee ice cream. I felt a bit rebellious in choosing a caffeinated flavored ice cream at night - but it was totally worth it. Being a chocoholic, I asked for hot fudge to be smothered on my ice cream. I was given two large scoops of ice cream that was swimming in hot fudge sauce. Oh my gosh, totally worth every bite! Mitchell's ice cream is super fluffy, creamy, and fresh. I ate every bite possible in my cup. So glad to have ventured down here in the Mission and try Mitchell's. The best ice cream spot in San Francisco! You'll be hooked like a sugar hooker. Give it a try!

title: Review: Mochinut Houston Heights — 2024-08-23
summary: Pretty good. Warm, crispy yet chewy at the same time. A mochi donut should have that distinct chewiness. This location serves up some good products. Everything is fresh and customer service is great. They have these new mochi balls that are a little different than their mochi donuts. Chewy, soft, ye
body:
Pretty good.
Warm, crispy yet chewy at the same time. A mochi donut should have that distinct chewiness. This location serves up some good products. Everything is fresh and customer service is great. They have these new mochi balls that are a little different than their mochi donuts. Chewy, soft, yet there's a filling inside the mochi balls. Plenty of flavors to choose from. For the mochi balls we chose matcha. Yummy with a creamy matcha filling inside the ball. For the mochi donut we chose pistachio as well as their yogurt flavor. These two flavors must be new. I've never seen them before and I often visit various locations of Mochinut. This location, as well as the Chinatown location are definitely my favorites. A few other ones serve their mochi donuts cold.
Tea beverage's are plenty on the menu. We opted for Thai tea with less sweetness and full ice. Crisp and creamy. Good flavor and paired well with the donuts.
Open air environment and plenty of windows. This area is a bit further out with where I typically venture, but will definitely be back to visit and grab more mochi donuts. I also liked how the sweets weren't too sweet. Chewy and yum. Perfect on this Friday evening.
Until next time!

title: Review: Monster Dessert Bar — 2013-02-02
summary: I recently checked out Monster Dessert Bar about two weeks ago with my friend.. This spot is brand spankin new to Sugar Land. body:
I recently checked out Monster Dessert Bar about two weeks ago with my friend..
This spot is brand spankin new to Sugar Land. Upon entering, there was even an employee posting an 'open sign' on the window.
The layout of the place is neat and clean & scattered with small tables and chairs.
My friend opted for the vanilla cupcake with butter cream frosting, and I chose the cake batter frozen yogurt. What I like about this place is that they have several different desserts, and not just frozen yogurt. I cant say much about the pastries, since I havent tried them yet, but I do believe my friend liked her cupcake. I enjoyed my cake batter frozen yogurt. The consistency was creamy and sweet, with a pleasant aroma of vanilla. The manager was friendly and told us the history about the business. Supposedly there's a few locations around the world. Other than that, this place was okay.

title: Review: Naha Thai Restaurant — 2022-07-26
summary: 111th review! :) Naha Thai is fantastic.. ! From the food, to the environment, as well as the service.. there isn't much to say except that it's warm and cozy. The owners are quite friendly and talkative; it makes all the difference in the world with a chatty diner such as myself. I enjoy relishing
body:
111th review! :)
Naha Thai is fantastic.. ! From the food, to the environment, as well as the service.. there isn't much to say except that it's warm and cozy.
The owners are quite friendly and talkative; it makes all the difference in the world with a chatty diner such as myself. I enjoy relishing in conversations, especially with older folk that are full of wisdom. The folks that run this place are talkative and quite accommodating. The food is tasty and packs in a punch of heat. I love the fact that they use fresh red chilies in most of their items, instead of just ground red pepper. The pad thai here is light, fresh and crisp. Far from the typical greasy bowl types. It was nice to eat a different variation of it.. typically Northern Thai style. Every region has its own take.. but this one was refreshing. The penang curry is great here as well. Aromatic and bubbling. The coconut milk is creamy and brimming with different veggies. I ordered the vegetarian option and found it to be delightful. Will definitely try a meat item next time and pair it with a different curry. I'm picky with curries but I can honestly say this one was the better one that I've had. Looking forward to revisiting and trying their soups, tea + so much more. The echoes of the old restaurant that used to be here are gone. This new spot is better. I'm glad Naha is in this part of town. We needed to crank up the heat in sweet old sugar land.

title: Review: Nails by Yen — 2021-12-15
summary: Great service, it has improved over the years. Many of the nail technicians are friendly and will remember you if you visit often. body: Great service, it has improved over the years. Many of the nail technicians are friendly and will remember you if you visit often. I typically opt for a water bottle while getting a manicure or pedicure. They have a decent selection of nail polish to choose from. The colors are vivid and nothing is stale. Overall a good choice for selecting a polish shoppe in the greater Sugar Land area. They are convenient and will call you if you're running late to your appointment. Prompt, courteous and no language barrier. This place has been a family favorite for years. Until next time!

title: Review: Naseeb Indian Restaurant — 2015-01-26
summary: I'm not usually into the concept of a buffet... but the buffet showcased at Naseeb Indian Restaurant is great. I came here a few months ago with my sister and mum.
