summary: Service was super awkward, cold, and dry. Just as the cutting cold winds that passed through the door on that chilly night. The drinks are just okay here. Simple yogurt based drinks. Creamy and mellow flavored. I prefer my yogurt drinks with a bit more of a sharp, tart flavor. Almost lemony (Mediter
body:
Service was super awkward, cold, and dry. Just as the cutting cold winds that passed through the door on that chilly night.
The drinks are just okay here. Simple yogurt based drinks. Creamy and mellow flavored. I prefer my yogurt drinks with a bit more of a sharp, tart flavor. Almost lemony (Mediterranean style). Their yogurt reminded me of Australian style yogurt, creamy, light, but without any zest to it. The dragon fruit flavors did not really shine through the yogurt. The fruit might not have been in season. I did enjoy the yogurt and oats drink. Although a bit more flavor in it would have been nice. It was simple and not too sweet as I had lowered the sweetness level. I was amused by the menu and was wondering if I could add fruit to my oat drink, that should definitely be an option. In regards to the menu, they did not break it down for me. Again. Awkward. These cold yogurt based drinks are great after eating a spicy meal. Acid reflux and indigestion completely float away when sipping on a cold lactic based bevvie from Yomies. I wasn't able to finish my bevvie, threw it into the fridge and tried it the next day thinking it would taste like overnight oats. But the next day, the yogurt separated a bit and did not taste good. LOL. Oopsies. Will I be back? Maybe. Service definitely needs to be improved.

title: Review: Yummy’s Hot Chicken — 2020-08-16
summary: Hot. Crispy. Chicken sandwich. But with a Syrian twist. Wow this atypical sandwich was hecka good. Lots of flavor, layers and textures. Yummy's Bite has a lot to offer in terms of flavor and ingenuity. It's a simple and plain food truck but don't be fooled by their small menu. Got there early on a S
body:
Hot. Crispy. Chicken sandwich. But with a Syrian twist.
Wow this atypical sandwich was hecka good. Lots of flavor, layers and textures. Yummy's Bite has a lot to offer in terms of flavor and ingenuity. It's a simple and plain food truck but don't be fooled by their small menu. Got there early on a Saturday evening and thankfully there wasn't a line wrapped around the truck. I tried most of their items and was left wanting more. Jk. I left feeling satisfied. If anyone knows me well enough.. I rarely eat anything fried. Including these types of chicken sandwiches that became ever so popular.
But with the unique twist that Yummy's offers.. this sandwich is in a league of it's own. Super crispy, fresh and loaded with the good stuff. The slaw is bright and vibrant and the crumb coating of the chicken is crisp and golden. They have a few spice levels for their Syrian chicken sandwich as well as their tender basket. I asked for medium spice and it was just right. Ordered the curry fries as well.. quite unique and interesting take on fusion fries. The curry sauce was exquisite meshed with the mild flavors of the cheese sauce. Fries were very hot (temperature wise). My sandwich came with a challah bun rather than the pretzel bun advertised. I'm glad I asked in advance as I prefer the challah bread. You may have to ask when ordering your sandwich. All in all, everything was crisp and yummy. This spot packs heat and taste. I'll probably revisit in the Fall. It's quite hot out and eating in these temps was an adventure of its own. Thanks Yummy's. Hope y'all continue to thrive on the simple yet humble grounds of the Galleria food truck park.

title: Review: Zeyad Bakery & Sweets — 2018-02-20
summary: A shabby and rundown strip on Richmond Ave.. Zeyad Bakery & Sweets offers up some savory and sweet Palestinian baked goods. The outside of the bakery gives off an unkempt and uninviting feel. I still made my way here as the cravings for baklava were unreal. When I stepped inside, no one asked if I n
body:
A shabby and rundown strip on Richmond Ave.. Zeyad Bakery & Sweets offers up some savory and sweet Palestinian baked goods.
The outside of the bakery gives off an unkempt and uninviting feel. I still made my way here as the cravings for baklava were unreal. When I stepped inside, no one asked if I needed any help. Two of the guys working in the back were speaking loudly in Arabic. They kinda just stared at me in awkward silence. I made my way through the dusty shelves and checked out the grocery items. They have quite a few products here, ranging from fresh baked bread, candies, coffee/tea, spices, etc. They also have a refrigerator full of cheese and yogurt. I decided not to pick up any grocery items and made myself towards the baked goods. I picked up a large Spinach pie (Fatayer bi Sabanekh) and three pieces of the baklava filled with cream. The bakery didn't have a large selection of desserts at the time I came in. The bright orange kanafeh seemed enticing but I'll try that for another visit. I'd say this bakery is a good place to order a large quantity of desserts for a party. I'd like to try the Levantine pizza on my next trip. It's called Sfina and its layered with ground beef and tomatoes. They have one with ground thyme (zaatar) and cheese as well (manakeesh). Cedar Bakery is right near this plaza.. so the competition is stiff up on the bakers.
Zeyad Bakery has a small dining area if you decide to order and eat within the premises. I'd probably eat the warm pizza and fried snacks such as kibbeh in house. I'm not too sure if I'll be back anytime soon. Im curious to try Cedar Bakery next door. The unkempt bakery and silent service was awkward. But I recommend picking up dessert from here if you're curious to try something new.

title: Review: Zoa Moroccan Kitchen — 2024-02-12
summary: This was the third Zoa Moroccan Kitchen location that I have visited within Houston. They have locations all around the city and are rather convenient for visiting over lunch or dinner. So far with this location? Unimpressed and left much to be desired. This location is super skimpy with their porti
body:
This was the third Zoa Moroccan Kitchen location that I have visited within Houston. They have locations all around the city and are rather convenient for visiting over lunch or dinner.
So far with this location? Unimpressed and left much to be desired. This location is super skimpy with their portions and the price point is heavy. For two bowls, 1 bread and 1 green tea, you'll shell out about $30 and leave feeling a bit underwhelmed. Not sure why they are so skimpy with their portions and their service. Food was good, warm and flavorful, but I've had better at their other locations. This location is quite small and grab and go style as well. Parking is a bit small and limited and as mentioned, this location is smaller than the other ones that I have visited. With the food: The meats were tender and their toppings were decent. Unfortunately, I may never revisit ever again due to their lack of decent portions of their bowls and the overall presentation of their meals. I'm already hungry after writing this review and I was just visiting with their location not that long ago - LOL. Their super sweet Moroccan green tea is great, but honestly, I can make that at home (Atay Bi Nana). We don't have that many Moroccan food choices in Houston, I wish Zoa could do a bit better. Probably wont revisit this location ever again as mentioned. Until next time!

title: Review: Asiatown Crawl at Westcroft Center — 2022-06-03
summary: What a cosy gathering full of my favorite people! Those are the best UYEs, the ones where you can laugh, talk and relish with good company. No frou frou or weird vibes whatsoever. Just chill laid-back moments. Mike ended up surprising me and that made my day. Lou, as usual, was a great host. I co-ho
body: What a cosy gathering full of my favorite people! Those are the best UYEs, the ones where you can laugh, talk and relish with good company. No frou frou or weird vibes whatsoever. Just chill laid-back moments. Mike ended up surprising me and that made my day. Lou, as usual, was a great host. I co-hosted a bit of the event and loved sharing the cultural background of the food as well as the local ice cream shop, bakery, and market we visited. It is my absolute pleasure to bring rich cultural heritage and perspective thrown into the mix. We had such a great time noshing on some sweet ice cream and milkshakes. The folks at the bakery were just as warm and friendly - introducing everyone to exotic saffron tea and knafeh, which is a desert made from nablus cheese and shredded filo pastry. Nablus is a city in Palestine, and that is where the lovely dessert originates from. I shared my knafeh with everyone and some folks grabbed butter cookies (ghraybeh) & baklava as well. The bakery folks own the market next door and we equally enjoyed our time over there. Some friends bought saffron and others bought tea biscuits. All in all, we had a great time conversing and catching up like old times. Nostalgia at it's finest mixed in with a bit of new moments. I look forward to the next event! Might be mine next time around. Cheers and syoy!
author: Sara Loren

body: Well. What can I say? All my favorite platinum (black) folk already wrote essays upon essays about our grandeur Thai inspired evening in City Centre. It was a cosy summer night as we noshed upon food that was as big & bold with flavor, as our conversations were. First of all; I adore Jando; his bold and spunky persona is exactly what Houston was missing all this time. Like a gust of fresh East Coast air just chillin and vibin' with us. Thank you for making me laugh and spilling all the deepest and darkest depths of right on our table. Nothing about this was surface level shit, the hammer and axe broke through the table (¡gracias a Dios!). I was highly amused; as much as I was with the food that kept magically appearing in front of us. I kept thinking we would eat typical Thai cuisine that night. But that was far from our reality.. we were gifted with artisanal small plated meals that were decadent yet rich in taste. My favorites were the short ribs and crispy chicken. Thai tea was quite sweet yet refreshing in between savory meals. Their fresh coconut water was great as well. A bit of coconut meat and lightly iced, it was perfect in this summer season. Chef Jett was enthusiastic, energetic and fun to speak with. His name is quite huge in this city and it was lovely to finally meet with him. His wife and the rest of the culinary team were friendly and informative as well. Thanks to the Thai cultural ministry in their initiative to feed a bunch of platinum folk and tickle our taste-buds & minds. Now I have a strong longing and impulse to visit Thailand and nosh on penang curry that's sprinkled with just the right amount of kaffir lime leaves (a fav of mine). Aside from my wanderlust daydream, I had a great evening catching up with old-school folk. With summer finally ending (I think) it was a great initiative catching up and learning about prospective events & growth of the community. Much has changed in the past decade... The nostalgia of days gone by.. but this I know for sure.. so much growth and change will usher in more fun & unique events to come.. cheers and syoy! PS - thanks for the lippy balm/mints + other cute wee little gifts. The remembrance of a fun night will linger longer than the taste of those mints. *Besos*

title: Review: FACE FOUNDRIE Houston — Oct 3, 2023
summary: My goodness, I loved everything about this... it was different and unique. A cosy sort of experience that was wrapped around nurturing and pampering. I have always loved perks that were centered around food. But this one? Yeah, it hit differently. & it was exactly what was needed on a Friday, a perf
body: My goodness, I loved everything about this... it was different and unique. A cosy sort of experience that was wrapped around nurturing and pampering. I have always loved perks that were centered around food. But this one? Yeah, it hit differently. & it was exactly what was needed on a Friday, a perfect way to end the week by getting a facial close to evening time. Right from the start, upon walking in, I knew that I would love this spot. It was bright, airy and quite roomy. I love how this spot uses as much natural light as possible, instead of keeping it dim. The aroma was fresh and inviting and the service was just as warm. They have snacks and tea to choose from before getting your facial. My facialist was busy arranging everything in the beginning so I made myself a nice snack and tea to munch on. I was not running hastily on time and wanted the pleasure of soaking in this experience. Once the facial got started, I knew that I was in for a real treat. Every single thing about this facial treatment was mind-blowingly amazing. I had received a facial one month prior to this experience at another spot. It was good. But this one? It took the cake. From the beginning of service, til the end, my facialist, Drea was knowledgeable and geared for great service. The aromatherapy used was one to delight the senses and tickle the soul. I loved the facial cupping that was used as well. & the aromatic cocoa butter which I opted for. I was often asked if everything was okay and if I was comfortable. It was nice for Drea to check in on me from time to time. Facilities here are clean, including their restrooms. I loved how my facialist took her time to give me the best pampering service. Nothing was rushed here. Throughout the session I would get a scalp/head massage and was also given a weighted blanket that made me feel oh so cosy and snug. I was wrapped up like a burrito with nowhere to move. Perfect. Will I be back here? Most definitely. Service was great from all those that were working here that day. As mentioned, my experience here was perfect and one that I am grateful for. They also have gift cards here if you want to get one for family or friends. You can also sign up and become a member for recurrent facials. Thanks Houston & team and Jando. Y'all truly kicked this one out of the park. This was one for the books. So nourishing, deep down in all aspects. SYOY!

body: What a fun, relaxing and refreshing event on a cosy and blissful Sunday afternoon. Literally everything was perfect about this gathering. All that rain? It totally added towards the lush background and serene surrounding. It was nice to revisit this spot after all these years. But mix it in with friends? Totally an entertaining experience, mixed with knowledge and learning. Thanks for such a zen-like moment and making this event happen, Lou. It was good to connect over fresh tea, warm nutritious eats, and touring the temple together. I loved looking over the books as well as their mini museum area. We heard live music softly playing in the background as the temple came to a quiet close for the day. We all agreed that we felt like we were elsewhere. Far away in another country or something. A home away from home experience. The smell of incense wafting and burning in the background gave the gathering a grounded touch. We all felt recentered within before going our own ways. What a great way to blissfully bring in a new week ahead. Cheers to all and see you on.

body: It was great to visit this spot for Community Week! I didn't even know community week was a thing and thought this was an sorta deal. Nope! More boba tea for all! R&B has some tasty beverage choices and it was not my first time visiting this spot within the land of Sugar. Quality of beverages and customer service is spot on. Brandon and Julia were friendly and answered any of the questions I had in mind. I ordered a fresh milk beverage (strawberry matcha tea with tapioca). Asked for half sweet, but Brandon mentioned the matcha is quite strong and bitter. Bumped it to 70% sweetness and it was perfect! R&B tapioca is always chewy with the right texture and flavor. All in all, the matcha blended well with the bright flavors of strawberry. Will definitely reorder this next time! Their milk teas in general are great. Plenty of options for flavors, mixins and toppings. Thanks Houston for presenting this sweet opportunity for the month of. This was a great spot to visit on a warm Monday afternoon. Getting the week started with a tasty caffeinated fix! Until next time! SYOY. :)

body: What a wonderful event. Thank you Luis M Chen for organizing and putting this event together. All on your own, as usual, you made it happen and everything went seamlessly and integrated the event with the theme. All things Korean food and stopping at HMART as the last part of the adventure tour! I remember when Luis mentioned Shabu style food, I was already intrigued from the get- go. Because of it having a Korean flair I knew that I would enjoy the food, simply because of the sauces, spice and many different condiments (banchan) veggies and herbs. That is what I got here as I inhaled my vegetarian style shabu and my friends equally enjoyed their meal as well. They have seafood and meat options as well and everyone dug in and went back for more for this AYCE style concept. Service was attentive and everything was well taken care of; Luis often checked on us as well which was appreciated. What a great host! I got to learn a few techniques in regards to Shabu and hot soup dining. I like this style as it's not a communal pot that you all dig out of. You can adjust the temperature of your soup as well or just turn it off, all with a remote on the side of the table. A few of us ventured off to Hmart afterwards in search of more unique goodies. We purchased rambutan, fresh nectarine and a few shelf items. It was fun exploring the grocery store with Luis and Chris, always good company and even more fun on a very crowded Sunday. Thank you for giving us all goodie bags at your foodie adventure gathering. It was great catching up with a few old school yelpers while munching on hot soup. Good seeing Victoria, Tabatha and Genea as well. Thank y'all for your humor, silliness and good company. Cheers and SYOY until next time!

Absolutely enjoyed the refreshing shaved ice that we all ordered. A great way to end the night with a crisp plate of fruit and snowy ice. Good times with the Yelpies and fun moment's. body: Such creamy, dreamy and ultra decadent chocolates at ROYCE chocolatiers! This spot is awesome and has such an international vibe because of the ingredients they showcase within their chocolates. Pistachios and so many other variations within their chocolate! I love it and purchased the pistachio variation (more of that on their main business page). Royce originates from northern Japan... From an area known for its dairy products. I have always loved products originating from Hokkaido, such as their milk breads and cheese tarts + many other items. These chocolates are of no other exception... So milky and creamy with every bite you take.. especially their famous 'nama' chocolates which were provided as samples for this particular perk. My favorite being their matcha 'nama' chocolate sample. Soo good. Love anything with matcha! You could taste the quality of the fine tea leaves meshed with the creaminess of the cacao beans. Service was good, prompt and attentive. Just stayed for a bit as I was headed to an appointment somewhere else. Everything was appreciated though in regards to chocolate samples and answering all of my questions. Thank you Jando and Houston for this great little perk for the month of May. Cheers and SYOY.

body: Juicy brewin' tea drinks and crunchy lil' nuggets? My type of hour right here! Exclusive convos with the homie Jando? Yes please! I love office hours and this one was a real treat. The first had nata jelly (made with coconut pulp and pineapple flavoring) & the second drink consisted of tapioca pearls. Both were chewy and tantalizing, but I must say, the pineapple with jasmine tea and nata jelly were totally delightful. The floral notes of jasmine were quite aromatic and sensual. Perfumy without being overwhelming. Probably the best I've had. Thanks for the complimentary tea(s) Jando! As well as the loot, cute little trinkets scattered round' the table. The pizza cutter will come in clutch as well as the travel accessory bag. Always appreciated. It was a tasty Tuesday tea day. Spent with good chatter, caffeine and fruity chews. We also had the youngest yelper join in on all the fun. The bebe was all giggles and smiles. What a delight. Until next time!

body: Mmm mmm milk + sugar! I think most of us are familiar with this adorable ice cream shoppe? I know that I am. summary: Loved this little sweet perk! This ice cream spot is bright and cheery, perfect on this sunny Saturday visit. body: Loved this little sweet perk! This ice cream spot is bright and cheery, perfect on this sunny Saturday visit. I've been to V.L. before, and the establishment was just as nice and clean, well organized like last time. The lines were non existent, so Lou and I grabbed our ice cream and got to comfortably sit indoors inside the shoppe. The scooper was friendly and allowed us to try a few samples. Spoon samples were metal spoons that we got to throw into the used spoon section. Interesting. I love coffee so I just went for the coffee affogato flavor, as well as the dark chocolate brownie flavor. Out of the two, the affogato was creamier and a lot more lush. It was easier to eat and had a nice and light coffee flavor. The brownie ice cream was a bit on the drier side, but still had good, deep chocolatey flavor. I mixed the two a bit to get a better viscosity. Spoons are cute and well rounded, made of plastic. We also tried the Texas rodeo sundae and root beer soda, which Lou paid for. Flavors were great, sundae was dreamy and creamy. Crunchy with the praline pretzels and fluffy whipped cream. Overall we had a great time. It's sweet to be. This perk is taking place throughout the week and ends on the 19th of June. Thanks for a cozy opportunity to revisit the Montrose Collective plaza. Until next time!
author: Sara Loren

summary: What a wonderful foodtastic event! Thank you Houston and Jando for putting this together during the mid of April. Clear and sunny skies called for a milkshake paired with burgers and fries. body: What a wonderful foodtastic event! Thank you Houston and Jando for putting this together during the mid of April. Clear and sunny skies called for a milkshake paired with burgers and fries. Smashburger has been around for some time... scattered throughout Houston, but I had barely visited in the past. Simply because I don't eat burgers that often. But are they tasty? Most definitely. Whether stacked, smashed or simply a classic patty no cheese, you can't go wrong. I ordered the grilled chicken sandwich. Paired it with tator tots and a strawberry milkshake. No frills, just simple. Asked for avocado with my sandwich as well. Meal came out piping hot and fresh. The grilled chicken breast was on the smaller side, but still good. Buns were toasted and the tomato slices were fresh in the sandwich. The only thing that was missing was the avocado - they forgot to put it in the meal so I had to go and grab it. Avocado was a let down because it tasted dull and prepackaged, just as similar as the ones from Sam's club. Other than that, my meal was good. Fresh rosemary tossed into crispy and warm tator tots? Goood stuff! As well as the sweet and creamy strawberry milkshake paired with the meal. Very nostalgic of childhood. Met with other Yelpers as we chowed down on good grub. Twas warm and friendly company on that bright day. Will I revisit this particular smashburger location? Most definitely. It's central within most spots in the inner loop. Thank you Houston for a scrumptious food week. It is so appreciated. Until next time!
author: Sara Loren

body: This was a cosy n' cute sweet to be! I'm so glad I made it back from out of town to snag a cupcake, cake pop and hot coffee?! Sweeeet! Literally. This location of CRAVE has been around forever and yet it was my first time steppin' in! Thanks for the opportunity! I've been to their other location before, which has also been around for some time. Remember the absolute obsession trend of cupcake shoppes opening up in the 2010's?? Yeah some of us are that old. One of the reasons why I don't visit CRAVE that often is because their cupcakes are too sweet for me. I do appreciate their variety, as well as how they serve coffee all day? Didn't know that until this recent visit. They're basically a coffee cupcakery shoppe that serves up pretty much any kind of caffeine. I had their toasted cinnamon coffee with a coconut cream cupcake and cake pop. I'm not sure what flavor the cake pop was? But it was okay. Too sweet, just like their cupcakes. What I do appreciate, is how their baked goods are so tender. Another spot not far from here makes their cupcakes too dry, like a brick, IYKYK, Y'all can spot that review from another time. Back to CRAVE: Each bite was tender n' soft, aromatic (thanks coconut!) n' creamy. Coffee was hot, fresh, and paired well with the sweet treat. It was 6ish pm and that did not stop me from having a cup of coffee with whole milk. Service was great, can't complain and the folks in the back were all smiles. They happily waved goodbye as we left, no crumb left behind, and bebe was with me as well. Warm vibrations and the wafting aroma of va va vanilla and butter. You're in for a real treat. They also have frosted cookies here and other sweet stuff. I'll try to revisit again in the near future, especially with knowing they have various types of coffee. Thanks Hou for giving us all this sweet opportunity to nosh on cupcakes. It's my birthday month and this was totally appropriate as well. Lol. Cheers n' toasting to decadent cupcakes this summer. Until next time!
author: Sara Loren

body: We had a weekend mini getaway to Hawaii over the past weekend. All thanks to our Yelpie friend Ann L. for hosting a colorful and interactive. It was a warm and sunny Saturday afternoon. The restaurant was tucked all the way out in Katy.. an area I almost never frequent. Despite that.. all of us close Yelpies showed up. Im glad we did as we all had a fun time. Many pictures were taken, but the cool part was when we received our own pictures from Ann's Fujifilm. That instant picture is a memory that I will always cherish. Everyone of us enjoyed the Hawaiian and Vietnamese cuisine offered at the restaurant. The owners of the restaurant were kind and often checked up on us. Towards the end of our meal, we were presented with some yummy pecan pie. The came to a complete end after having dessert and coffee at Cocohodo. It was nice to try different places in a far away town. It was also a lovely way to spend a warm Saturday afternoon. Mahalo to our Yelpie Ann and all who showed up. I look forward to more 's coming up. Until next time! :)

Enjoyed the hot coffee which was locally sourced through Katz. Always a good choice. It was a lovely opportunity to get together on a Saturday afternoon. Thanks to Belly, Carlos, Jason and the gang for some good laughter. We stayed for a few hours and were treated with warm service. Thanks to all for showing up at my first Brunch Series. We are officially a part of The Breakfast Club. Lol. More to come in the future. Stay tuned.
